thesis:
Sage (product name MoPilot) is the host for multiple coding harnesses: the UI keeps the look of ChatGPT/Codex, each harness declares its own capabilities, and Sage only polyfills what a harness lacks and what must be consistent across all harnesses.
1. Eight independent axes: Harness, Provider, Account, Model and session config, Target, Chat and segments, Sage platform services, Sage shared capabilities. HarnessKind = 'codex' | 'claude' | 'acp:<id>'. There are exactly two first-class harnesses: Codex (app-server JSON-RPC) and Claude Code (Agent SDK), each with a dedicated adapter, and both instances live in Electron main. dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI and Goose are all basic tier: they go through the same generic ACP adapter plus one quirks file per harness (opencode uses 'opencode acp'), appear in the picker only after passing runtime admission, and carry a Basic badge. The recommended DeepSeek path is Claude Code plus the DeepSeek Provider; dsh exists separately as a basic-tier harness. The MoPilot gateway is a Provider under Codex and Claude Code; for basic-tier harnesses, the Provider and credentials are managed by the harness itself, and Sage injects no key.
2. Capabilities are negotiated. Each adapter declares in three layers: static info, connect-time negotiation, and dynamic session state (held by main, with a rev; a window takes a snapshot first, then applies patches). 34 semantics (goal, plan, review, multiAgent, compact, init, skills, plugins, and so on) each get one binding: rpc, passthrough, config, polyfill, route, or none with a Why. The effective capability is the intersection of six layers: harness, provider, model, account, feature flag, and session. Components read only this result, and no harness name appears in them. CLI versions only set a minimum version and known-bad versions; each capability that depends on undocumented behavior gets a runtime probe, and a failed probe turns off only that one item.
3. One presentation rule, based only on Why.layer: native; Sage polyfill (small label “by MoPilot”); route to another harness (state the target harness, the account, and “this is a new chat”, with a confirmation dialog the first time it crosses vendors); grey out with the reason and a fix action; hide. Never silently degrade into a plain message. The app UI is in English, and the English copy is authoritative.
4. Native first, pass through by default. A harness's own commands and workflows are handed to the harness verbatim, and state follows what the harness reports. Sage intercepts only three kinds: pure UI commands, commands that only have an interactive implementation (a static list determined per CLI version, plus init.terminal_slash_commands), and commands that would break the session. Claude's / commands must go in the last content block. If a basic-tier harness has never pushed a command catalog, any typed /xxx is passed through verbatim.
5. Polyfills serve only the first-class harnesses, under three criteria: state ownership is stated; the difference can be explained in one sentence; any extra model spend is user-initiated with a visible budget. The polyfill engines are reduced to init (Codex has no /init), shell (Claude has no '!'), and archive/search (Sage metadata). Claude's /goal has no pause, so Sage holds a pause that meets the criteria: Stop or Pause = interrupt() then send '/goal clear', the condition is stored in Sage, and Resume re-sends '/goal <condition>'; the GoalBar is labeled “by MoPilot” and states that the turn count restarts. The goalLoop, goal_report, planGuard and review polyfills are all deleted; basic-tier harnesses get no polyfill that does a harness's job for it.
6. Platform services and shared capabilities belong to Sage. fs, terminal, search, projects, scheduled tasks, worktrees and notifications are implemented in Electron main and do not go through Codex. Computer use and browser control are core capabilities and must work on every harness, including the basic tier. There are three injection channels: Claude gets one in-process SDK MCP server per session (alwaysLoad), Codex uses mcp_servers in the thread config (thread/start and thread/resume), and basic-tier harnesses use mcpServers in session/new; a basic-tier harness whose injection does not succeed is not admitted. The injected server name carries a per-session random suffix, sage-mcp is a signed native helper, and the Electron fuses turn off RunAsNode. Authorization is enforced only inside Sage's tool handlers; the agent can never control MoPilot itself or system security UI; an unattended turn can only use apps that have already been authorized; the user moving the mouse takes over immediately; when there is no vision model at all, it works from an AX plus local OCR element table.
7. Accounts fail over automatically only within the same Provider and the same billing method, and switching from a subscription to pay-as-you-go always asks first. Changing Provider is a single user-confirmed switch: it opens a new segment with a handoff, does not resume the original session, and states where the data goes. Subscriptions, API keys and MoPilot credits are all account rows under some Provider, managed in one place only (Accounts & billing), and can be chosen per chat; a switch only affects the next session start, does not interrupt a running turn, and does not rewrite the CLI's own credential files. After an account or segment change, the adapter re-applies the goal and plan mode to the new session and inserts a note into the chat.
8. Parity is required only between the two first-class harnesses: the P0 journeys (including five new ones: leave after setting a goal, plan first then execute, control a Mac app, use my Chrome, and scheduled tasks while nobody is around), plus goal, plan, multi-agent, review, init, compact, skills, computer use and browser, must all be completable on both Codex and Claude Code. Basic-tier harnesses only commit to basicTierContract: the core session journeys, passthrough of native commands and modes, and computer use plus browser. Whole features that are unique to one harness, such as voice chat, Codex Cloud and output style, are allowed to differ, but their ownership must be labeled.
Delivery: one target design and eleven work packages (WP0–WP10), ordered only by dependency, all part of the final architecture and shipped in the same release; before public release there are two internal dogfood rings (Ring 0 internal, Ring 1 trusted users). There is no “stop the bleeding first, refactor later” and no transitional code to delete later; the work packages merge into one long-lived release branch in dependency order, and half-finished work is never merged to trunk. The conformance checks for Claude Code 2.1.295 (Agent SDK 0.3.295) and codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 have been measured, and the results are written directly into this version; items not yet measured (admission of the 8 basic-tier harnesses, per-thread shutdown of node_repl and codex_apps, whether Claude's Stop hook survives restartResume, re-testing on the Codex stable release, process-kill scenarios) are written as conformance checks that choose between branches already written out. #16 has already completed the rename (MoPilot, ai.mopilot.code), Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, notarization and Squirrel auto-update; the computer use helper and sage-mcp join that signing chain directly. Line numbers are as of 7a5bf12. The last work package runs the full acceptance suite in a real Electron release build and checks the 84 issues one by one.

axes.name: Harness (runtime)
axes.definition: The program that runs the agent loop. It owns tools, permissions, session storage, hooks, skills and native commands, determines which actions are possible, and also determines whether a feature is “native” or “not native”.
axes.today: HarnessId = 'codex' | 'claude' is a closed union, and HARNESS_IDS is fixed at two entries (src/harness/types.ts:2-3). Thread ownership is decided by the 'claude:' prefix, and anything unrecognized is treated as Codex. There are 99 lines in src comparing === 'claude' | 'codex', spread across 13 files; src/components has 6 harnessOfThread calls, and 11 component files import rpc directly; gates.txt records 128 gating points and 18 missed gates. Codex has no adapter: its RPC is written directly in store.ts and in components, and it lives in the renderer. The Claude adapter code is about 2,350 lines (claude.ts 781, claudeTranslate.ts 491, harness/claude/index.cjs 841, harness/claude/accounts.cjs 243). No ACP harness has any code. When launched from the Dock, PATH only gets /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin added (main.cjs:89-90), so CLIs installed under ~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, nvm, or ~/.bun/bin are not detected.
axes.proposed: An open registry HarnessKind = 'codex' | 'claude' | 'acp:<id>'. Two first-class harnesses: codex over app-server JSON-RPC, claude over the Agent SDK, with both adapter instances in main. Basic-tier harnesses all go through the generic ACP adapter, with one quirks file per harness: dsh (dsh --profile acp --patch sage.patch.yml), opencode (opencode acp), Kimi (kimi acp), Qwen (qwen --acp), Copilot (copilot --acp), Cursor (agent acp), Gemini (gemini --acp), Goose (goose acp). Detection and launch both use an env snapshot from the login shell ('$SHELL -ilc env -0'), and Settings allows specifying a bin path manually. Only basic-tier harnesses that pass admission (initialize succeeds, sage-mcp handshake, image return, and the privacy check declared in quirks) appear in the picker, with a Basic badge; those that fail are shown in Settings → Other harnesses as “Installed · not supported in this version” with the reason. Thread ownership is read from the kind recorded on the segment instead of being guessed from the id string.
axes.examples: First level of the picker: Codex, Claude Code, plus dsh (Basic), opencode (Basic) and Kimi Code (Basic) if installed and admitted. A chat that starts on Claude Code and switches to Codex has two segments, each recording its own kind and instance; switching from Claude to Kimi Code only offers “new chat with summary”.

axes.name: Provider (model endpoint)
axes.definition: Where the model comes from: the wire protocol (Anthropic messages, OpenAI Responses, Chat Completions), base URL, model catalog, each model's capabilities (whether it can see images, effort levels, speed tier), the compaction window, and which features this endpoint turns off. Provider is orthogonal to harness, but only first-class harnesses have their Provider injected by Sage.
axes.today: There is no such entity in the code. Claude's endpoint is hidden in the Billing key, and cleanEnv() applies to all Claude accounts at once; #16 added a third branch, where MoPilot mode injects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://code.mopilot.ai and the device mpk_ key (harness/claude/index.cjs:152-170), also globally. The CLI reports the gateway token as authMethod=oauth_token, apiProvider=firstParty (measured locally on 2.1.295), so subscription probing and the Fast gate cannot recognize the gateway. Codex's baseUrl only takes effect when the relay passes traffic straight through (relay.cjs:163, apiBase() at accounts.cjs:772-775; the relay does not start under the condition at accounts.cjs:213-221), and MoPilot is a hidden apiKey account in accounts plus relay passthrough. ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_CODE_* in the user's shell are removed at startup by scrubProcessEnv() (main.cjs:17, list at harness/claude/index.cjs:31).
axes.proposed: ProviderProfile {id, wires, baseUrl, firstParty, models, drops, effortLevels, compactWindow, visionFallbackModel}, where each model in the catalog declares its input modalities, effort levels, and whether it has ultra and a speed tier. Presets: anthropic, openai (first-party), deepseek, mopilot, custom (an Anthropic, Responses or Chat Completions compatible endpoint), shell (Claude config from the user's login shell). Injection covers only the first-class harnesses: Claude gets the full env plus a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; Codex uses thread/start.modelProvider plus model_providers.<id> in the thread config (accepted by codex-cli 0.162 as measured, both nested and dotted keys work), with credentials passed only through auth.command. auth.command runs immediately at thread/start, not lazily when first used, so Sage's key helper must be fast (read the cached key from the keychain, return within 200ms) and show no interaction. For basic-tier harnesses, the Provider and credentials are managed by the harness itself (the user configures them in the harness or in Sage's embedded terminal). The catalog shows real model ids, and image ability is marked per model. The drops for mopilot are delivered by WP0's gateway capability table.
axes.examples: “Claude Code · DeepSeek · deepseek-flash”, “Codex · MoPilot · gpt-6.1-sol”, “Claude Code · MoPilot · claude-sonnet-5”. Under MoPilot the ⚡ reads “Fast isn't available on MoPilot yet · Use your Claude subscription” (the second half only when a subscription exists).

axes.name: Account (account instance)
axes.definition: Whose credentials are used and who pays. Credentials can be the CLI's own subscription login, a login managed by the harness itself, or an API key or MoPilot device key held by Sage. This axis also includes the config directory, the usage source, and how to switch accounts when a quota runs out. One (harness, provider, credential) combination is an instance.
axes.today: After PR #14 both sides have multiple accounts, but the mechanisms are asymmetric: Codex is accounts.json plus a relay that swaps accounts and replays within the same request; Claude gets one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account, .claude.json is a one-way copy (harness/claude/accounts.cjs:122-128), and key-only account records are filtered out on load. #16 pushed mopilot into Codex's state.accounts, so every accounts.length check counts it as a second account (#70); with no Codex login it is selected by default (#71); apply() logs in with account/login/start(apiKey), which may write the mpk_ key into ~/.codex/auth.json (#72). On the Claude side, MoPilot is a harness-level mode, and any change in signedIn calls closeAll() (main.cjs:982, #74).
axes.proposed: Instance {id, harness, provider, kind: cliLogin | harnessAuth | sageKey, billing: subscription | apiKey | credits, configDir, usage}. AccountDriver is fully implemented only for Codex and Claude (failover, perChat, usage). Automatic account switching happens only when both conditions hold: the same ProviderProfile, and the same billing method (subscription to subscription, key to a key of the same Provider); switching from a subscription to pay-as-you-go always shows a confirmation, even within the same Provider. The UI keeps only two concepts: Default for new chats and This chat, and drops “In use”. A basic-tier harness has just one “Managed by the harness” account row: it shows the ACP authMethods, those that need a terminal login go through the platform pty; failover=none, perChat=false, and usage comes from usage_update or is none. Keys are stored in the keychain and injected per Provider, never written into any CLI's own credential files. A switch only affects the next session start or the next turn and does not call closeAll.
axes.examples: Settings → Accounts & billing is grouped by Provider: Anthropic (Max subscription a@b.com, API key ·· 9c1e), OpenAI (ChatGPT a@b.com), MoPilot (credits, balance $12.40), DeepSeek (key ·· 4f2a), and each row states which harnesses it can be used for. The Anthropic row reads “When the quota runs out: switch automatically to another subscription / ask me before using an API key”. Within the same Claude Code, one chat uses a subscription and another uses MoPilot credits.

axes.name: Model and session config
axes.definition: The values you can adjust in a session: model, effort, speed tier, multi-agent switch, permission tier, plan, output style, and their scope: whether a change affects only this chat or becomes the default for new chats.
axes.today: A fixed Selection{model, effort, fast}. Codex's model, effort and fast are global prefs (select.ts:62-76, #29), fast is hard-coded to true (select.ts:45, #57), and 'ultra' is filtered out (select.ts:43, #15). turn/start.effort applies to this turn and all later turns. Claude's model and effort are stored per chat, while fast is written into the global claudeSelection; changing effort sends only {effortLevel, fastMode}, which on 2.1.295 silently turns ultracode off (measured). Permission is the global prefs.permission, and the same tier means different things on the two sides (#27). planMode is a useState in the Composer (Composer.tsx:156, #3).
axes.proposed: The adapter delivers ConfigOption[] (same shape as ACP configOptions) and a list of native permission tiers with anchors, replaced wholesale on receipt. All values are stored per chat, and each instance also keeps one set of new-chat defaults. Scope rules: choosing on the new-chat page changes that instance's new-chat default; choosing inside an existing chat changes only this chat, with a footnote offering “Make default for new chats”; the provider level is hidden when there is only one Provider; the first time after the upgrade that a model is changed in a Codex chat, show once “Model changes now apply to this chat only.”. The top-level model in config.toml is used only as the initial value for the Codex instance default. Default permissions in Settings is the default anchor for new chats on all harnesses, and the toggle in the Composer changes only this chat (the menu bottom reads “This chat only”). plan is an independent state in SessionState, following what the harness reports. The multi-agent switch appears only when the harness has a session-level switch, using the native name (Codex's Ultra appears only when the model declares ultra; Claude's ultracode follows getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable). Basic tier: configOptions pushed by the harness are rendered as-is into generic controls, taking effect on the next turn per ACP rules; modes are listed under their native names, quirks may optionally give each mode an anchor, and unmarked ones are treated as ask (this only affects the computer use authorization table).
axes.examples: Changing a Codex chat to high does not affect other Codex chats; the bottom of the picker reads “This chat only · Make default for new chats”. Choosing opus for Claude on the new-chat page makes every later new Claude chat use opus. The model and thinking controls in a Kimi Code chat come from the configOptions pushed by Kimi.

axes.name: Execution location (Target)
axes.definition: Where the agent runs: a local directory, a worktree created by Sage, or a cloud environment.
axes.today: The worktree is created before branching by harness, but the default branch prefix is 'codex/' (types.ts:215) and the root comes from the codexHome returned by Codex initialize (main.cjs:814, #63); setup and cleanup scripts have no execution path; Work in: Cloud is rendered only when prefs.harness==='codex'; cloud tasks use the default account in $CODEX_HOME/auth.json.
axes.proposed: Target becomes its own axis. Local and worktree are provided to all harnesses by Sage platform services: default prefix mopilot/, root ~/.mopilot/worktrees, and ~/Documents/MoPilot for chats with no project directory (existing settings are not migrated); the setup script runs before adapter.start, and cleanup runs on archive or delete. Cloud is the ext cloudTasks of the (Codex, ChatGPT account) combination and is not polyfilled; choosing Cloud in a new chat only makes that new chat use Codex, the chip states the account and where the data goes, and credentials follow the account chosen for the chat.
axes.examples: A user whose default harness is Claude Code picks worktree under Work in, the branch is named mopilot/fix-login, and the Claude session starts only after the setup script finishes.

axes.name: Chat and segments
axes.definition: A Sage chat consists of several native sessions called segments, each belonging to one instance. The title, archive, pin, unread state, project, account-switch notes, switch notes, the goal pause held by Sage, and the transcript of harnesses without native history replay are all held by Sage.
axes.today: The chat id equals the native id of the first segment, and Claude chats carry the 'claude:' prefix. A new window parses the hash with /thread=([\w-]+)/, which cuts off at the colon (store.ts:591, #24). Copy resume command copies 'codex resume claude:<id>' (TitleBar.tsx:202, #69); export labels Claude as Codex (transcript.ts:16, #61). The approval-card label, message editing, and thumbs-up decide the harness by chat id (#40). Archive, pin and claudeArchived live in ui-state.json, which every window rewrites in full every 250ms (store.ts:228-252, #39). threads/<id>.json is written only for multi-segment chats, written directly with writeFileSync, and errors are swallowed.
axes.proposed: Keep existing ids; the native id of a basic-tier harness is stored as 'acp:<harness>:<id>' ('acp:dsh:…', 'acp:opencode:…', 'acp:kimi:…'). Every segment (including single-segment chats) explicitly stores kind, nativeId, instance, provider, model and handoff. Every action first resolves a NativeRef before calling the adapter. Chat data is written to threads/<id>.v2.json (older versions do not read this file name), written only by main, to a temp file first and then renamed. For basic-tier harnesses without loadSession (such as dsh), the transcript is stored by Sage in threads/<id>.items.jsonl, replayed on reopen, and then continued with session/resume. resumeCommand is provided by StaticInfo; for basic-tier harnesses it is provided by quirks and enabled only after conformance verification; without it, it returns null and the copy item is hidden.
axes.examples: A Claude chat can be opened in a new window; the copy command for an opencode chat is given by quirks (for example 'opencode --session <id>', shown only after conformance verification); a dsh chat keeps full history after a restart, and the info panel says “History is kept by MoPilot”.

axes.name: Sage platform services
axes.definition: Services that are harness-independent and used directly by the user: file read/write, terminal, file search, projects, chat list and search, storage and scheduling of scheduled tasks, worktrees and environment scripts, instruction file editing, notifications. They are also the implementation behind the ACP client-side fs and terminal reverse calls.
axes.today: Half is in Electron main (git:*, git:worktreeAdd, fs:readText), and the other half goes through the Codex app-server: fs/writeFile (including saving CLAUDE.md), fs/createDirectory (projectlessCwd, failures swallowed), command/exec (terminal and claude auth login, TerminalPanel.tsx:134), fuzzyFileSearch, project/*, thread/list (⌘K, SearchPalette.tsx:60), $CODEX_HOME/automations. The main view renders only when conn==='ready' and not requiresAuth (App.tsx:108-110; requiresAuth = codexSignedOut && !claudeUsable, App.tsx:42-45); otherwise it shows a Login that only handles Codex login (Login.tsx titled “Welcome to Codex”); the app-server is started unconditionally at launch.
axes.proposed: All of it goes into electron/platform/*, served through platform:* IPC: node fs, node-pty (N-API prebuilt, unpacked to app.asar.unpacked and signed with the release build), bundled ripgrep, projects.json, chat metadata and search index, the scheduler, worktrees and environment scripts, instruction file read/write, notify(kind) (only one notification per chat at a time, with same-kind ones within 60 seconds merged). The Codex app-server is used only by the Codex adapter and started on demand. The App gate becomes “at least one harness is available”; when there is none, show a three-step welcome page: choose how to pay, install a harness recommended for that choice in one click (showing the official install command in the embedded terminal first, then running it), choose the default harness.
axes.examples: A user with only one basic-tier harness installed (such as Kimi Code) can still use the terminal, ⌘K and @ files; scheduled tasks can only pick Codex or Claude Code. Clicking Sign in for Claude in Settings opens the terminal inside the settings page, and detection reruns automatically after login.

axes.name: Sage shared capabilities (tools injected into the agent)
axes.definition: Tools implemented once by Sage and injected per session into each harness: computer use, browser control, and vision fallback for text-only models (locate, describe); plus harness-independent dictation.
axes.today: The agent has no computer use or browser tool at all. Codex's item/tool/call returns -32601 in every window (store.ts:1641-1643); Claude's startSession does not pass mcpServers. server.intercept is a single function slot already taken by accounts.cjs:193. Every app-server message is broadcast to all windows (main.cjs:159-161). The app-server started by Sage auto-loads from ~/.codex cua_repl (plugin unified-computer-use@openai-bundled), the user's own node_repl (wired to Sky CUA and browser-use), and codex_apps (302 ChatGPT connector tools). Settings → Browser only manages Sage's own webview. Dictation borrows the ChatGPT token of the Codex account in use.
axes.proposed: electron/capabilities builds the tool registry, policy, approval and action log; execution happens only once, in main. The three injection channels are declared by the adapter in Negotiated.toolInjection: Claude uses one createSdkMcpServer instance per session (tools set to alwaysLoad, not hidden behind ToolSearch); Codex uses mcp_servers.sage_<nonce> in the thread config (carried by both thread/start and thread/resume, default_tools_approval_mode="approve"), and sets plugins["unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"].enabled=false per thread to turn off the native cua_repl; all basic-tier harnesses inject the stdio sage-mcp through mcpServers in session/new. The server name carries a per-session random suffix, and allow-listing and authorization recognize only this name. Desktop control is executed by the signed MoPilot Computer Use.app helper, and the browser by a Sage-proxied Playwright MCP and the built-in browser's CDP.
axes.examples: “Claude Code wants to control Notes” and “Kimi Code wants to control Notes” are the same authorization card; when Claude Code is paired with a text-only custom endpoint, screenshots go to vision fallback for recognition and the main model only receives the element table; when the user declines cross-vendor consent and has no MoPilot, the task still completes with the AX plus OCR element table.

principles.title: Capabilities are negotiated; anything undeclared is treated as unsupported
principles.rule: A capability appears only after the adapter explicitly declares it. If it is undeclared or negotiation fails, it is treated as unsupported and carries a Why stating the layer, a reason code and a fix action. The Codex CLI, the Claude CLI and all basic-tier harnesses are installed by the user themselves; Sage neither distributes nor pins them. Version policy: StaticInfo.versions only lists a minimum version and known-bad versions; anything above the minimum and not on the known-bad list works as usual, and is only marked “unverified” in Settings' compatibility table, with no badge at chat entry points. Each capability that depends on undocumented or experimental behavior gets a runtime probe (Claude: getSettings, perTaskStopAffordance, origin; Codex: model_providers in the thread config, plugins disabling cua_repl, experimentalFeature/list); a failed probe only greys out that one item (Why.layer=version) and does not turn off the whole harness. When session start fails, show “Claude Code {version} doesn't work with this version of MoPilot. Update it.” and provide an entry for specifying the CLI path manually. Basic-tier harnesses additionally have runtime admission checks (sage-mcp handshake succeeds, image return, privacy patch in effect); if they fail, no new chat can be created. A fix action must actually fix the problem, not be a toggle that stops working after a restart.
principles.why: Today many entry points are assumed to work and only fail on Claude (/review, Feedback, the global voice hotkey). The SDK is pinned at 0.3.295, but the CLI is whatever latest binary is on the user's machine, and Claude updates almost daily; if everything beyond testedVersions were flagged “needs verification”, most users would see it most of the time, and the badge would lose its meaning.
principles.example: Codex goals are on by default (features.goals is stable, defaultEnabled true). Only when the user turns it off themselves does Goal grey out with the fix action “Turn on goals”, written to config.toml via config/value/write (with confirmation before writing); Sage decides by reading experimentalFeature/list, without waiting for the -32600 “goals feature is disabled” error. experimentalFeature/enablement/set is process-level and is lost as soon as the app-server restarts, so it cannot be used as a fix action. If Claude 2.1.3xx removes getSettings, only the ultracode switch greys out: “Claude Code {version} changed how ultracode works · Update MoPilot”.

principles.title: Components read only capability keys, never harness names
principles.rule: No harness name appears under src/components, and no rpc import either. Show/hide, grey-out and routing all read useCaps(chatId), and execution always goes through runSemantic(chatId, cap, args), over IPC to main. Harness names appear only in src/harness/adapters/* (IPC proxies) and electron/harness/*. Pages that belong to a single harness live in the exempt directory components/harness/<kind>/*. tests/boundary.test.ts scans the source to hold the boundary; the count may only go down, never up, and reaches 0 at the end of WP7.
principles.why: Today there are 99 === comparison lines in src, 6 harnessOfThread calls and 11 components importing rpc directly, scattered everywhere, and the same capability is gated inconsistently at different entry points. Nearly all 18 missed gates in gates.txt are components calling Codex RPC directly (Dialogs.tsx:85 feedback/upload, Composer.tsx:133 thread/name/set, TerminalPanel.tsx:134 command/exec, SearchPalette.tsx:60 thread/list); counting === alone cannot hold the line.
principles.example: The Composer's Voice button and the global hotkey both read caps.voiceChat. In Claude and basic-tier chats the two behave identically: route to Codex (with a confirmation dialog the first time it crosses vendors), or hide when Codex is not installed.

principles.title: Pass through by default; Sage intercepts only three kinds of commands
principles.rule: Any command that a harness has a headless implementation for is sent to the harness verbatim. Sage takes over only three kinds: pure UI commands (/new, /settings, /diff, /fork, /model and /permissions without arguments); commands for which the harness only has an interactive implementation: a static list determined per CLI version (on Claude 2.1.295, /tasks, /status, /memory, /skills, /plan, /permissions, /feedback and /resume, which are not listed in supportedCommands and reply “/X isn't available in this environment.”), plus init.terminal_slash_commands (doctor, color, focus and reload-plugins on 2.1.295), and /design-login (not listed either; Sage offers it wherever Claude lists /design or /design-consent, routes /design login to it, and runs the CLI's host sign-in `claude design-login --json`), for which Sage builds its own UI with the control API (local-jsx and terminalOriented are CLI-internal fields that the SDK does not expose); and commands that would break the session (/clear and /reset, /new map to creating a new chat, /exit is forbidden). The only native semantics with no command form are Codex's goal, review and compact, which use the rpc binding. Basic tier: if the harness has pushed available_commands_update, those commands are listed in the menu and typed text is passed through verbatim; typing a command that is not in the catalog shows one line of explanation plus “Send as plain text”; if the harness has never pushed a command catalog (such as dsh), then apart from Sage's UI commands, any typed /xxx is sent to the harness verbatim, with no interception and no prompt.
principles.why: The root cause of “goal doesn't work on Claude” is that Sage intercepted a /goal that could have been passed through, and then degraded it to plain text (store.ts:1253). /init, /review, /compact <args> and /rename are the same class of problem.
principles.example: Typing '/goal all tests pass' in a Claude chat sends it to the CLI as the last content block; the CLI replies with a synthetic “Goal set: all tests pass”, and afterward each unmet check arrives as a synthetic “Stop hook feedback” message, from which Sage assembles the GoalSnapshot. In a Kimi Code chat, /goal appears in the menu via available_commands_update and is likewise passed through verbatim.

principles.title: When something cannot be done, look only at which layer blocks it
principles.rule: Every entry point can land in only one of five presentations: native, Sage polyfill, route to another harness, grey out with a reason and fix action, hide. Which one is chosen depends only on the binding and Why.layer, not on where the entry point is. layer=harness with no polyfill: context menus (+, /, message ⋯, approval cards, TitleBar ⋯) hide it; global entry points (hotkeys, Work in, Voice, ⇧⌘N, quota banner) route to an installed first-class harness that can do it, and otherwise hide. layer is version, provider, model, account, flag or session: all entry points grey out and give a fix action. When the user types exactly a hidden command, show one line of explanation or a route, do not send it to the model, and do not clear the input. “Pop a toast and then send it as a normal message” is forbidden.
principles.why: Today there are five ad hoc treatments of “unsupported”: disable, hide, degrade plus toast, error toast, silently skip, and users cannot tell which of them is a bug. Deciding by layer lets a developer holding a new feature decide directly how to present it; harness-layer differences do not show up in menus, which preserves the clean Codex-style UI.
principles.example: The + menu in a Claude chat does not list Codex plugins (harness layer). Under Claude Code·DeepSeek the ⚡ is greyed out and reads “The DeepSeek endpoint doesn't support Fast” (provider layer). The / menu in a Kimi Code chat lists only the commands Kimi pushed, not Sage's Review (harness layer; basic tier gets no polyfill). In a temporary chat Goal is greyed out and reads “Temporary chats can't have goals · Start a regular chat” (session layer).

principles.title: Polyfills serve only first-class harnesses, and have criteria
principles.rule: For Sage to polyfill a semantic that is missing at the harness layer, it must meet all three conditions: one, state ownership is stated, either reported by the harness or explicitly marked as held by MoPilot, never impersonating the harness's state; two, the difference from the native implementation can be stated in one sentence; three, any extra model spend arises only when the user initiates it and has a visible budget. The polyfill engines are only init (Codex has no /init), shell (Claude has no '!'), and archive/search (Sage metadata), placed in src/harness/polyfills/* and depending only on the adapter contract. The pause for a Claude goal follows the same three conditions: the state (the paused condition) lives in Sage's chat metadata and is labeled “by MoPilot”; the difference is “the turn count restarts after resume”; resume is initiated by a user click. Basic-tier harnesses get no polyfill that does a harness's job for it (no goal, plan, review, init, compact or '!'), and only get Sage's shared tools and Sage-side chat metadata.
principles.why: In both first-class harnesses goal, plan, review, compact and multiAgent are native, so the goalLoop, planGuard and review polyfills are no longer needed; for basic tier, “native passthrough” fits the owner's rule better than “Sage does it for them”, and it also reduces the basic-tier workload to a single generic adapter.
principles.example: Codex's /init: the menu description reads “Create AGENTS.md for Codex · by MoPilot”, and the hover reads “Codex has no built-in init. MoPilot asks Codex to write AGENTS.md and checks with you first if one exists.”. After a Claude goal is paused, the GoalBar reads “Goal paused (kept by MoPilot) · Round count restarts when resumed”.

principles.title: State follows what the harness reports; side effects run once, in main
principles.rule: HarnessAdapter instances, the ChatController's send queue, pendingSwitch settlement and the turn state machine all live in main (electron/harness, electron/session); the renderer has only the IPC proxy and the pure functions resolveCaps and present. plan, permission tier, goal, effort, multi-agent, background tasks, command catalog and context usage are all stored in the SessionState held by main and written only by adapter events. SessionState carries a rev: when a window subscribes it first gets a full snapshot, then applies patches by rev, and refetches the snapshot if it detects a gap. Windows only project; component-local state holds only drafts. Handlers with side effects (shared tool calls, goal pause, approval replies, unattended pause) run only once, in main. The same native session may be written by external clients (the official Codex desktop app, codex resume in a terminal, claude --resume): when the rollout or jsonl changes, adapter.reconcile() rereads thread/read, thread/goal/get, thread/settings or the jsonl; when an external turn is detected running, the Composer is greyed out (session layer: “This chat is running in another app”).
principles.why: planMode sits in the Composer's useState, and when an approval card appears the Composer is unmounted, so Plan is lost (#3). Every app-server message (including server requests) is broadcast to all windows (main.cjs:159-161); if the adapter and send queue stay in the renderer, two windows opening the same chat have two queues and two sends, one computer use click would be executed several times, and unattended handling in main could not reach interrupt.
principles.example: Claude reads permissionMode from init and system/status, Codex reads thread/settings/updated, and basic tier reads current_mode_update and config_option_update; the Plan chip lights and dims with them, and for basic tier the Plan chip appears only if quirks marked which mode is plan. A window opened mid-turn gets the snapshot and shows the same Plan, goal and approval cards.

principles.title: Route by segment, never across vendors
principles.rule: Any action targeting a particular turn or the current session first resolves a NativeRef before calling the adapter; command-type semantics settle pendingSwitch first. The rpc layer asserts that the segment kind matches the adapter kind. Account switching happens only within the same Provider and the same billing method. Cross-vendor data flows (changing Provider, handoff, routing to a new chat on another vendor, cross-vendor vision fallback, the dictation engine) require an explicit user choice and must state where the data goes; the first time routing to another vendor, use a confirmation dialog, not a chip; later route chips also state the target harness, the account and “this is a new chat”.
principles.why: Feedback would send a Claude session id along with Codex logs to OpenAI (#8). With pendingSwitch, /goal would be set on the old harness, and the old thread would auto-continue with an active goal (#11). If switching to a DeepSeek or MoPilot key were allowed when the subscription quota runs out, it would resume the same transcript carrying Anthropic thinking, and the content would also be sent to another vendor. A user who defaults to Claude clicking Cloud or voice would have their content sent to OpenAI without knowing it beforehand.
principles.example: Editing a message on a Claude segment uses Claude's rewind binding, and no longer calls thread/revert on the Codex thread of the first segment. When the Max subscription quota runs out, the banner offers “Continue on MoPilot credits”; clicking it opens the SwitchSheet and starts a new segment without resume. Pressing the voice hotkey in a Claude chat shows “Voice chat is provided by Codex. It starts a new Codex chat on your ChatGPT account, and what you say goes to OpenAI. ☐ Include a summary of this chat”.

principles.title: Respect the harness's default behavior
principles.rule: When the adapter starts a session, it reproduces the harness's default behavior as in its own CLI. Sage's instructions may only be appended, and configuration may only be merged, never replaced. There are only three places that change a harness's default behavior: privacy (turn off default uploads), capability prerequisites (for example tool injection, turning off the harness's built-in computer use and browser), and declarations that pair with Sage's UI (for example perTaskStopAffordance must ship in the same version as the task stop entry). Privacy changes must fail closed: verify before launch that they truly took effect, and do not start if verification fails. All of these are written as conformance checks.
principles.why: Sage's Claude sessions differ from the terminal in five places: no systemPrompt preset (the SDK sends an empty string, and on 2.1.295 the system prompt measured only 141 tokens versus 3,315 tokens with the preset, #7), no perTaskStopAffordance (Stop kills background subagents too, #17), CLAUDE_CODE_* removed (#35), messages carry no origin (ultracode keywords stop working, #6), and / commands not in the last block (#19). By default dsh attaches up to 8 MiB of session log upload to every request body; now that dsh is demoted to a user-installed basic-tier harness, if the patch format changes the protection silently stops working.
principles.example: The Claude adapter always passes systemPrompt {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append, snapshot:true} (snapshot keeps changes to append from breaking the cached prefix). dsh's quirks launch argument --patch sage.patch.yml only turns off session-log-deepseek and changes the acp-line model to deepseek-flash, and env adds DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; before launch it runs dsh --dump-config with the same arguments to confirm session-log-deepseek is disabled, and if not it refuses to start and shows “This dsh version can't turn off session log upload”. DSH_HOME is no longer isolated, and customSkillDirs is not added.

principles.title: Platform services and shared capabilities belong to Sage, and authorization is in Sage's hands
principles.rule: fs, terminal, search, projects, scheduled tasks and instruction files are provided by SagePlatform, not through any harness. Computer use, browser and vision fallback are implemented once by Sage and injected per session through the channel declared by the adapter, without writing ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.claude.json or any harness's global config, and without changing the native host manifest. The injected server name is sage_<per-session random nonce>, and the harness's permission layer allows only this name; any MCP server named sage in user or project config is never auto-allowed. Authorization is enforced only inside Sage's tool handlers. Three floors that no mode can lift: the agent cannot control MoPilot itself or system security UI; approval cards and permission settings accept only human-initiated input (judged by the event's source process: allow system assistive technologies, block synthetic events produced by the helper or any agent process; there is also a keyboard alternative: hold ⌘↩ for one second on an approval card to confirm); an unattended turn can only use apps that have already been authorized.
principles.why: Users with only Claude installed get stuck at “Couldn't connect to Codex”. Each vendor's native computer use is limited by plan, login method and interaction mode: Claude's built-in one is available only in interactive subscription sessions, Claude in Chrome is disabled under an API key and a third-party base URL, Codex's is tied to the ChatGPT account and region, and dsh's is an experimental plugin. You cannot assemble “works on all harnesses” from them. Judging by “is it a synthetic event” would lock users of voice control and switch control out of approvals.
principles.example: In the Claude read-only tier, mcp__sage_7f3a__screenshot and mcp__sage_7f3a__get_state are added to allowedTools one by one; in the default and auto tiers canUseTool allows mcp__sage_7f3a__* directly (on 2.1.295 canUseTool was measured to fire for SDK MCP tools), and the handler decides. When a basic-tier request_permission sees a sage_7f3a tool, it automatically replies allow-once, and the real authorization card is shown by Sage.

principles.title: One release, no transitional code
principles.rule: The design has exactly one target form. The code each work package produces is part of the final architecture, developed in dependency order and merged into one long-lived release branch (half-finished work is never merged to trunk), and shipped in the same release; before public release two dogfood rings are allowed, Ring 0 and Ring 1. Remote switches are used only as kill switches (turn off a harness, an injection channel or computer use), not to hide half-finished work. Uncertain items that need measurement are written as conformance checks, and the check result only chooses between branches already written out in the design, without triggering a redesign. Line numbers are as of 7a5bf12 and should be checked by function name during implementation.
principles.why: The previous version first stopped the bleeding with a very thin ops.ts and then wired in the adapter, which means writing the same capability twice; Phase 0 declared perTaskStopAffordance first and Phase 1 only built the stop entry, so in the intermediate version a runaway Workflow could not be stopped. The previous version also wrote “until the gateway capability table is ready, treat everything as unpriced”, which is transitional logic to be replaced later; now the capability table is in WP0 and WP3 reads it directly.
principles.example: For Codex's computer-control channel, conformance X7 chose the latter between dynamicTools and mcp_servers in the thread config (dynamicTools turns images into data-URL strings under the forced code mode, so the model cannot see the image unless it calls image()); both branches are written out in the design, and once chosen only the design text of the unchosen one is deleted, and the code is written only once.

layers.name: UI shell (src/components, src/App.tsx)
layers.owns: Rendering, interaction, copy, and the Codex-style layout.
layers.today: Components call Codex RPC directly: Dialogs.tsx:85 calls feedback/upload, Composer.tsx:133 calls thread/name/set, TerminalPanel.tsx:134 calls command/exec, SearchPalette.tsx:60 calls thread/list. About 40 places hard-code “Codex”. The / menu is two unrelated tables (Composer.tsx:91-138 and 987-1066). Plan state lives in the Composer's useState. The banners, chips and strips around the Composer have no position budget. Settings has 21 sidebar sections, about 32 navigable pages and about 150 setting rows.

The command menu is generated from a registry; ConfigOption, approval cards, GoalBar and the task panel are all rendered by generic components, with copy fetched by key from the English copy table and info.label interpolated. The Composer keeps only one status strip and one “next message” chip slot. Settings information architecture: accounts live in Accounts & billing only (grouped by Provider, each row stating which harnesses it can be used for, with harness pages holding only a link); each first-class harness gets one page with sub-sections (no 6 tabs); all basic-tier harnesses go into one Other harnesses page; “Sage tools” is renamed Built-in tools (Computer use, Browser, Voice & dictation); Applies to is shown only when it is not “all harnesses”; at release the sidebar has no more than today's 21 items, and the total number of Rows is no more than today's plus 10. Harness-specific pages live in components/harness/<kind>/*.

layers.today: Does not exist. The relevant decisions are scattered across store.ts:1253 (goal toast), select.ts:43 (filtering ultra), Composer.tsx:494 (voice), FAST_BLOCKED_TEXT (src/harness/types.ts) and other places.

Inputs are the adapter descriptor, ProviderProfile, ModelInfo, account capabilities, feature flags and SessionState; outputs are the Binding and CapState of each semantic. init and shell run in main, depend only on the adapter contract, and apply only to first-class harnesses. layers.name: Chat orchestration layer (electron/session/*; the renderer has only an IPC proxy)
layers.owns: Routing among chat, segment and native; send queue and steer; migration rules for handoff and SwitchSheet; the turn state machine (idle, running, awaitingUser, crashed); per-chat instance and config; SessionState; reconciliation of external writes; the exit gate.
layers.today: All piled into store.ts, running in the renderer. Codex notifications change state directly in onNotification, while Claude goes through a separate onEvent. Some actions use the chat id and others use nativeOf. Queue items drop SendOptions (store.ts:1270, #50). Goal routing happens before performSwitch (store.ts:1253-1263, #11). There is no handling at all when a harness process exits mid-turn.
layers.proposed: All in main. Every action first resolves a NativeRef, and pendingSwitch settles first. SessionState is updated only by HarnessEvent. Whether a goal is active and whether a turn is running are modeled separately; each turn is marked as to whether it was initiated directly by the user (needed for the unattended determination). Queue items store the complete SendOptions, and messages carrying a plan or goal do not go through steer. Crash path: when a harness process exits mid-turn, the turn enters crashed: clear all pending approval cards of that session and label them “{label} quit”, abort any computer use action in progress, release the desktop lock, and invalidate that session's sage-mcp token; the queue is kept and not auto-resent; Codex goals are marked paused. The app-server auto-restarts with backoff, at most 3 times, after which it becomes a banner.

layers.name: Harness adapter layer (electron/harness/*; src/harness/adapters/* is only an IPC proxy)
layers.owns: The native protocol, the three-layer descriptor, semantic bindings, command catalog, event translation, native default behavior, injection channels, history reading, and reconciliation of external writes.
layers.today: Codex has no adapter: the UI item is the Codex v2 shape, and the RPC is in the renderer's store.ts; Claude is translated into this shape by claude.ts, claudeTranslate.ts and harness/claude/index.cjs, dropping task_*, subagent messages (claudeTranslate.ts:269, 288) and system/status. There is no ACP.
layers.proposed: Three adapters, all in main: codex (RPC moved out of store.ts), claude (wrapping the existing harness/claude/index.cjs), acp (a generic implementation, one quirks file per harness, with privacyDefaults and admission required in quirks). The control plane takes the ACP shape, the data plane keeps v2 items, plus Sage extension items (goal, task, commandOutput, switchNote, computerAction). Each adapter gets a conformance test and golden replay of recorded sessions; the ACP adapter also has a fake agent for tests (tests/fixtures/fake-acp-agent).

layers.name: Identity layer (electron/identity/*: consolidated from accounts.cjs, harness/claude/accounts.cjs, relay.cjs, mopilot.cjs, billing.ts)
layers.owns: ProviderProfile, Instance, AccountDriver, credential and config-directory isolation, endpoint injection, model catalog, usage, account-switching policy, billing method, env snapshot, and the payment choice on the welcome page.
layers.today: Codex is an account pool plus a relay, non-default accounts use a sidecar CODEX_HOME, and mopilot is mixed into the account pool. Claude has one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account, and API key and MoPilot are harness-level mode files. scrubProcessEnv uses /^(ANTHROPIC_|CLAUDE_CODE_|CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_|CLAUDECODE$)/ to delete the user's variables at startup (harness/claude/index.cjs:31, 176-178).
layers.proposed: An Instance registry, one AccountDriver each for Codex and Claude, one generic “Managed by the harness” account row for basic tier, and a ProviderProfile registry. Account switching is limited to the same ProviderProfile and the same billing method. At startup, first save an env snapshot of the login shell; scrubProcessEnv and cleanEnv share the narrowed list, and Provider variables are written last. Usage is unified as UsageSnapshot{windows, source, at}. Background calls (title, extras, command catalog prefetch) use the account the chat uses.

layers.name: Sage platform services layer (electron/platform/*)
layers.owns: fs, terminal pty, file search, projects, chat metadata and search index, scheduler, worktrees and environment scripts, instruction files, notifications; the implementation of ACP client-side fs and terminal.
layers.today: git:*, git:worktreeAdd and fs:readText are in main; the rest goes through the Codex app-server. When Codex is not connected or not logged in, App.tsx:108-110 does not render the main view, and Scheduled.tsx requires conn to be ready.
layers.proposed: All in main, through platform:* IPC. The Codex app-server is used only by the Codex adapter and started on demand; on first launch, if Codex is installed, start the app-server once on demand in the background, import project/* into projects.json, and if that fails, record it and import again the next time Codex connects. Chat metadata merges into threads/<id>.v2.json.

layers.name: Shared capabilities and security layer (electron/capabilities/*, Contents/Helpers/MoPilot Computer Use.app, Contents/Helpers/sage-mcp)
layers.owns: Tool definitions for computer use, browser and vision fallback; policy (restricted-area table, app authorization, site permissions, irreversible actions, credential rules, unattended rules, takeover rules); approval events; the global desktop lock; the action log; engine health status; peer verification for sage-mcp and the helper.
layers.today: Does not exist. The packaging config has no Electron fuses (scripts/package.mjs has only asar: true and no flipFuses), and RunAsNode is on by default: any local process (including the agent's own bash) can run the signed MoPilot binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, so “verify the peer's signature” can be fooled.
layers.proposed: One tool definition injected over three channels, with authorization enforced inside the handler. Packaging uses @electron/fuses to turn off RunAsNode, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable and EnableNodeCliInspectArguments, and to turn on OnlyLoadAppFromAsar and EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation; @playwright/mcp therefore runs in a utilityProcess instead. sage-mcp is a signed native helper (Swift, Contents/Helpers/sage-mcp) and does not rely on Electron running as node. main's socket verifies two things for each connection: a per-session token, and that the direct parent process pid equals the pid of that session's harness process; the token rotates on every resume, is valid only in main's memory, and is invalidated when the session ends (the Codex thread config is written into the rollout, so an old token left on disk is useless). The helper accepts only connections whose audit token pid equals the registered main pid and whose signature matches. The helper is signed with #16's Developer ID, with separate entitlements, signed from the inside out. Engines (@playwright/mcp) are pinned to exact versions; the helper does not embed cua-driver (decision WP8-3). The desktop lock lives in the helper, one global per user (only one even when several profiles run at once), and the holder is shown in the tray. Indication has three layers: tray, a glow on the target window, and an activity strip in the chat.

layers.name: Persistence and data model (userData = ~/Library/Application Support/MoPilot Code)
layers.owns: Chats, segments, chat metadata, transcripts stored by Sage itself, goal pauses held by Sage, preferences, scheduled tasks, projects, Provider and account metadata (secrets in the keychain).
layers.today: ui-state.json is rewritten in full by every window every 250ms, and holds prefs, pinned, unread, claudeArchived, claudeChats and worktreeOf. segments are stored in threads/<id>.json, written only for multi-segment chats, written directly with writeFileSync, with errors swallowed; the old readSegments reads any json that has a segments array, and treats any unrecognized kind as Codex. plan, goal and account-switch notes are not persisted. #16 already migrated the profile from Sage Codex to MoPilot and added a per-profile single-instance lock.
layers.proposed: threads/<id>.v2.json = {schemaVersion:2, segments[], meta{archived, pinned, unread, projectId, config, account, goalHeld, notes[]}}, written atomically per chat by main only (temp file plus rename); threads/<id>.items.jsonl for basic-tier harnesses with history:'sage'; prefs merged by key in main; automations/, projects.json. Migration runs in main before any window opens, is idempotent, and carries a schemaVersion and a completion marker; old keys in ui-state.json are frozen and not deleted, old threads/<id>.json are kept, and changes to Codex and Claude segments are mirrored back to the old location write-only during 0.3.x (acp segments are never mirrored), so reinstalling an older version shows the old data but not basic-tier chats created after the migration or the new fields. Old chats with no file get a v2 file generated lazily by one hard-coded legacy rule ('claude:' prefix → claude, everything else → codex), and this rule appears only once, in the migration code. The userData path and bundle id are not changed again.

layers.name: Harness engine processes
layers.owns: Their own agent loops and session files.
layers.today: codex app-server is started at launch and is a global hard dependency. Since #17, Codex threads idle for 5 seconds (on screen or not) are thread/unsubscribed, checked every 2 seconds (store.ts:523, 670), and on-screen ones follow the disk instead (store.ts:758-760); threads with a background terminal, a server-side queue or an active goal keep a lease (store.ts:744-752). Claude has one SDK process per active session, reclaimed after 10 idle minutes (harness/claude/index.cjs:366, 831), and the reclaimer looks only at keep, busy and perms.
layers.proposed: The app-server starts on demand and auto-restarts with backoff after a crash, at most 3 times; the existing goal, background terminal and queue checks in release() are kept. The Claude reclaimer does not close a session that has background tasks, a loop or cron (close() kills all background tasks). Each basic-tier instance gets one ACP process, reclaimed when idle. All harness child processes are started with the login shell's PATH and env snapshot, and launched via disclaim so they do not inherit the helper's TCC grants.

layers.name: MoPilot cloud (web/: gateway, accounts, telemetry)
layers.owns: The code.mopilot.ai gateway (Anthropic, OpenAI, and an optional DeepSeek upstream), pricing and settlement, /v1/models and the capability table, accounts and device keys, consent and telemetry intake.
layers.today: proxy.ts has only three upstreams, anthropic, openai-responses and openai-chat (proxy.ts:12-15), and forwards requests unchanged apart from rewriting model; usage.ts parses only input, output and cache tokens and does not read server_tool_use or service_tier (#76). The desktop app PUTs the consent value on every launch (#80).
layers.proposed: WP0: /v1/models returns only priced models and attaches the capability table (the mopilot ProviderProfile's drops are delivered from it); service_tier and speed are priced separately or rejected; parse server_tool_use and web_search billing. WP9: a DeepSeek upstream for Claude Code·MoPilot to use deepseek-flash (optional, and not a dependency of any basic-tier harness); a transcription route for dictation; consent merges to the stricter party.

descriptorNote: Besides the two first-class adapters, codex and claude, any ACP harness plugs in as acp:<id>; components read only the result of resolveCaps and the CapState given by present(). Binding has no tool variant, and polyfill is reduced to init, shell, archive and search, effective only for first-class harnesses. Negotiated.toolInjection has exactly one value per harness (sdkMcp, threadConfigMcp, sessionMcp): after conformance, Codex uses only the MCP in the thread config, so no array is needed. Negotiated's history and toolInjection cover the differences that basic-tier harnesses have no history replay and can only inject MCP in session/new; versions and probes implement the version policy of “minimum version plus known-bad versions, probing per capability”. GoalSnapshot no longer has an owner: goal state is always reported by the harness, and only Claude's pause and round cap are held by Sage (stated by pauseBy and budgetBy), with source distinguishing Codex's rpc from Claude's synthetic messages. SessionState carries a rev, and a window takes a snapshot first and then applies patches. ProviderProfile, ModelInfo, AccountCaps, FeatureFlags, SageToolset and SageItem all have sketches.

uiPolicies.when: The current segment's harness supports this semantic natively (binding is rpc, passthrough or config)
uiPolicies.pattern: Entry point position, icon and shortcut are fixed per semantic and identical across all harnesses. How it is executed is decided by the adapter. Labels and documentation links use the harness's native wording. State is projected into the same generic component, which draws only the controls the adapter has declared and does not invent buttons the harness lacks; controls held by Sage are labeled “by MoPilot”.
uiPolicies.example: /goal: Codex calls thread/goal/set (on a new thread it starts the turn itself, and Sage renders the user's “/goal X” bubble itself), and the GoalBar has pause, resume, budget, edit and clear, with the budget stated to be a soft cap; Claude passes through '/goal <condition>', and the GoalBar has round count, clear, and a pause and resume labeled “by MoPilot”; Kimi Code passes /goal through, the output is rendered in the command output style, and no GoalBar is drawn. Plan: Codex sends collaborationMode and Claude uses permissionMode, with the same Plan chip; for basic tier the Plan chip appears only if quirks marked a plan mode.
uiPolicies.surfaces: / menu, + menu, GoalBar, Plan chip, Review page, model picker

uiPolicies.when: Why.layer=harness, the current segment is first-class, and a polyfill engine meets the three criteria (state ownership stated; difference explained in one sentence; extra spend user-initiated with a visible budget)
uiPolicies.pattern: Placed in the same position and under the same name as the native one, with no harness badge. Only a small label “by MoPilot” is used, and hover shows a one-sentence description of the difference; in Settings' capability matrix this cell reads “MoPilot”. When the criteria are not met or the current segment is basic tier, always handle it as hide or route at the harness layer.
uiPolicies.example: Codex's Init: “Create AGENTS.md for Codex · by MoPilot”. A '!cmd' in a Claude chat is run by Sage's terminal, and the output is sent as an attachment, annotated “Ran on this Mac, outside Claude Code's sandbox”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: / menu, + menu, GoalBar, Composer, ⌘K, archive page

uiPolicies.when: Why.layer=harness, no usable polyfill, and the entry point is in a context menu (+, /, message ⋯, approval card, TitleBar ⋯)
uiPolicies.pattern: List only what the current segment can do, with no greying out and no errors. The one exception: when the user types a hidden command exactly in the input box and presses Enter, a popover shows one line of explanation (with a route button if an installed first-class harness can do it), does not send it to the model, and does not clear the input. When a basic-tier harness has not pushed a command catalog there are no “hidden commands”, and /xxx is passed through verbatim.
uiPolicies.example: The / menu in a Kimi Code chat has only the commands Kimi pushed; typing /feedback and pressing Enter in a Claude chat shows “Claude Code only takes feedback in its own terminal. Your message wasn't sent.”. A /xxx typed in a dsh chat (which has no command catalog) is sent to dsh verbatim.
uiPolicies.surfaces: + menu, / menu, message ⋯, approval card, TitleBar ⋯

uiPolicies.when: Why.layer=harness, no usable polyfill, the entry point is global (hotkey, Work in, Voice button, ⇧⌘N, quota-exhausted banner), and another installed first-class harness can do it
uiPolicies.pattern: Show a greyed-out line with a harness badge, a one-sentence reason and an action button. For an existing chat: “Continue on X” opens the SwitchSheet with the target preselected. For a new chat: only this new chat's harness changes, shown in the Composer's “next message” chip slot and undoable, without changing the default harness; the chip must state the target harness, the account and “this is a new chat”. The first time each user routes to another vendor, use a confirmation dialog instead of a chip, stating where the data goes; voice routing offers a “bring a summary of this chat” option, with the summary generated by the source harness. When the target is not installed the action becomes “Install / Sign in”; when no harness can do it, hide. Never switch automatically.
uiPolicies.example: Pressing the voice hotkey in a Kimi Code chat shows a confirmation dialog the first time: “Voice chat is provided by Codex. It starts a new Codex chat on your ChatGPT account, and what you say goes to OpenAI. ☐ Include a summary of this chat [Start] [Cancel]”. Pressing ⇧⌘N when the default harness is a basic-tier one shows the chip “This temporary chat uses Claude Code (Max · a@b.com) · Kimi Code can't keep chats off disk · Undo”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: Global hotkeys, Work in, Voice button, ⇧⌘N, quota-exhausted banner

uiPolicies.when: Why.layer is version, provider, model, account, flag or session: the harness has this capability, but it is blocked by a version probe, endpoint, model, account, feature flag or current state
uiPolicies.pattern: All entry points (including the / menu and + menu) keep the control and grey it out, dimmed in the primary color rather than plain grey. Hover shows a one-sentence reason, and clicking offers the fix action. Reasons come from a unified English copy table, in the format “one sentence of reason · one action”. Session-layer reasons (turn running, awaiting approval, signing in, temporary chat, chat running in another app) become available automatically once the state recovers, with no toast. Never leave the user at a dead end.
uiPolicies.example: The ⚡ under Claude Code·DeepSeek: “The DeepSeek endpoint doesn't support Fast”. Claude's ⚡ under MoPilot: “Fast isn't available on MoPilot yet · Use your Claude subscription”. The user turned off Codex goals themselves: “Goals are off in Codex · Turn on goals”. Switching harness mid-turn: “Wait for this turn to finish”. Approve for me under a Claude model that does not support auto: “This model can't auto-approve · Switch model”. Editing a message in a Claude chat created before the upgrade: “Created before checkpoints · Fork from here instead”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: Model picker, attachment menu, permission menu, / menu, + menu, HarnessPicker, account row

uiPolicies.when: A whole feature unique to one first-class harness
uiPolicies.pattern: Placed only in that harness's settings page, and where needed offer passthrough of the native command in that harness's chats, with a harness badge. Not put into Built-in tools, not polyfilled, and no control added on the Composer. Features unique to a basic-tier harness do not appear in Sage and are used only through command passthrough.
uiPolicies.example: Unique to Codex: Codex Cloud, Credits and reset vouchers, Experimental features, Control this Mac, import into Codex, realtime voice. Unique to Claude: output styles (set in Settings → Claude Code, with /output-style passed through in chats), the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, plugins (managed by the claude plugin CLI, listed read-only by Sage, installed through the embedded terminal), /schedule cloud routines (menu description reads “Cloud routine on claude.ai (not in MoPilot Scheduled)”).
uiPolicies.surfaces: Settings pages per harness, the Codex Cloud group in the sidebar

uiPolicies.when: A setting applies to only some harnesses, or is overridden by a setting elsewhere
uiPolicies.pattern: Applies to is shown only when it is not “all harnesses”: a specific harness, this chat, new chats, or “Only affects Codex outside MoPilot”. Dead settings with no reader are deleted or wired up, and deletions are recorded in the release notes (“These settings never took effect and were removed”). Source badges appear only in the / menu, in Settings, and on hover. Applies to generates an inventory snapshot from the Settings descriptors that goes into npm test, and acceptance only checks that the snapshot matches the UI.
uiPolicies.example: Approval policy on the Codex page is labeled “Only affects Codex outside MoPilot”. “When a limit is reached” appears only once in each Provider group of Accounts & billing.

uiPolicies.when: A lossy migration: switching harness mid-chat, switching Provider, or switching to an account that does not share the session directory
uiPolicies.pattern: The SwitchSheet has three columns: Comes along / Stays behind / Changes. The “Changes” column always lists: the account and Provider used by the new segment (and where the data goes), the effort mapping (for example “Effort: xhigh → high”), the multi-agent state (not migrated by default, the user must tick it), and permission changes (may only stay the same or become stricter, for example “Approve for me → Ask for approval (this model can't auto-approve)”). Queued messages are listed under “Stays behind”, or sent along with the switch (the user chooses). Goal: across harnesses, the old segment's goal pauses and is not carried over by default, with a checkbox to continue it on the new segment; when changing Provider within the same harness, “Continue this goal” is ticked by default. After the switch a divider note is inserted in the chat and persisted; when switching back to a harness already used, the divider reads “Back on Codex · Caught up on 6 messages from Claude Code”.
uiPolicies.example: Codex to Claude Code: “Goal "all tests pass" pauses on Codex ☐ Continue this goal on Claude Code”; “Account: Claude Max (a@b.com) · Your next messages and the handoff summary go to Anthropic”; “2 background terminals will stop”. Switching to a basic-tier harness offers only “New chat with summary”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: SwitchSheet, switch divider, chat info panel

uiPolicies.when: Around the Composer, multiple states need to be shown at once (goal, approval, control, tasks, switch, Cloud, billing, keywords)
uiPolicies.pattern: Only two positions. One status strip, showing a single item at a time, with priority: controlling the computer > awaiting approval > goal > background tasks, the rest going into the task panel. One “next message” chip slot, shared by switching harness, Cloud, and new chats routed to another harness, with only one shown at a time. Billing is shown only in the model picker and the avatar menu. Keywords such as ultracode and ultrathink are highlighted only inside the input box. The Full access banner is kept, with its copy interpolated per harness.
uiPolicies.example: In a Claude chat with a goal running and 2 background Workflows at the same time: the status strip shows the goal, and the task panel icon shows “2”. When the agent starts controlling Notes, the status strip changes to “Controlling Notes · Move the mouse to take over · Esc to stop”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: Composer, task panel, model picker, avatar menu

uiPolicies.when: Sage shared capabilities: computer use, browser, vision fallback, dictation
uiPolicies.policy: Sage polyfill (one implementation for all harnesses)
uiPolicies.pattern: All harnesses use the same authorization card, the same activity strip and the same stop button. Differences appear in only two places: the “control source” column in the Settings matrix, and a one-line explanation when the model cannot see images. A harness's own computer use or browser is not used as a source: Codex has cua_repl turned off per thread, Claude always passes --no-chrome (the Claude in Chrome option is removed, and “Your Chrome” is provided by Sage's browser channel), dsh's experimental plugin is off by default and quirks only assert it is not enabled. Where it cannot be turned off (the user's own node_repl in Codex, before it is verified), the helper's event tap is the backstop, and computer use is marked “needs verification” on Codex segments.
uiPolicies.example: “Claude Code wants to control Notes” and “Kimi Code wants to control Notes” are the same card. When Claude Code is paired with a text-only custom endpoint, the activity strip reads “glm-5v reads the screen · Screenshots go to Zhipu”.
uiPolicies.surfaces: Approval card, chat activity strip, tray, Settings → Built-in tools

conflicts.conflict: Goal mechanics and available controls differ per harness; Claude's goal won't stop
conflicts.codex: thread/goal/set|get|clear plus thread/goal/updated and thread/goal/cleared. States: active, paused, blocked, usageLimited, budgetLimited, complete; carries tokenBudget; when the thread is idle the server resumes it automatically. Measured on 0.162: calling set on a new thread with no turn starts a turn by itself, produces no userMessage and writes no goal item; set paused does not stop a turn that is already running (the model changed the goal from paused to complete within the same turn); set active on a goal that is already complete re-runs it; tokenBudget is a soft limit that is only enforced at turn boundaries, and a single turn overshot it by about 90x in testing; the model has its own create_goal, get_goal and update_goal tools, so a goal can appear without going through Sage; goals is enabled by default, and when it is disabled set, get and clear return -32600 "goals feature is disabled", while an ephemeral thread returns -32600 "ephemeral thread does not support goals". appendTranscriptItem is not part of ThreadGoalSetParams and the server silently ignores it. Sage's problems: after setting a goal it also calls startTurn, so '/goal clear' gets set as a new goal (#10; the part that called set with the chat id was already fixed by #17's withLease->nativeOf, store.ts:1257); Esc only sends turn/interrupt and does not pause the goal (store.ts:1489, #2); when setting a goal on an ephemeral thread fails, the objective is still sent (#49).
conflicts.claude: Send plain text '/goal <condition>' (it must be the last content block). The CLI registers a session-level Stop hook and replies with a synthetic message "Goal set: <condition>", then keeps working within the same turn; each unmet check arrives as a synthetic user message "Stop hook feedback:\n[<condition>]: <reason>", and once the condition is met the turn simply ends, with no "met" event in the stream. Measured on 2.1.295: active_goal is only emitted when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is set and never appears in the local SDK stream; goal_status (met, condition, reason) is only written to the transcript jsonl; the goal is still active after interrupt(); a '/goal clear' queued while the loop is running is not executed until the loop ends; the only usage is '[<condition> | clear]', with no pause, resume or budget. When Sage intercepts it, it shows a toast and the goal is never set (store.ts:1253, #1). Basic tier: Kimi and Qwen push /goal through the command catalog, Copilot has an autopilot mode; dsh's create_goal and update_goal are just tools the model calls itself.
conflicts.decision: goal is one semantic, the GoalSnapshot state is always reported by the harness, and the controls are declared by the adapter. Codex is bound to rpc with the full set of controls, all via nativeOf: '/goal X' always only calls thread/goal/set {threadId, objective, status:'active'}; on a new thread it starts the turn by itself, so Sage no longer calls startTurn and no longer does "send the first turn, then set"; because there is no userMessage item, Sage renders the user's "/goal X" bubble locally and writes it into the chat metadata; on an existing thread it only calls set; if Plan is on, switch back to default first; Stop or Pause = set paused followed by turn/interrupt (500ms timeout), and the UI accepts a late paused->complete that arrives afterwards; a complete goal does not show Resume (resume would re-run it), only Clear and edit-then-reset; always subscribe to thread/goal/updated and cleared whether or not Sage did the set; call thread/goal/get when a thread is opened; keep release()'s existing checks for goal, background terminals and queue; ephemeral threads are greyed out at the session layer, and when it fails the send is aborted and the input is put back; whether goals is disabled is read from experimentalFeature/list. The exit gate sets every active Codex goal to paused before exit and records "paused on exit"; if an active goal is found at launch (the last run crashed before it could pause), set paused first, then thread/resume. Claude is bound to passthrough, the GoalSnapshot is assembled from the synthetic messages, and pausing and the round limit are held by Sage (see claudeGoal): Stop or Pause = interrupt() then '/goal clear', with the condition stored in meta.goalHeld; Resume re-sends '/goal <condition>'; reaching the budget limit likewise does interrupt first, then clear. Basic tier: if the command catalog has goal (Kimi, Qwen), pass it through, and Copilot's autopilot is passed through as a mode; otherwise it is none(harness), and Goal appears in neither the + menu nor the / menu; dsh's create_goal and update_goal render as ordinary tool cards. Goal routing goes after performSwitch; on switching away, the old Codex segment gets set paused, and the old Claude segment gets interrupt then clear with the condition recorded; Sage does not manage basic-tier goals, and SwitchSheet only shows the hint "{label} may still have a goal running".
conflicts.ui: A single GoalBar that draws its buttons from controls. Codex: "Goal: {condition} · {n} rounds · {b} token budget (soft, checked between turns) [Pause] [Edit] [Clear]". Claude while running: "Goal: {condition} · round {n} [Pause] [Clear]"; after pausing: "Goal paused (kept by MoPilot) · Round count restarts when resumed [Resume] [Clear]". A limit added by Sage is labelled separately as "Limit set by MoPilot", and when the limit is reached a note is inserted into the chat: "Reached the limit (30 rounds). Goal paused · Limit set by MoPilot [10 more rounds] [Clear]"; units the harness does not support are not shown (Codex shows only tokens, Claude only rounds). Chat rows in the sidebar show a goal icon; notifications are sent when a goal completes, is blocked, reaches its budget or needs authorization, following the rule "one per chat, items that need your action first, merged within 60 seconds".
