Goal is greyed out in temporary chats and side chats.

conflicts.conflict: Plan mode is implemented in different places, and its state gets lost
conflicts.codex: turn/start.collaborationMode {mode:'plan'} is a thread-level setting; when Sage turns Plan off it passes undefined, never sends default, and there is no "execute this plan" (store.ts:1400, #13). Measured on 0.162: a plan turn emits thread/settings/updated; gpt-6.1-sol produces a plan ThreadItem (streamed as item/plan/delta), while gpt-6-luna only gives an ordinary agentMessage; turn/plan/updated is only used for the update_plan checklist; thread/settings/update can switch the mode without sending a turn.
conflicts.claude: permissionMode 'plan' plus ExitPlanMode approval; approving without updatedPermissions leaves a session that started in plan landing in default (#12). On both sides planMode lives in the Composer's useState and is lost as soon as the approval card appears (#3), and queued messages lose plan (#50). Measured on 2.1.295: setPermissionMode('plan') emits system/status; the model writes the plan to ~/.claude/plans/<slug>.md, loads ExitPlanMode via ToolSearch and calls it, and canUseTool receives {plan, planFilePath}; approving with updatedPermissions [{type:'setMode', mode:'acceptEdits', destination:'session'}] goes back to an execution tier. Basic tier: Kimi, Cursor, Qwen, Copilot and Gemini have a plan mode or configOption; dsh has no modes.
conflicts.decision: Plan is a standalone state in SessionState, and the harness's report is authoritative. Codex sends plan or default explicitly every turn, takes presets from collaborationMode/list, has the Plan chip read thread/settings/updated, and uses thread/settings/update when the chip is toggled, with no turn needed; when a plan turn ends, Sage builds the plan card from the plan item (or from the last agentMessage if there is none), and "Implement this plan ▾" switches back to default and then sends. Claude remembers the tier from before entering plan, and when ExitPlanMode is approved it returns updatedPermissions setMode to go back to that tier; it reads EnterPlanMode and system/status; the plan card is rendered once from ExitPlanMode's plan field, with planFilePath attached. Basic tier: the Plan chip appears only if plan is in modes or in a category-mode configOption and quirks flags it; toggling goes through session/set_mode or set_config_option; Cursor's cursor/create_plan is rendered as a plan card only when quirks defines the mapping; planGuard is no longer used for modes that are merely read-only; if none of these apply, the chip is hidden. '/plan <description>' is equivalent to turning Plan on and sending the description.
conflicts.ui: The Plan chip (Shift+Tab) does not change when the approval card appears. Codex and Claude use the same plan approval card, the plan body is rendered only once, and the "Implement this plan ▾" button lets you pick the execution tier.

conflicts.conflict: Review entry points, implementation and the Code Review page
conflicts.codex: review/start {threadId, target, delivery}. startReview does not check the harness: when the current segment is Claude, withLease hands claude:<id> unchanged to Codex review/start (store.ts:697-698, 1612); delivery takes prefs.reviewDelivery, which may be the deprecated detached (measured on 0.162 to emit a deprecationNotice). The Code Review page always calls startThread first to create a new Codex thread (#4). Item order of an inline review measured on 0.162: enteredReviewMode, userMessage, commandExecution, agentMessage, exitedReviewMode (the review field is the full text), then another agentMessage with the same text.
conflicts.claude: Has /code-review (alias /review), /security-review and /ultrareview. Measured on 2.1.295: '/code-review low' ran non-interactively in a temporary git repo, goes through a background task (task_started, then task_notification), and the result arrives via task_notification and the final result. Sage's startReview does not distinguish harnesses and only produces an error toast. Basic tier: Qwen has /review, and opencode may have /review among the commands pushed over ACP.
conflicts.decision: review is a semantic, with five unified targets: uncommitted changes, compare against a branch, a commit, custom instructions, Pull request. Codex uses rpc review/start (nativeOf, delivery fixed to 'inline', ignoring prefs.reviewDelivery), with PRs done as custom plus the PR diff; the result card is rendered from exitedReviewMode.review, and the same-text agentMessage that follows is dropped. Claude uses passthrough '/code-review <target>' (for a PR, '/code-review <PR url>'); the menu reads aliases from supportedCommands, and variants appear only if they are in the command catalog; the result is taken from task_notification and result and rendered as Markdown inside the same review result card frame, without parsing; this review is a background task, so Stop and the reaper handle it under the task rules. Basic tier: if the command catalog has a review command it is passed through (Qwen /review, opencode's /review), otherwise none(harness). The harness dropdown on the Code Review page lists only first-class harnesses and basic-tier harnesses that declare a review command, defaulting to the default harness for new chats. The Review delivery setting is removed (fixed to inline).
conflicts.ui: The Code review submenu has the same structure on both first-class harnesses, with variants carrying a source badge, and ultra noting "Runs in the cloud and is billed". Codex's structured result is split into individual findings; Claude's result is Markdown inside the card frame. The button on the Review page reads "Review in a new chat".

conflicts.conflict: Which file /init generates; instruction files and memory
conflicts.codex: Sage sends a prompt that generates AGENTS.md without checking whether the file already exists. There is a $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md editor and features.memories.
conflicts.claude: The native /init is intercepted and what gets generated is AGENTS.md (#14); the CLAUDE.md editor hard-codes ~/.claude and saves through Codex fs/writeFile. Measured on 2.1.295: '/init' generates CLAUDE.md non-interactively (6 turns). sharedRoot in harness/claude/accounts.cjs:29 is a module-internal function, and line 243 exports only { ClaudeAccounts, CLAUDE_DEFAULT_ID }. Basic tier: Kimi and opencode push /init; dsh reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md and has no init.
conflicts.decision: init is a semantic. Claude passes /init through; Codex uses the init polyfill to write AGENTS.md (instructionsFiles[0]), asking first if it already exists; basic-tier harnesses pass init through if they have an init command (Kimi, opencode), otherwise none(harness), with no polyfill. Two files in the same repo will gradually drift apart: when running /init on Claude and AGENTS.md already exists, the first option is "AGENTS.md exists · Let Claude Code read it instead (recommended)" (written to the user-level settings.json, with a preview before writing); when running /init on Codex and CLAUDE.md already exists, symmetrically offer "let Codex read CLAUDE.md too" (project_doc_fallback_filenames). The Instructions page shows which files each harness actually loads for this project; export sharedRoot() from harness/claude/accounts.cjs, use it for the CLAUDE.md path, and read and write through main's fs. Memory is built as an ext panel for each first-class harness.
conflicts.ui: The description for Init reads "Create {file} for {label}", with "by MoPilot" added for Codex. Settings → {harness} → Instructions & memory uses the same page template.

conflicts.conflict: Multi-agent: Ultra, ultracode and sub-agents
conflicts.codex: effort 'ultra' is filtered out by select.ts:43 (#15); child threads are filtered out of the sidebar, and the UI shows only a single 'Spawned agent' line (#18). Measured on 0.162: ultra appears only in supportedReasoningEfforts of gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-daybreak-blue-latest, and not in the luna series; these models report multiAgentVersion v2; ThreadStartParams/TurnStartParams.multiAgentMode is deprecated in favour of effort 'ultra'.
conflicts.claude: The ultracode keyword is recognised only in messages with origin {kind:'human'}, and Sage does not send one (#6; measured on 2.1.295: without origin no workflow_keyword_request is produced). When changing effort, only {effortLevel, fastMode} is sent, which was measured to silently turn ultracode off; applyFlagSettings({ultracode:true}) works, and availability is in q.getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable (present at runtime but not declared in sdk.d.ts), with no stream event announcing changes; a Workflow is shown as a single line, and task_* and sub-agent messages are dropped (claudeTranslate.ts:269, 288). Basic tier: Kimi has a swarm configOption and /swarm, Copilot has /fleet.
conflicts.decision: multiAgent is a single ConfigOption (_sage.multi_agent) and appears only when the harness has a session-level switch: Codex effort=ultra (appears only if the current model declares ultra, mutually exclusive with the other tiers, locks the slider when on and restores it when off); Claude ultracode=true (orthogonal to effort; every later applyFlagSettings that changes effort or fast carries the current ultracode value; availability follows getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable, which is a version-probe item, and if the probe fails only this switch is greyed out). Basic tier: show the switch when a matching configOption exists (Kimi's swarm), and pass /swarm and /fleet through; sub-agent tool_calls render as a generic Agent card, and Stop can only do a whole-session session/cancel. Messages typed by the user carry origin human, and those synthesised by Sage do not. Claude turns on includeHookEvents and agentProgressSummaries. Multi-agent is not migrated by default when switching harness.
conflicts.ui: A switch under the effort popover, with the label using the original name (Codex says Ultra, Claude says ultracode) and the subtitle "Multiple agents · Uses noticeably more tokens". The Agent card and Workflow card show the phase, the number of subtasks and a stop button; Codex child threads open in a read-only sidebar.

conflicts.conflict: / commands and the skills catalog
conflicts.codex: The app-server has no RPC for listing commands, and skills come from skills/list. Sage has two hard-coded tables (SLASH_COMMANDS and useSlashItems), so typing and the menu come from different sources, and /usage, /plan and /status are intercepted by the popover (#20).
conflicts.claude: supportedCommands(), the slash_commands and skills in init, and commands_changed are all unread; Claude threads list Codex skills, which are rewritten to '/<codex name>' once selected (claude.ts:472-486, #5). Measured on 2.1.295: supportedCommands() equals initializationResult().commands, 69 entries, with only the fields name, description, argumentHint, aliases, builtin; /review is merely an alias of code-review; skills are not commands, but they appear in the list in the form of commands and also in init.skills; terminal_slash_commands appears only in system/init ([doctor, color, focus, reload-plugins]) and not in initializationResult(). extras(bin) has no cwd parameter and uses the account's cleanEnv() (harness/claude/index.cjs:593). Basic tier: Kimi and Qwen push via available_commands_update; dsh pushes no commands.
conflicts.decision: One CommandRegistry: Sage UI commands plus the current segment's CommandProvider, of which there are only three kinds: Codex's static table plus feature gating; Claude's supportedCommands and commands_changed; and the basic tier's available_commands_update. Claude: the menu reads aliases; when the home page has no session yet, extras gains cwd and account parameters and prefetches initializationResult().commands, terminal commands are first filtered against the static list, and once system/init from a live session arrives they are corrected by terminal_slash_commands; cache by (instance, cwd), and replace the whole set when commands_changed arrives. Skills: Codex sends a structured skill item; Claude inserts '/name '; the basic tier lists only the skill commands the harness pushes (Kimi '/skill:<name>'), and those not pushed are loaded by the model itself and not listed by Sage. The popover matches by command-name prefix; when a name is exactly the same as a native command, passthrough takes priority.
conflicts.ui: The / menu is grouped as App, {label} commands, Skills, Workflows (the former "Sage" group is renamed App). Source badges and argument hints are shown only in the menu and on hover. The Skills page is split into tabs per first-class harness and lists the source directories.

conflicts.conflict: Sage's sessions deviate from the harness's default behaviour
conflicts.codex: The app-server uses the built-in base instructions automatically, so there is no problem.
conflicts.claude: startSession does not pass systemPrompt, and SDK 0.3.295 sends an empty string (harness/claude/index.cjs:391-405, #7); scrubProcessEnv deletes the user's ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_CODE_*, and when launched from the Dock the shell environment is not inherited either (#35). By default dsh attaches a session-log upload of up to 8 MiB to every request body, and OTel telemetry carries an anonymous id; dsh ships a new version every 2-6 days, each with breaking changes, and as soon as a line id (session-log-deepseek) or the --patch format in the patch changes, the patch silently stops working.
conflicts.decision: Write it into the adapter contract: reproduce the harness's default behaviour in its own CLI, and Sage only appends or merges. Claude passes {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append, snapshot:true}; at launch, before scrubProcessEnv, save an env snapshot of the login shell, and both places share a narrowed list (clear only authentication and parent-session identity), with feature variables restored from the snapshot and Provider variables written last. A basic-tier harness's quirks must declare privacyDefaults, and without it the harness does not enter the picker. dsh: --patch sage.patch.yml only turns off session-log-deepseek and changes the model on the acp line to deepseek-flash, with env adding DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, written into acp/quirks/dsh.cjs; before launch, run dsh --profile acp --patch sage.patch.yml --dump-config with the same arguments, parse the result, and confirm session-log-deepseek is disabled and telemetry is off; if it cannot be parsed or is not off, refuse to launch (fail-closed). DSH_HOME is no longer isolated and customSkillDirs is not added. All of this is written as conformance checks, and dsh's acceptance requires packet capture.
conflicts.ui: No new controls. Settings → {harness} → Advanced says "Uses {label}'s default instructions (plus MoPilot's additions)" and lists the config items MoPilot changed and why; when dsh validation fails, the Other harnesses page shows "This dsh version can't turn off session log upload".

conflicts.conflict: Passthrough format, message origin and attachments break native commands
conflicts.codex: Input is structured items. The app-server does not parse slash text, and '/xxx' is silently handed to the model as ordinary text.
conflicts.claude: Measured on 2.1.295: a / command is recognised only when it is the last content block; placed in the first or a middle block, the whole message is handed to the model as ordinary text and the goal is not set (the root cause of #19); Sage puts images after the text (claude.ts:472-486), so with an image attached the / commands, @file, ultrathink and ultracode all stop working; skill attachment rewriting, the handoff prefix and the selection template all break commands; heic and bmp are rejected by the API (#58); an intercepted command does not clear the attachments (#53). User messages pushed by send() carry neither a uuid nor an origin. An unknown command, with or without origin, goes through unknown_command_fallback to the model and does not report "Unknown command". The basic tier uses ACP content blocks (text, image, resource_link).
conflicts.decision: adapter.send takes a typed SageInputPart[], an origin and a uuid, and the adapter serialises them. Claude: block order is handoff, images, user text, and text starting with / is always the last block; only messages typed by the user carry origin human, and messages synthesised by Sage do not; every user message writes SDKUserMessage.uuid (corresponding to Sage's clientId; fork and rewind use it for positioning, and the CLI does not echo it in the stream); remove the Codex skill rewriting and the handoff concatenation (on 2.1.295 adding origin does not make unknown commands error, so the two have no ordering requirement and are just cleanups in the same work package). Codex: structured skill and mention, with the handoff in the first text item. ACP: content blocks, handoff in the first block, files as resource_link. Image formats are declared by Negotiated.prompt.image; unsupported formats are converted to PNG at the attachment stage, and if conversion is impossible the attachment is rejected with an explanation. An intercepted command either takes its attachments with it or clears them.
conflicts.ui: No new controls. Sending /code-review with an image attached also works. Typing an unknown command in a Codex thread lists the available commands below and offers "Send as plain text".

conflicts.conflict: Permission tiers share names but mean different things
conflicts.codex: approvalPolicy and sandbox are sent with every turn/start, derived from the global prefs.permission; read-only is a read-only sandbox and can still request privilege escalation. The Approval policy and Sandbox from config.toml in Settings are overridden in Sage chats (#30).
conflicts.claude: There is no OS sandbox. read-only is dontAsk plus a read-only allowlist, and Bash is silently refused; the Composer shows read-only as Ask for approval (#27); Approve for me does not check supportsAutoMode (#67); switching to Full access mid-session lacks allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, which can only be set at launch (#28). The basic tier's modes all differ (Qwen's approval-mode has plan, default, auto-edit, auto, yolo; Copilot has standard, plan, autopilot); dsh has no modes, and permissions are decided by DSH_PERMISSION_MODE at launch.
conflicts.decision: Store two things per chat: a semantic anchor (read-only, ask, auto, full) and the current segment's native tier. The adapter publishes a list of native tiers, each tagged with one anchor. Claude always passes allowDangerouslySkipPermissions at launch, and Sage guarantees that setPermissionMode('bypassPermissions') is called only when the user picks full access; auto appears only when the model has supportsAutoMode. Basic tier: show only the harness's own modes (original names), with quirks optionally tagging anchors; harnesses without modes (such as dsh) have permissions decided by the launch default (dsh is workspace-write plus ask), which cannot be changed within a session, and the menu shows only a single line "Set by {label}". When switching harness, permissions can only stay the same or get stricter. Default permissions in Settings is the default anchor for new chats on every harness; toggling in the Composer changes only this chat. Two items of config.toml on the Codex page are labelled "Only affects Codex outside MoPilot".
conflicts.ui: The permissions menu is titled "What {label} can do", the button shows the anchor name, keeping Codex's look and shortcuts; the second line of each row gives the native name and a one-sentence difference, such as "No sandbox" or "Writes and Bash are refused"; the bottom of the menu says "This chat only". The read-only item is added. The Full access banner text is interpolated per harness.

conflicts.conflict: Approval types differ across harnesses, and the copy hard-codes Codex
conflicts.codex: commandExecution (including network context and Allow similar), fileChange, permissions, requestUserInput (supports isSecret), mcpServer elicitation; unknown requests are hard-coded as 'Codex sent an unsupported request'.
conflicts.claude: Commands, files, questions (multiSelect not supported), toolApproval, ExitPlanMode; onElicitation is not passed, so the SDK rejects automatically; a rejection always replies with the fixed 'The user declined this action.'; card labels are decided by chat id (#40). Measured on 2.1.295: under the default tier canUseTool fires for SDK MCP tools (that is, Sage's tools). The basic tier has only session/request_permission, with options decided by the harness (some have allow_always, dsh has only allow-once and reject-once).
conflicts.decision: ApprovalRequest adopts the ACP shape, with options carrying a kind; cards render by ApprovalKind, and the label takes the harness of the originating segment. Claude gains onElicitation, multiSelect and rejection reasons. Basic-tier approvals render the options of request_permission as they are (show allow_always if there is one). Sage's own tools do not go through the harness's generic tool approval: Claude's canUseTool auto-allows mcp__sage_<nonce>__*, Codex thread config sets default_tools_approval_mode="approve", and for the basic tier request_permission auto-allows once for tools named sage_<nonce>; only this per-session random name is recognised, to avoid asking twice for the same action and to avoid letting through a same-named sage server in the user's repo. Approval cards accept only human-initiated input (judged by the event's originating process, with system assistive technology allowed), with a keyboard alternative: hold ⌘↩ for one second to confirm. Approval notifications go through notify('approval').
conflicts.ui: Card title "{label} wants to run a command", 1/2/3 number shortcuts, and on rejection you can attach a line such as "Try something else".

conflicts.conflict: Background tasks and Esc mean different things
conflicts.codex: Has thread/backgroundTerminals/list|terminate|clean (an experimental interface, measured working on 0.162, with the osPid and cpu fields possibly null), which Sage does not list. Esc only sends turn/interrupt (store.ts:1489), and an active goal resumes automatically; set paused alone also fails to stop a running turn.
conflicts.claude: perTaskStopAffordance is not declared: measured on 2.1.295, interrupt() stops background subagents (local_agent), and once it is declared they survive; background shells survive in both cases; close() kills all tasks. The reaper kills quietly waiting loops and Monitors after 10 minutes (#17). After interrupt() the /goal is still active and the next message resumes the old goal. The basic tier has only session/cancel; dsh may keep working autonomously even when no prompt is in progress.
conflicts.decision: Stop is unified into one semantic: stop the current turn and pause the goal. Codex: when the goal is active, set paused first, then turn/interrupt (500ms timeout). Claude: interrupt(), and when the goal is active also send '/goal clear' and store the condition in meta.goalHeld (a pause held by Sage). Basic tier: Stop = session/cancel; if tool_call-type session/update messages are still received afterwards with no prompt in progress, send session/cancel again and treat subsequent tool calls as unattended. A computer use action that is executing is aborted immediately and the desktop lock released. Claude declares perTaskStopAffordance:true, shipped in the same release as the task panel and q.stopTask; the task table uses background_tasks_changed as the level signal and task_* as the edge; the reaper skips when there are tasks, loops or cron jobs. Codex lists background terminals and can terminate them. The basic tier's task panel is absent. Pressing Esc a second time within 2 seconds pops up "Stop all background tasks (3)?", confirmed with Enter.
conflicts.ui: The Stop tooltip reads "Stop this turn and pause the goal · Background tasks keep running (press Esc again to stop all)". An entry point for stopping background tasks can always be found in the status bar or the task panel; the task panel is a single component shared by both first-class harnesses.

conflicts.conflict: Scope of model, effort and speed tier, per-turn override, and Fast gating
conflicts.codex: All three are global prefs, so changing one chat affects every Codex chat (#29); fast is hard-coded to true (select.ts:45), without reading serviceTiers or looking at the account type (#57); turn/start.effort stays in effect for all later turns. Measured on 0.162: apart from daybreak, each model has only one serviceTier {id:'priority', name:'Fast'}, defaultServiceTier is null, and thread/start accepts serviceTier:'default'; the CLI version appears only in initialize's userAgent.
conflicts.claude: model and effort are per chat, fast is written into the global claudeSelection; fast_mode_disabled_reason is in initialize and result, and is sdk_opt_in_required when settings.fastMode is not passed; Sage looks at the account in use. Under MoPilot the CLI reports the gateway as firstParty, so fast is not blocked (#76). Changing effort without ultracode turns ultracode off. The basic tier's model and effort come from configOptions.
conflicts.decision: All harnesses save per chat, with each first-class instance also storing a default for new chats (scope rules in axes[3]). Options come from the adapter: Codex reads efforts from model/list (ultra per model), serviceTiers and inputModalities; Claude reads ModelInfo, with the "auto" tier using applyFlagSettings({effortLevel:null, ultracode}) and carrying ultracode every time. Codex sends effort explicitly every turn, resolving defaultReasoningEffort when prefs is empty. The speed tier on Codex is a binary choice: priority (Fast) or default. Per-turn deepening: Codex sets high for this turn and explicitly sets it back on the next; Claude uses the ultrathink keyword. The basic tier's model and effort come from configOptions and take effect on the next turn per ACP, and per-turn deepening is none(harness). Fast availability is the intersection of model, Provider and the chat's account: third-party endpoints and MoPilot (when the gateway capability table gives no Fast pricing) are always greyed out at the provider layer, and the CLI's firstParty report is not trusted.
conflicts.ui: A line at the bottom of the picker: "This chat only · Make default for new chats"; when there is only one Provider, the provider level is not shown. When ⚡ is unavailable, it says which layer is blocking it, and gives a fix action where there is one (for example "Use your Claude subscription").

conflicts.conflict: Session history, resume and list come from different sources
conflicts.codex: thread/list, thread/read, thread/resume. After #17, threads idle for 5 seconds are thread/unsubscribed, on-screen ones follow the disk, and threads with background terminals, a server-side queue or an active goal keep a lease (store.ts:744-752). Measured on 0.162: thread/search (an experimental interface) lags behind writes: a thread just renamed or just finished cannot be found, and another process finds it a little later; thread/list {searchTerm} is visible immediately.
conflicts.claude: listSessions(limit:200) plus jsonl, resumed by sessionId; anything beyond 200 entries is invisible (#38). Basic tier: those with loadSession can use session/load; dsh has no session/load, and session/resume does not replay old updates. The same native session may be written at the same time by the official Codex desktop app, codex resume in a terminal or claude --resume, and #17 is already watching the rollout file.
conflicts.decision: adapter.history() is implemented by each: Codex thread/read; Claude reads jsonl; basic-tier harnesses with loadSession use session/load, and those without declare history:'sage', and main writes SageItems into threads/<id>.items.jsonl, replays them on reopen, then continues with session/resume. The sidebar merges each adapter's list, and the Claude list loads in pages; the sidebar lists only basic-tier chats created inside MoPilot (session/list is not used). External-write reconciliation: when the rollout or jsonl changes, adapter.reconcile() re-reads thread/read, thread/goal/get, thread/settings or the jsonl; when an externally running turn is detected, the Composer is greyed out with the text "This chat is running in another app", and a new turn is not started on a thread someone else is running.
conflicts.ui: The sidebar mixes them, with a small harness icon on each row; the info panel of a basic-tier chat without loadSession says "History is kept by MoPilot".

conflicts.conflict: The Codex app-server is the app's hidden infrastructure
conflicts.codex: Codex depends on the app-server anyway, and that is fine; the problem is that it is started unconditionally at launch, with no start/stop switch.
conflicts.claude: The main view renders only when conn==='ready' and not requiresAuth (App.tsx:108-110); the terminal (including claude auth login), CLAUDE.md saving, projectless directory creation, projects, file search, ⌘K, scheduled tasks and environment files all go through Codex RPC; when connect() fails, deep-link resolution in a new window cannot proceed; clicking Sign in in Settings does nothing (#42), the first-login page has only Codex login (Login.tsx "Welcome to Codex", #41), and once the Codex login expires the default harness is permanently changed to Claude (#66). Users with only a basic-tier harness installed cannot get in either. A new user with neither Codex nor Claude installed and registered only with MoPilot has no way forward: a MoPilot account does not come with a harness, and there is no CLI installer anywhere under electron/.
conflicts.decision: All platform services move into electron/platform/* (WP2), and the app-server is started on demand and serves only Codex chats and Codex-specific features. The App gate changes to "at least one harness is available", and a missing Codex affects only Codex entry points. The default harness falls back only for the current run and is not written back to prefs. Settings embeds a login terminal, and detection reruns automatically after the process exits. The welcome page has three steps (WP3): 1) choose how to pay (MoPilot credits / my Claude subscription / my ChatGPT account / API key); 2) recommend a harness based on the choice and install it in one click: show the official install command in the embedded terminal first, then run it, and Re-check automatically when done (for Codex the app-server is started automatically after install); when only MoPilot is used, "Claude Code · MoPilot" is recommended by default and no claude.ai login is needed; when MoPilot is chosen and only Codex is present, set provider=mopilot for the Codex instance and suppress the ChatGPT login prompt; 3) choose the default harness, which is no longer changed automatically afterwards. Detected basic-tier harnesses are listed last, with a Basic badge.
conflicts.ui: The full-screen "Couldn't connect to Codex" is no longer shown; it becomes a Codex status card and a banner in Codex threads, with install guidance. The first welcome step reads "How do you want to pay for AI?", and the install step reads "MoPilot will run this official install command in the terminal below: {cmd} [Install] [I'll do it myself]".

conflicts.conflict: "Shared tools" in practice only apply to Codex; each harness configures extensions differently
conflicts.codex: Plugins, Apps, MCP, Skills and Hooks are all written to config.toml through the app-server. The MCP editor replaces the whole table on save, dropping hand-written keys, and user-configured HTTP servers have no Authenticate (#45).
conflicts.claude: startSession does not pass mcpServers, plugins or hooks and relies only on settingSources; changes in Shared tools have no effect on Claude (#31); a Codex plugin mention arriving at Claude becomes '@plugin://' plain text (#22); the .claude.json of a non-default account is a one-way copy, so MCP written by the CLI is lost (#44). Rail → Plugins is a global entry point yet its contents are entirely the Codex plugin marketplace; Claude's MCP has no add entry; the Hooks page is in the Codex group, and Claude's hooks cannot be seen. Measured on 2.1.295: mcpServerStatus() and toggleMcpServer() work. The basic tier's MCP is decided by the harness's own configuration.
conflicts.decision: "Built-in tools" holds only things Sage implements and injects into all harnesses: Computer use, Browser, Voice & dictation. SSH moves to Connections. Extensions are offered only for the two first-class harnesses: Codex is editable (saved with merge, and user servers also get OAuth); Claude uses the same MCP form, and on save runs 'claude mcp add --scope user …' (previewing the command before execution, and executing under the shared config), with toggleMcpServer to enable and disable within a session; Claude plugins are listed read-only from init.plugins, offering "Install with claude plugin…", with the command prefilled in the embedded terminal; Claude's hooks are listed read-only from the hooks in settings.json, offering Open settings.json. The tops of the Plugins and Customize pages are tabbed per first-class harness, defaulting to the current default harness. The basic tier has no Extensions page, only an Overview for each in the Other harnesses page (path, version, compatibility, admission result, login, data-destination notes). The + menu lists only the current harness's plugins. Revised (plugins across harnesses): plugins are installed once, in MoPilot's own store (~/.mopilot/plugins, marketplaces in Claude Code's or Codex's layout), and delivered to every harness in its own form: Claude Code loads each plugin folder through the Agent SDK's per-session plugins option; Codex installs them from MoPilot's own local marketplaces (mopilot-<marketplace>) with plugin/install and switches them per thread; the basic tier gets their MCP servers in session/new mcpServers and their skills and commands from MoPilot (the / menu and the plugin_skills tools). A plugin a harness already turns on itself is left to it. Install shows what the plugin will run (MCP commands and URLs, hook commands) and is refused if that changed since. The Plugins page and the + menu become one harness-neutral list; each harness's Extensions page keeps its native MCP and hooks.
conflicts.ui: The Settings sidebar is renamed following layers[0]'s information architecture, and Applies to is shown only when it is not "all harnesses". Import moves to the Codex page and is renamed "Import to Codex" (#36). Old links are kept with SECTION_ALIAS.

conflicts.conflict: The account pool and account-switching mechanisms are asymmetric, and a switch may cross Providers
conflicts.codex: When the relay hits 429/401 it switches accounts within the same request; pinning an account per chat requires the relay to be on and at least two accounts; an API-key account, once pinned, is moved away by healthy(), and a "quota exhausted" row is also inserted (#64).
conflicts.claude: Only when quota is exhausted, after the turn ends the process is closed and resumed, and a visible 'Continue where you left off.' is sent; whether the session-level /goal Stop hook and permissionMode are still present after resume is undefined; an expired login does not switch accounts, and the re-login button only re-logs-in the account in use (#43); the usage bar and background calls use the account in use (#65); the switch note exists only in memory. The accounts share ~/.claude/projects via symlinks, and subscriptions and API keys of the same Provider are in one pool, so when quota runs out it may automatically switch to a pay-per-use key.
conflicts.decision: Codex and Claude each get an AccountDriver that declares failover, poolPolicy and perChat. The contract is fixed: automatic switching and the "This chat" account choice stay within the same ProviderProfile and the same billing method; switching from a subscription to pay-per-use (even an API key of the same Provider) always pops a confirmation; switching Provider always goes through SwitchSheet, with a new segment plus handoff and no resume. When a Claude login expires, it also switches accounts within the same Provider and the same billing method and leaves a note; the switch note is written into segments; the usage bar reads the chat's account; when there is no reading it shows "unknown"; background calls use the chat's account; temporary chats pin their account; the continue message is synthesised by Sage, carries no origin, and is shown as a note. After an account switch (restartResume) or opening a new segment on a different Provider within the same harness, the adapter reapplies the goal and plan mode from SessionState to the new session: Claude calls setPermissionMode first, and when the goal is active re-sends '/goal <condition>' (the condition comes from the 'Goal set:' text Sage recorded, and this turn is treated as unattended), and inserts a note. When a Codex API-key account is pinned to a chat it goes straight through and is no longer moved away; the switch note states the real reason. For the basic tier failover is none, and when quota runs out only a banner is shown.
conflicts.ui: The account list lives only in Accounts & billing, grouped by Provider; the "This chat" account choice uses the same control for both first-class harnesses and lists only accounts of the same Provider and the same billing method; choosing another harness's account in an existing chat is always treated as a switch (opens SwitchSheet) and does not change the global default. The account row says "When a limit is reached: switch to another subscription / ask me before using an API key". Switch note: "Max limit reached. Continued on b@x.com · Goal and plan mode carried over". Confirmation before moving to pay-per-use: "Your subscription limit is reached. Continue with your Anthropic API key? You'll pay per use from here." The expired-login banner targets the account the chat is using and offers "Use another account".

conflicts.conflict: The MoPilot gateway is built twice, once per harness, and both are global switches
conflicts.codex: The hidden apiKey account mopilot is passed through the relay: it is counted as a multi-account, so even single-ChatGPT-account users see Share usage and per-chat account selection, and after being pinned to MoPilot it is moved away (#70); when there is no Codex login it is selected by default, and the next connection starts silently deducting credits (#71); account/login/start(apiKey) may write mpk_ into ~/.codex/auth.json (#72); after signing out of MoPilot the revoked key continues to be used (#73).
conflicts.claude: A harness-level mode plus cleanEnv injection, which applies to all Claude accounts; as soon as signedIn changes, closeAll() runs, turns are interrupted, and the keep-side chats are lost (#74); the CLI reports oauth_token, firstParty, the status card shows the cached subscription plan, and after sign-out it silently falls back (#75). The MoPilot entries on Pay with, the model picker and the Login page are incomplete (#81).
conflicts.decision: MoPilot is a ProviderProfile (wires anthropic, responses, chat; baseUrl code.mopilot.ai; the model catalog and drops come from WP0's /v1/models capability table) plus a sageKey account (the device's mpk_ key stored in the keychain). It serves only Codex and Claude Code: Claude uses a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR plus env; Codex uses thread/start.modelProvider plus the thread config's model_providers.mopilot and auth.command (executed immediately at thread/start, so the key helper must be fast and non-interactive), and no longer uses account/login/start. Account counting and routing exclude sageKey; mopilot does not take part in active() fallback or syncDefault; signing in to or out of MoPilot restarts only the sessions that are using mopilot, waits for idle, and skips keep sessions; on sign-out it explicitly writes back a subscription or switches to a remaining key, and if there is neither, it calls account/logout on the app-server and shows a prompt. detect() recognises mopilot as a billing mode.
conflicts.ui: The model picker shows "Claude Code · MoPilot · claude-sonnet-5", with the balance in the avatar menu and at the bottom of the picker. Pay with, the picker and the welcome page all have MoPilot credits; after a successful sign-in switching continues, and on failure a prompt is shown.

conflicts.conflict: Third-party endpoints and environment variables are handled asymmetrically
conflicts.codex: baseUrl only takes effect with relay passthrough; when config.toml has openai_base_url, a custom model_provider or SAGE_NO_RELAY is set, it is silently ignored (#32). Thread config is saved together with the thread settings, and a key written into it may land in the rollout in plain text. Measured on 0.162: model_providers plus modelProvider in the thread config is accepted (nested and dotted keys both work, and config.model_provider can also be used to select); an undefined provider returns -32600 "Model provider ... not found"; auth.command is executed immediately at thread/start (the same whether defined at thread level or at launch-argument level), and when the command fails it logs "Failed to resolve external auth".
conflicts.claude: Injecting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and AUTH_TOKEN works, but the picker still shows Claude aliases, and the effort tiers and compaction window are not adjusted per endpoint; the gateway and feature flags in the user's shell are deleted (#35); env, model and apiKeyHelper in the shared settings.json may override injected variables and send a key that can spend money elsewhere; under a non-first-party base URL the fast mode check and the WebFetch domain check still request api.anthropic.com.
conflicts.decision: ProviderProfile is injected per wire and overrides only first-class harnesses. Claude uses the full set of env (DEFAULT_*_MODEL, SUBAGENT_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW), one separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per sageKey account, without a claude.ai login, with settings.json copied and env, model and apiKeyHelper stripped out. Codex's custom endpoints use the thread config's model_providers.<id> plus modelProvider, with no secret in the definition, and credentials only via auth.command (Sage's signed helper reads the cache from the keychain, returns within 200ms, and on failure exits non-zero immediately without any interactive prompt); the relay serves only the ChatGPT account pool. No fallback needing app-server launch arguments is required, and there is no need to restart the app-server because a definition changed. When something cannot be applied it is greyed out with the reason, instead of being silently ignored. "Use the Claude config from my shell" is a Provider that reads '$SHELL -ilc env -0' (5-second timeout). The settings page states that under third-party endpoints requests still go to api.anthropic.com.
conflicts.ui: The picker shows "harness · provider · model" and the real model id; items the endpoint does not support are greyed out with the reason.

conflicts.conflict: Billing methods and API key management
conflicts.codex: An API key is a row in the account pool; Replace key actually adds a new row, and Remove deletes the first apiKey account (#33).
conflicts.claude: An API key is a harness-level mode; setApiKey and setAuthMode call closeAll(), which interrupts all turns, and take effect on all Claude accounts (#34); an account record with only a key cannot be stored; "When a limit is reached" is displayed once on each of the two harness pages.
conflicts.decision: For first-class harnesses, API keys, MoPilot and DeepSeek keys are all nameable account rows under some Provider and can be chosen per chat; Add API key lives only in Accounts & billing → {Provider}, and the harness pages carry only a link. Changing billing affects only later new sessions or the next turn, and does not call closeAll. Replace updates the row in use in place, Remove deletes the row in use, and if none is in use the user is asked to choose. "When a limit is reached" is set once in each Provider group. Existing billing methods are never changed by an upgrade.
conflicts.ui: In the account list, subscriptions, API keys, MoPilot and third-party endpoints are grouped by Provider, each with a badge. The tooltip of the API chip points to Accounts & billing.

conflicts.conflict: Usage windows differ in source and precision
conflicts.codex: Structured rateLimits, updated live from the x-codex-* headers on every response; Credits and reset tickets apply only to the account in use.
conflicts.claude: rate_limit_event updates only the current session's account; for other accounts /usage is parsed every 10 minutes; under MoPilot the cached subscription window is still shown. Most basic-tier harnesses have only usage_update{used,size}, and some have none.
conflicts.decision: The adapter outputs a unified UsageSnapshot{windows, source: live | polled | parsed | none, at}. Codex's Credits and reset tickets and Claude's extra usage are each an ext section. API key, MoPilot and DeepSeek show no quota window: MoPilot shows the balance, and the others give a link to spend or balance. Basic-tier usage shows only the context occupancy from usage_update, and shows nothing if there is none.
conflicts.ui: The reading time is shown next to the usage bar ("8 minutes ago"), and parsed values are labelled "estimate".

conflicts.conflict: Voice chat and dictation depend on Codex
conflicts.codex: Voice chat goes through thread/realtime/*, with the voice hard-coded. Dictation goes through chatgpt.com/backend-api/transcribe, using the token of the Codex account in use.
conflicts.claude: There is no realtime voice. The button is disabled, yet the global hotkey still calls Codex realtime for claude: threads, and the home page first creates an empty Claude chat (#23). Users logged in only to Claude, or on the basic tier, cannot dictate.
conflicts.decision: Speech input stays in the current chat. Shared dictation is editable text; explicitly negotiated audio messages start tasks only on Send; native realtime remains capability-specific. VOICE.md owns provider prerequisites, capture lifetime, delivery recovery and reference retention.
conflicts.ui: The Voice entry offers explicit available dictation services, audio messages and native conversation. Unsupported native operations explain why without creating another harness chat.

conflicts.conflict: Codex Cloud exists on only one side
conflicts.codex: codex cloud exec/list/apply, with credentials being the default account in $CODEX_HOME/auth.json, not following the account Sage selected; API-key accounts cannot use it.
conflicts.claude: No corresponding integration; Claude's cloud sessions and /schedule require a claude.ai login. Work in renders only when prefs.harness==='codex'. The basic tier has no cloud execution.
conflicts.decision: Cloud is the ext cloudTasks of (Codex, ChatGPT account), with no polyfill. In a new chat, Cloud is shown only when Codex is installed and logged in with ChatGPT, and choosing it only makes this new chat use Codex. It is hidden in existing non-Codex chats. Cloud calls switch to the credentials of the account selected for the chat. Claude's own cloud commands are passed through via the command catalog.
conflicts.ui: The Cloud row in Work in carries a Codex badge; once selected, the chip slot shows "This new chat uses Codex Cloud (ChatGPT · a@b.com) · Undo"; the first time each user crosses vendors, a confirmation dialog is used instead.

conflicts.conflict: Temporary chats are silently written to disk on some harnesses
conflicts.codex: thread/start passes ephemeral and nothing is written to disk; an ephemeral thread does not support goal.
conflicts.claude: The Claude branch does not read this flag, and the session is written to ~/.claude as usual and appears in the sidebar (#9). Measured on 2.1.295: a session with persistSession:false writes no jsonl, is not in listSessions, getSessionInfo returns undefined, and it cannot be resumed after the process ends, so when switching accounts the process cannot be closed and then resumed. ACP has no unified non-persisting session.
conflicts.decision: temporary is a semantic, and Negotiated.session.ephemeral declares native or none. Codex ephemeral (such a thread does not support goal, -32600); Claude persistSession:false, with the session kept alive, not in the list, no title generated, pinned to the account at creation time, and not taking part in account switching; all basic-tier harnesses are none(harness), and ⇧⌘N is routed to Claude Code or Codex per the global-entry rule (the chip states the account). Goal is greyed out in temporary chats.
conflicts.ui: The Temporary marker is shown only when nothing is really written to disk; all harnesses use the same "won't be saved" banner.

conflicts.conflict: Archive and search are asymmetric
conflicts.codex: thread/archive lives on the server; after typing a keyword in ⌘K the results are wholly replaced by thread/list(searchTerm); the protocol has an unused thread/search.
conflicts.claude: Archiving is only claudeArchived in ui-state.json, subject to the listSessions(200) limit, and invisible when not logged in (#38); ⌘K cannot find Claude chats (#25); multiple windows overwrite each other (#39). No basic-tier harness has archiving.
conflicts.decision: Archive, pin, unread and project membership are Sage's chat metadata, stored in threads/<id>.v2.json; harnesses with native archiving (Codex) are mirrored as well. ⌘K merges Codex thread/search and thread/list(searchTerm) (thread/search lags behind writes, so the latest threads rely on the latter), main's scan of Claude jsonl, Sage's own saved transcripts and the title index of basic-tier chats, mixed and de-duplicated. The archive list is completed by id and is not limited to the latest 200. When migration fails, the banner reads "Couldn't move archived chats · Restored from backup · Retry".
conflicts.ui: ⌘K results are mixed, each with a small harness icon; the archive page behaves the same for all harnesses, grouped by project.

conflicts.conflict: Scheduled tasks are tied to Codex
conflicts.codex: Tasks are stored in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (src/lib/automations.ts:1, 48-51) and read and written through the app-server; every new run does startThread; the scheduler requires conn to be ready; Run now does not carry the task's model and effort (#37).
conflicts.claude: Only tasks that point to an existing Claude chat can run, and model and effort are ignored; /loop and Monitor get killed by the 10-minute reaper; /schedule is a cloud routine on claude.ai, requires a claude.ai login, and has nothing to do with Sage's Scheduled page. The basic tier's scheduling capability is not exposed through ACP.
conflicts.decision: Scheduled tasks can choose only Codex or Claude Code (Run with ▾ lists only these two), and the basic tier is notProvided. Tasks are stored in userData/automations, recording harness, instance, model, effort, cwd, whether computer control is allowed (off by default) and the allowed apps, and what to do when approval is needed (default Wait and notify, with Skip this run as an option; if not handled within 1 hour, mark this run as needs attention); the Sage scheduler and Run now share one execution function and run through adapter.start/send, so the scheduler goes in WP7 (it needs WP5's adapter). Sharing with the official Codex app is an optional dual write. The reaper does not close sessions that have cron jobs, loops or background tasks. Claude's /loop and /schedule are passed through via the command catalog, and the menu description of /schedule reads "Cloud routine on claude.ai (not in MoPilot Scheduled)". Trigger messages carry no origin.
conflicts.ui: When creating a task, choose "Run with ▾", and the model list comes from the selected harness and Provider; in the dialog, "Allow computer control" and the app list are off by default; the subtitle of the Scheduled page reads "Runs on this Mac"; the empty-state copy is changed to neutral wording.

conflicts.conflict: Feedback, Status, the MCP submenu and Logout use Codex interfaces
conflicts.codex: feedback/upload attaches logs; account/logout; Status reads prefs.model and rateLimits.
conflicts.claude: /feedback and /logout exist only in the TUI (2.1.295's supportedCommands has no feedback). Feedback sends the claude: session id together with the Codex logs to OpenAI, and the thumbs-up is judged by chat id (Dialogs.tsx:85, #8); the Status and MCP submenus show Codex data (#21); /logout and the menu's Log Out delete the Codex account in use, and when it is the last account delete $CODEX_HOME/auth.json (#26). The basic tier's feedback channels are all in their own TUI or web client.
conflicts.decision: feedback is Codex's ext feedbackUpload, appears only in Codex segments, and uses nativeOf; segments of other harnesses hide it, and nothing is ever uploaded across vendors. Claude replies keep the thumbs-up, with data going only to MoPilot's own telemetry (when the user has consented) and never sent to OpenAI. Status reads the current segment's SessionState (Claude uses getContextUsage, the basic tier uses usage_update). The MCP submenu fetches data per segment. /logout and the menu's Log Out open the account row in Accounts & billing that the chat uses, for the user to confirm, and do not delete directly; the basic tier offers it only if auth.logout is declared.
conflicts.ui: Status uses a single template and shows the harness, Provider, model, account, context and usage actually used by the current segment.

conflicts.conflict: Computer use has no usable native implementation on any harness
conflicts.codex: The ChatGPT app ships unified-computer-use (cua_repl plus Codex Computer Use.app), which requires a ChatGPT login and has regional restrictions. Measured on 0.162: every ordinary thread Sage spawns loads from ~/.codex/config.toml cua_repl (js, js_reset, turn_ended), the user's own node_repl (env pointing to the Sky CUA service and browser-use), codex_apps (302 ChatGPT connector tools, including side-effecting ones like doordash_checkout), dataAnalyticsWidgets, and the model's own create_goal, get_goal and update_goal. Per-thread config {plugins:{"unified-computer-use@openai-bundled":{enabled:false}}} removes cua_repl; disabling only computer-use@openai-bundled, --disable computer_use, and features.computer_use=false all fail; setting mcp_servers.cua_repl.enabled=false per thread is rejected (invalid transport). All tool calls go through a mandatory code mode (the model writes JS scripts), which cannot be turned off. An image result from dynamicTools is a data-URL string inside the script, and the model cannot see the image unless it calls image(); mcp_servers in the thread config can hand the image natively to the model, but when approvalPolicy is never every call fails ("requires approval"), so default_tools_approval_mode="approve" must be set or the tool marked readOnlyHint. The namespaceTools capability flag assumed in the previous design revision does not exist.
conflicts.claude: The built-in computer-use is available only in interactive sessions, Pro/Max, with a claude.ai login; SDK sessions cannot get it, and under API key, DeepSeek or MoPilot it is even less usable. Measured on 2.1.295: an image tool from an in-process createSdkMcpServer can be read by the model, but tools are hidden behind ToolSearch by default (deferred); the handler's extra.sessionId is null, with only claudecode/toolUseId and requestId in _meta; under the default tier canUseTool fires for it, and under dontAsk plus allowedTools it does not. Basic tier: dsh's computer use is an experimental plugin that is off by default, and no other basic-tier harness has a built-in one.
conflicts.decision: Use Sage's own toolkit: a signed MoPilot Computer Use.app helper (Swift, LSUIElement, launched via LaunchServices, with a native CGEvent / AX / ScreenCaptureKit implementation; it does not embed cua-driver, decision WP8-3), plus Sage's policy, approval and logging. Three injection channels (see shared). Codex: Sage tools go through the thread config's mcp_servers.sage_<nonce> (carried by both thread/start and thread/resume), with default_tools_approval_mode="approve" and readOnlyHint added to observation tools; the same config sets plugins["unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"].enabled=false to turn off cua_repl; dynamicTools is not used. node_repl is an MCP server the user configured themselves: Sage turns it off per thread by setting mcp_servers.node_repl.enabled=false (verified by conformance X14; if it does not take effect, computer use in the Codex segment is marked "needs verification", with the helper's event tap as the backstop). codex_apps is not computer control but has side effects: turn it off per thread where possible (X14 looks for the per-thread switch); when it cannot be turned off, those calls go through Codex's own MCP approval, Sage renders them as a generic approval card, and when unattended they are never auto-approved. Should cua_repl still appear (version drift), intercept the mcpServer/elicitation/request it sends and reject it unconditionally, with a one-line explanation in the chat. Claude: one SDK MCP server per session, with tools set to alwaysLoad. Basic tier: mcpServers in session/new, and if injection does not succeed the harness is not admitted. Safety floor: the forbidden-zone table cannot be relaxed in any mode; the helper's event tap drops all synthetic events landing on MoPilot windows (not only the helper's own; system assistive technology is allowed by originating pid); approval cards, permission settings and the Full access switch accept only human-initiated input; screenshots are taken by the helper itself with SCContentFilter, excluding MoPilot windows and the glow overlay. Takeover rule: when the helper detects physical input (pointer movement beyond a threshold or any key press) it immediately pauses the current action and releases the lock, and the activity bar shows "You took over. The agent is paused · Resume"; only Esc from a HID source is honoured and synthetic events are ignored; if the system permission needed for the emergency stop is missing, control is refused and a guidance card is shown. Authorization: the card has three buttons Allow once / Allow in this chat / Always allow, plus three levels View only / Click / Full control; grants persist per chat, and Always allow writes into the global list in Settings.
conflicts.ui: On first use a guidance card appears first, explaining what the helper is, and then jumps to Accessibility and Screen Recording in System Settings. Settings → Built-in tools → Computer use shows permission status, the app lists (the chat list and the global list), the forbidden-zone table and the engine version, and notes that Screen Recording needs re-confirming about every month. Indication has three layers: the tray (always has "Stop controlling your Mac"), a glow on the target window, and the activity bar in the chat. When the desktop lock is held, the activity bar shows "Waiting: another chat is controlling your Mac · View". When cua_repl is rejected, the chat shows a line "In MoPilot, computer control is provided by MoPilot. Codex's built-in version is off."

conflicts.conflict: Computer control when unattended: nobody can click the authorization card
conflicts.codex: When a goal is active, the server resumes automatically after the thread goes idle, and the user may not be present; collab child threads also run in the background.
conflicts.claude: The /goal loop keeps working within one turn, and background Workflows, sub-agents and /loop all continue while the user is away. Basic tier: dsh's round-driver continues working when no prompt is in progress, and Kimi /goal and Copilot autopilot run for a long time within a single prompt. Sage's scheduled tasks are the same.
conflicts.decision: computer use is authorized by permission anchor: readOnly lets only observation tools through; ask and auto authorize per app, with confirmation when an irreversible category (payment, sending, deletion, permission changes and so on) is hit; full still authorizes per app, and irreversible categories still need confirmation. "Unattended" means: this turn was not triggered by a message the user just sent (goal resume, a /goal re-sent after an account switch, scheduled tasks, background tasks, sub-agents), or there has been no physical input for more than 10 minutes; the basic tier adds: any tool_call that arrives when no user prompt is in progress counts as unattended. An unattended turn may only use apps in the chat list and the global list; when new authorization is needed or an irreversible category is hit, the handler rejects this call and tells the model why, then pauses the goal (Codex set paused then interrupt; Claude interrupt then '/goal clear' with the condition recorded; basic tier session/cancel), sends one notification, and does not queue a card. Scheduled tasks do not allow computer control by default.
conflicts.ui: The notification reads "{chat} needs your OK to control {App}. Goal paused.", with only one per chat, and multiple chats within 60 seconds merged into "3 chats need you". Opening it shows the authorization card and Resume goal.

conflicts.conflict: Browser control depends on each vendor's own login
conflicts.codex: The chrome@openai-bundled extension plus a native host, depending on a ChatGPT account.
conflicts.claude: Claude in Chrome requires a claude.ai login, and the extension must be in the same organization as the CLI login; API keys, gateways (including MoPilot) and multiple accounts across organizations all make it fail; when it is on, browser authorization is not in Sage's hands, and neither the forbidden zones nor site permissions take effect. The CLI has a --no-chrome flag (present in the 2.1.295 strings, but conformance has not actually passed it yet). Sage's Browser page governs only its own webview, and the option is also written as 'Codex' (#54). Basic tier: dsh has experimental Playwright and Chrome DevTools plugins that are off by default.
conflicts.decision: Two channels: Sage acts as an MCP client proxying a version-pinned @playwright/mcp --extension (run by a utilityProcess, because the RunAsNode fuse is off), connecting to the user's real Chrome, with one instance and one tab group per chat and tokens stored in the keychain per profile; the built-in BrowserPanel uses CDP over webContents.debugger, with a clean profile. BrowserPanel uses its own partition, nodeIntegration off and no preload; CDP can attach only to this webContents, and the code asserts the target is not the app UI's webContents. Site permissions are enforced at the proxy layer. Injection uses the same three channels. Claude always passes extraArgs {'no-chrome': null}, and the Claude in Chrome option is removed: the "Your Chrome" channel covers the same use cases and works on every harness. Migration: users who had Claude in Chrome on before the upgrade see an explanation once at first launch in Built-in tools → Browser and once in the next Claude chat, guiding them to install the Playwright extension; the release notes carry one line "Claude in Chrome is replaced by Your Chrome in Built-in tools. It works with every harness and keeps site permissions in MoPilot."
conflicts.ui: The Browser page has two channels, "MoPilot browser (clean profile, none of your logins)" and "Your Chrome (uses sites you're signed in to, needs an extension)", with install guidance and a connection test; site permissions are split into read-only and read-write. The 'Codex' in "Local URL open destination" is changed to 'MoPilot'.

conflicts.conflict: Text-only models cannot use screenshots
conflicts.codex: What Codex intercepts by input_modalities is only images pasted by the user; images in MCP tool results from thread config are handed to the model natively. Measured on 0.162: gpt-6-luna misreads even single letters in images the user inputs directly, so visual checks need a sol-class model.
conflicts.claude: All Claude models can see images; models under third-party endpoints may not (GLM text, Kimi K2, user-configured endpoints). Basic-tier models are managed by the harness itself, and ACP's configOptions give only the model name and not the input modalities; promptCapabilities.image only says whether a prompt can carry images, and does not mean images in MCP tool results will be handed to the model.
conflicts.decision: Whether a model can see images is decided by ModelInfo.input, not by Provider. If it can see images: tool results carry the screenshot plus an element table. If it cannot: give only the AX and OCR element table, and inject two tools, locate and describe, backed by the same Provider's visionFallbackModel; if the Provider has none, use a vision model on MoPilot credits, asking for consent on first use and stating where the data goes; the coordinate convention is converted on the server side. When the basic tier's modality is unknown (ModelInfo.input='unknown'), treat it as "may not be able to see images": tool results carry both the screenshot and the element table, and locate and describe are injected; quirks may provide a model-to-modality table to turn off the downgrade. When there is no vision backend at all (not logged in to MoPilot, cross-vendor consent refused), computer use still works with the element table generated from the helper's AX tree plus local Vision framework OCR, giving only element ids and text, with locate and describe not injected, and nothing is blocked.
conflicts.ui: When taking a screenshot in a chat with a text-only model, the activity bar reads "{vision model} reads the screen · Screenshots go to {vendor}"; when there is no vision backend it reads "Reading the screen as text on this Mac"; text-only models in the model picker carry a "Text only" badge.

conflicts.conflict: Switching harness or Provider mid-chat
conflicts.codex: Segment and handoff are already implemented, but approval card labels, message editing and thumbs-up judge the harness by chat id (#40); after switching away, an active goal on the old Codex thread keeps running automatically.
conflicts.claude: During pendingSwitch, /goal hits the old harness (#11); the handoff prefix is concatenated before the user's text, which breaks / commands; pushing the handoff message before the user message produces an extra turn. SwitchSheet does not list which account the new segment will use and does not handle queued messages; multi-agent is migrated along, and token consumption suddenly rises.
conflicts.decision: All actions are routed by segment, settling pendingSwitch first. On switch, mode and effort are migrated via semantic mapping (the mapping is written in SwitchSheet's Changes column); multi-agent is not migrated by default and needs the user to tick it; permissions only stay the same or get stricter; the old Codex segment's goal gets set paused, and the old Claude segment gets interrupt then clear with the condition recorded; across harnesses the goal is not carried over by default but can be ticked to be re-set in the new segment, and when switching Provider within the same harness it is ticked by default; background tasks still running in the old segment are listed, asking whether to stop them; queued messages are handled by the user choosing "send along with the switch" or "leave behind". Handoff text is not sent as a separate message, and the target adapter places it in the first block of the same user message. Switching Provider also goes through here, as a new segment. When switching back to a harness used before, the original session is restored and only the delta is sent, with the divider reading "Back on Codex · Caught up on 6 messages from Claude Code". Segment handoff is supported between Codex and Claude Code; switching to or from the basic tier offers only "New chat with a summary". A hint is given when another agent is already running in the same cwd.
conflicts.ui: SwitchSheet has three columns (Comes along / Stays behind / Changes), with the Changes column always carrying four rows: account and data destination, effort mapping, multi-agent and permissions; the privacy notice is emphasised only the first time crossing vendors.

conflicts.conflict: Turn diff, undo and fork positions are inaccurate
conflicts.codex: In a reopened chat, the Last Turn diff is assembled from fileChange; rollbackThread calls a non-existent thread/rollback (store.ts:1598, which returns -32600 unknown variant on 0.162); thread/fork supports forking to a given turn, which Sage does not pass, so Fork chat from here copies the whole chat (#62); a thread with a goal resumes immediately after being forked. Measured on 0.162: thread/revert {threadId, beforeTurnId} changes only the history and not the files; thread/fork {lastTurnId, excludeTurns:true} returns a new thread containing only up to that turn.
conflicts.claude: Last Turn diff overwrites by path, so for the same file only the last edit is kept; command output is not streamed, and exit codes are synthetic; editing a message cannot roll back (#68); forkSession supports upToMessageId, which Sage does not pass. Measured on 2.1.295: rewindFiles(uuid) needs enableFileCheckpointing:true and a uuid the caller writes on the SDKUserMessage itself (not echoed in the stream), and dryRun can preview which files would be restored; forkSession and renameSession are top-level functions, not Query methods; there is no /rewind command. Basic tier: some declare sessionCapabilities.fork, none has rewind.
conflicts.decision: Claude persists the structuredPatch of every Edit and accumulates them in order; Bash results use the structured exit code; turn on enableFileCheckpointing, have send() write a uuid on every user message, and editing a message goes through rewindFiles(uuid) (first dryRun to list the files that would be restored); chats created before the upgrade have no checkpoint, so message editing is greyed out, with the reason "Created before checkpoints · Fork from here instead". Codex switches to thread/revert; fork passes lastTurnId, and when there is a goal it carries deferGoalContinuation. Claude forkSession(sid, {upToMessageId: uuid}). Basic tier: use sessionCapabilities.fork if present, otherwise Fork is hidden; rewind is none(harness); the Diff panel shows only the diff content in ACP tool_calls. fork and side chat inherit the original chat's instance.
conflicts.ui: The Diff panel and the undo button behave the same on both first-class harnesses; editing a message is enabled by rewind capability; Fork chat from here really starts from that message; the side chat title bar shows the account in use.

conflicts.conflict: Chat identity leaks, so new windows, copy commands and export break on non-Codex chats
conflicts.codex: The chat id is the Codex thread id, so there is no problem.
conflicts.claude: 'claude:<uuid>' gets truncated by /thread=([\w-]+)/ when a new window parses the hash (store.ts:591), so both Open in new window and Fork into new window fail, and when Codex initialization fails even parsing is never reached (#24); Copy resume command copies 'codex resume claude:…' (TitleBar.tsx:202, #69); on export, Claude's replies are labelled Codex (transcript.ts:16, #61). Once 'acp:<harness>:<id>' is added, the same problem will grow.
conflicts.decision: Deep links are written with encodeURIComponent and read with decodeURIComponent, with the regex /thread=([^&]+)/, and parsing moves out of Codex's connect(); harness ownership is read only from segment records, and an unknown kind is an error; the rpc layer asserts that the segment kind matches the adapter; copying the ID and resume command is generated by StaticInfo.resumeCommand() (for the basic tier it is provided by quirks and exists only after conformance verification); export uses each segment's harness name, with a line of explanation at the switch.
conflicts.ui: The ⋯ → Copy submenu reads "Copy {label} session ID" and "Copy resume command", the latter hidden on harnesses with no terminal way to resume.

conflicts.conflict: Gateway billing loophole, and auto-update and consent sync interrupting the user
conflicts.codex: Under MoPilot, ⚡ forwards service_tier:'priority' unchanged to OpenAI, and the gateway deducts only the standard token price (#76).
conflicts.claude: Claude's fast requests and web search server-side tools are forwarded unchanged to Anthropic, and the gateway does not bill them separately (#76). Common to both: changing auto-update or the channel in About does not take effect immediately (#77); when not in /Applications, "Move MoPilot to Applications?" pops up repeatedly (#78); Restart to update does not check running turns (#79); every launch resets the account-level sharing switch to the local value (#80).
conflicts.decision: WP0: the gateway prices service_tier and speed separately, and when unpriced rejects with a readable error; parse the billing of server_tool_use and Responses web_search; /v1/models returns only priced models, with a capability table attached. The desktop ⚡ reads mopilot's drops. WP9: update-preference sync moves to the App root component, configure rebuilds the timer only when the value changes; periodic checks are silent and run only inside /Applications, with dialogs reserved for manual checks and remembering Not Now; supported is based on the signature check; consent is PUT only when the user changes it, and at sign-in is merged taking the stricter side and written back locally. WP7's exit gate is shared by Restart to update, Quit and helper upgrades, and counts three kinds of things that will be stopped: running turns, background tasks (Workflow, /loop, Monitor, background terminals), and active goals; the copy lists what will be stopped, and after confirmation it first sets active Codex goals to paused, does interrupt then clear on Claude goals and records the conditions, and then exits; confirmClose is hooked up.
conflicts.ui: When there are turns, the update banner reads "2 turns and 1 goal are running · Restart when idle / Restart now"; the Quit confirmation dialog lists "1 turn, 2 background workflows and 1 goal will stop. Goals are paused, not lost."

commandLayer.summary: Add a layer of semantic commands between the UI and the harness. Menus, buttons and shortcuts are organized by semantics (goal, plan, review, multi-agent, compact, init, skills, etc.), and each adapter gives one binding per semantic: rpc, passthrough, config, polyfill, route, or none with a Why. The harness's own command catalog is merged in dynamically and passed through by default. There are only three CommandProviders: Claude's supportedCommands and commands_changed (69 entries measured on 2.1.295, with only the fields name, description, argumentHint, aliases, builtin), the basic tier's available_commands_update, and Codex's static table plus feature gating. State triggered by a command (goal, plan, tasks) is written back to SessionState only from harness events; controls draw only the operations that were declared, and controls owned by Sage (pause and cap for a Claude goal) are marked "by MoPilot". When something cannot be done, Why.layer decides whether to hide, route or grey out. The two hard-coded tables today (Composer.tsx:91-138 and 987-1066) are the direct reason /goal, /init, /review and /usage fail on Claude.
rules: Use a single registry: Sage's UI commands plus the CommandProvider of the harness of the current segment. Typed commands and the / menu come from the same source and behave identically under the same name; every command that can be typed appears in the menu, marked with the arguments it needs; aliases (Claude's /review -> code-review) are read from aliases and can be typed as well.

Pass through by default. Sage takes over only three kinds: pure UI commands (/new, /settings, /diff, /fork, /model and /permissions without arguments); commands the harness implements only interactively: a static list measured per CLI version (on Claude 2.1.295, /tasks, /status, /memory, /skills, /plan, /permissions, /feedback and /resume, which supportedCommands does not list and which reply "/X isn't available in this environment.") plus init.terminal_slash_commands (doctor, color, focus, reload-plugins), for which Sage builds the UI with the SDK or RPC (local-jsx and terminalOriented are CLI-internal fields that the SDK does not expose and that cannot be read at runtime); and commands that would break the session (/clear and /reset, /new are mapped to creating a new chat; /exit is forbidden).

The adapter owns the pass-through format: for Claude, the last content block is plain text starting with / (measured on 2.1.295: it is not recognized unless it is the last block), and the block order is handoff, images, user text; Codex uses structured input items; ACP uses content blocks. Messages the user types by hand carry origin human; so does the '/goal <condition>' that Sage resends when the user clicks Resume (user-initiated); messages Sage synthesizes automatically (handoff, scheduled-task triggers, a /goal resent after an account switch) do not.

In the Claude adapter, remove the logic that rewrites a Codex skill into '/<name>' and the handoff prefix concatenation, and add origin human to user messages. The previous version worried that adding origin would make unknown commands report "Unknown command", so it prescribed an ordering; measured on 2.1.295 this does not reproduce (with or without origin, unknown commands go to the model via unknown_command_fallback), so this ordering requirement is dropped.
Matching rule: the popup matches by command-name prefix, not by title substring. When the input is exactly the same as a native command of the current harness, pass through first.

Presentation follows Why.layer: a command whose binding is none with layer=harness does not enter the menu; when the user types it exactly, show a one-line explanation or route instead of sending it as text. Commands blocked by version, provider, model, account, a switch or session state stay in the menu greyed out, with the reason and the fix action.

Polyfilled semantics (Codex's Init, Claude's '!') sit in the same position and use the same name as native ones; they apply only to the first-class tier, carry a small "by MoPilot" label in the description, and execute through the polyfills/* engine.

The rule for recognizing unknown commands in a Codex thread is narrow: look only at the first token, shaped like /name and not immediately followed by '/' or a path character. When recognized, show "Codex doesn't have this command" and offer "Send as plain text". Questions such as "can't find node under /usr/local/bin" are not intercepted.

Native output is rendered with dedicated styles: Claude's system local_command_output and synthesized command echoes ('Goal set:', 'Goal cleared:', 'Goal active:', '<local-command-stdout>') are shown in the "command output" style; the criterion is model '<synthetic>' plus the text prefix, and local_command_source is a CLI @internal field used only as an aid. The synthesized 'Stop hook feedback' user message collapses into one line, "Goal check #{n}: {reason}". When /goal is rejected because of restricted hooks (disableAllHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly) or an untrusted workspace, the text the CLI returns is shown verbatim. compact_boundary (trigger manual) and status's compact_result and compact_error render as divider lines.
