Workflow, Skill, Monitor, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode and Agent each have their own card; the basic tier's sub-agents and dsh's goal tool calls use the generic Agent card or tool card; only unrecognized tools use the generic card.

An intercepted command must also handle its attachments: either use them together or clear them, never leaving them to linger into the next message. Command execution must catch errors and show a prompt, leaving no unhandled rejection.

The command catalog is cached by (instance, cwd) and replaced wholesale when commands_changed or available_commands_update arrives. On the home page when there is no session yet, only Claude prefetches: extras(bin, cwd, account) reads initializationResult().commands, terminal commands are first filtered by the static list, and once the live session's system/init arrives they are corrected by terminal_slash_commands; the basic tier has a command catalog only after session/new, and before that the / menu lists only app commands.

When the basic tier has never pushed a command catalog, a typed /xxx is passed through verbatim, with no interception and no prompt (the harness decides how to handle it); once it has pushed one, typing a command not in the catalog shows a one-line explanation plus "Send as plain text".

table.semantic: goal (keep working until a condition is met)
table.codex: rpc: thread/goal/set|get|clear (using nativeOf), always subscribing to thread/goal/updated and cleared (the model has its own create_goal and update_goal, so a goal may appear without going through Sage). A new chat, like an existing thread, calls only set, and set starts the turn itself on a new thread; Sage renders the user's "/goal X" bubble locally. In Plan, switch back to default first; Pause or Stop = set paused, then turn/interrupt (500ms timeout); a completed goal gets no Resume. When the user turns goals off, grey out at the flag layer (read experimentalFeature/list, error code -32600); grey out at the session layer for an ephemeral thread. controls: pause, resume, budget (tokenBudget, a soft cap, settled per turn), edit, clear.
table.claude: passthrough: '/goal <condition>', '/goal', '/goal clear', as plain strings, as the last content block, through the send queue. GoalSnapshot comes from synthesized messages: 'Goal set:' sets active, 'Goal cleared:' clears, each 'Stop hook feedback' increments rounds by 1 and updates lastReason, and the transcript's goal_status (met) marks complete; active_goal is not read (the local CLI does not output it). controls: pause, resume (owned by Sage: interrupt() then '/goal clear', and Resume resends '/goal <condition>'), budget (Sage counts rounds and, at the cap, interrupts first and then clears), clear. When hooks are restricted or the workspace is untrusted, the CLI's rejection text is shown verbatim.

shared.summary: Some capabilities must behave the same on every harness, while the harness itself either lacks them or is limited by plan, login method or interaction mode. Sage owns these capabilities, in two kinds. The first kind is platform services users use directly: terminal, files, search, projects, scheduled tasks, worktrees, notifications, dictation, and saving the transcript for harnesses that have no history replay. They are implemented in Electron main without going through any harness, and are also the implementation of the ACP client-side fs and terminal. The second kind is tools called by the model: computer use, browser, vision degradation. They are injected per session through three injection channels: one in-process SDK MCP server per Claude session; mcp_servers in the Codex thread config (carried by both thread/start and thread/resume); and session/new mcpServers for all basic-tier harnesses. All shared capabilities obey the following: write no harness's global config, so turning them off fully restores things; the server name carries a per-session random suffix, the harness's permission layer allows only that name, and authorization is executed in Sage's handler; calls with side effects are handled only once, in main; only one set of tools of the same kind appears in the same session; the agent cannot control MoPilot itself; unattended turns can use only apps that have been authorized.

items.owner: electron/capabilities/computer (registry, policy, approval, logging) plus Contents/Helpers/MoPilot Computer Use.app: a Swift helper, LSUIElement, launched through LaunchServices, and the sole TCC authorization identity; it implements input, accessibility and capture natively (CGEvent, AX, ScreenCaptureKit) and does not embed cua-driver (decision WP8-3); it handles permission probing, a global Esc sourced from HID, the screen glow, the global desktop lock (one per user, shared by multiple profiles, with the holder shown in the tray), detection of physical-input takeover, SCContentFilter screenshots (excluding the MoPilot window and the glow overlay), an event tap that drops all non-assistive-technology synthesized events landing on the MoPilot window, and generating the element table from the AX tree plus local Vision OCR. It accepts only connections whose audit-token pid equals the registered main pid and whose signature matches. It is signed with #16's Developer ID and Team ID, with separate entitlements, signed from the inside out, and packaged via extraResource.
items.mechanism: Claude: every startSession creates a new createSdkMcpServer instance, named sage_<nonce> and placed in options.mcpServers; the tools are set to alwaysLoad and not hidden behind ToolSearch; the handler cannot get the sessionId, so call attribution relies on a closure plus _meta['claudecode/toolUseId']; under the default, acceptEdits and auto tiers, canUseTool allows mcp__sage_<nonce>__* directly, and the read-only tier adds the observation tools to allowedTools one by one; onElicitation is added. Codex: the config of thread/start and thread/resume writes mcp_servers.sage_<nonce> = {command: <sage-mcp path>, args, env: {token}} with default_tools_approval_mode="approve", and observation tools are marked readOnlyHint (when approvalPolicy is never, omitting this makes every call fail); the same config writes plugins["unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"].enabled=false to turn off cua_repl and mcp_servers.node_repl.enabled=false to turn off the user's node_repl (verified in X14); images are handed to the model natively through MCP; the token rotates on every resume, so an old token is useless even if it lands in a rollout; dynamicTools is not used (under forced code mode images become data-URL strings, and the model cannot see them without calling image()). Basic tier: session/new's mcpServers holds the stdio sage-mcp, with server name sage_<nonce> and env written as a {name,value} array, and sage-mcp is ready before the session is created; request_permission auto-allows once for tools of sage_<nonce>; if the sage-mcp handshake is not received within 10 seconds of the session being created, admission is judged failed.
items.harnesses: All harnesses, regardless of login method and billing method; if injection into the basic tier does not succeed, it is not admitted. Codex's native cua_repl, Claude's built-in computer-use and dsh's Cua plugin are not used as sources.

items.owner: electron/capabilities/browser: Sage acts as an MCP client and proxies an exact-version-pinned @playwright/mcp --extension (run by a utilityProcess; one instance and one tab group per chat, with the token stored in the keychain per profile); the built-in BrowserPanel uses webContents.debugger over CDP (separate partition, nodeIntegration off, no preload, with code asserting that the CDP target is not the app UI's webContents). Site permissions (read-only, read-write) and download and upload authorization are all enforced at the proxy layer.
items.mechanism: The same three channels as computer use, with tool prefix sage_browser: Claude's per-session SDK MCP, always passing extraArgs {'no-chrome': null}; Codex thread config's mcp_servers.sage_<nonce>; and the basic tier's session/new mcpServers (dsh's Playwright and Chrome DevTools plugins are off by default, and quirks only asserts they are not on).

items.owner: electron/capabilities/vision: locate(description) returns an element id or coordinates, and describe(region) returns a text description; the backend is the same Provider's visionFallbackModel, and when the Provider has none, a vision model on MoPilot credits. The fallback element table is generated by the helper's AX tree plus local Vision framework OCR and needs no model.
items.mechanism: When the current model's ModelInfo.input does not contain image, locate and describe are injected, through the same channels as computer use; screenshots go only to the vision model, and the main model gets only the element table and text. When a basic-tier model's modality is unknown, tool results carry both the screenshot and the element table and locate and describe are injected; quirks can provide a model-to-modality table to turn degradation off. The coordinate convention (pixels, 0-999, 0-1000, Retina multiples) is converted on the server side. The first time it crosses vendors, consent is requested. When there is no vision backend at all (not signed in to MoPilot, cross-vendor consent refused), computer use works from the AX plus local OCR element table, giving only element ids and text, injecting neither locate nor describe, and does not block.

Policy: a no-go table (MoPilot, the helper, System Settings' Privacy & Security, Keychain Access, password apps) cannot be unlocked in any mode; approval cards, permission settings and Full access accept only human-initiated input (judged by the event source pid, with system assistive technology allowed, plus a keyboard confirmation of holding ⌘↩ for one second); app authorization buttons are Allow once / Allow in this chat / Always allow, with levels View only / Click / Full control; irreversible action categories are confirmed in every mode; a CU authorization table by permission anchor; unattended runs can use only apps on the chat list and the global list, and when a new authorization is needed the goal is paused and a notify is sent; the user moving the mouse or pressing a key takes over immediately; the agent cannot type into a password field; project config cannot enable control; one operation timeline per chat. In telemetry, CU tool calls record only name and status, and screenshots, AX trees, and the type and clipboard parameters are not uploaded.

items.mechanism: Archive, pin, unread, project membership and the goal pause that Sage owns are written per chat into threads/<id>.v2.json, atomically and only by main. The transcript of a basic-tier harness with history:'sage' is written to <id>.items.jsonl. ⌘K merges Codex thread/search and thread/list(searchTerm), main's scan of Claude jsonl, and the index of Sage's own stored transcripts and basic-tier titles. Codex archives are mirrored to thread/archive. projects.json is imported on first launch: if Codex is installed, the app-server is started on demand in the background once to read project/*, and on failure this is recorded and the import is retried the next time Codex connects; afterwards, when Codex is online, it syncs one way.

items.owner: electron/platform/scheduler (userData/automations), with the code in WP7 (which needs WP5's adapter).
items.mechanism: A task record holds harness, instance, model, effort, cwd, whether computer control is allowed (off by default) and the app list, and how to handle needing approval (Wait and notify or Skip this run, marked needs attention after more than 1 hour); at the due time it runs through adapter.start/send, and Run now uses the same function. Sharing with the official Codex app is an optional dual write. The Claude reaper keeps sessions alive when there is a cron.

Before adapter.start, create the worktree and run the setup script, then hand the cwd to the adapter; on archive or delete run cleanup, and clean old worktrees per the autoDelete setting. The default prefix is mopilot/, the root directory ~/.mopilot/worktrees, with no dependence on codexHome. environment.toml keeps the original TOML and changes only the darwin fields.

Native sessions are never rewritten; across harnesses or Providers only a text projection is sent: Claude puts it in the first text block of the same user message (the / command stays in the last block), Codex puts it in the first text input item, and the basic tier puts it in the first content block. When switching back to a harness already used, its original session is restored and only the delta is resent, with the divider line stating how many items were added. The handoff panel lists what was not carried over and where the data goes.

items.mechanism: Titles are generated by the harness the chat is in, with the account the chat uses: Claude uses an auxiliary session that is not persisted to disk, and Codex uses a hidden ephemeral thread. The basic tier (including dsh and opencode) always uses the first user message truncated as the title, never sending chat content to another vendor. Handoff summaries and voice-routing summaries are generated by the source harness, and when that is not possible Sage's text projection is used, with no model call.

notify(kind) has five kinds: turn complete, approval needed, scheduled task, goal status, authorization needed; they all read the Notifications settings, each kind can be switched on or off separately, and there is also a preset "Only when I'm needed". Merging and throttling: each chat keeps only one notification at a time, with a new one replacing the old (the same thread identifier); "needs you" kinds (approval, authorization, goal paused) take priority over "complete" kinds; notifications of the same kind within 60 seconds merge into one ("3 chats need you"); an unattended denial notifies only once, when the goal is paused.

deepseek.verdict: DeepSeek's recommended path is Claude Code plus a DeepSeek Provider: first-class tier, with all capabilities (goal, plan, review, ultracode, computer use, browser), injected per DeepSeek's official Anthropic-compatible configuration. dsh is the basic tier: the user installs it themselves, and Sage neither distributes it, pins its version, isolates DSH_HOME nor injects a key, adding only the privacy patch and turning telemetry off, and verifying before launch that the patch took effect (refusing to launch if it did not); DeepSeek's own agent loop, goal tool and subagent_fork work as usual in dsh, but Sage provides only the basic-tier contract. For a new user who has filled in only a DeepSeek key: the default is Claude Code·DeepSeek; when Claude Code is not installed, the welcome page offers a one-click Claude Code install, and a dsh that is installed and has passed admission is listed as the basic tier. Billing can be the user's own DeepSeek key or MoPilot credits (only under Claude Code·MoPilot, with a gateway DeepSeek upstream as an option). On every path, computer use and the browser are provided by Sage's toolkit. harnessPlan.summary: Two tiers. First-class tier: Codex and Claude Code, with dedicated adapters (instances in main); every semantic is bound explicitly (native, polyfill, or none with a reason); the P0 journeys and all acceptance criteria must pass; versions are managed as "minimum version plus known-bad versions, probed by capability". Basic tier: dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose, with a generic ACP adapter plus a quirks file, promising only the basicTierContract; quirks must declare privacyDefaults; a harness appears in the picker, with a Basic badge, only after passing runtime admission (initialize succeeds, the sage-mcp handshake, image round-trip, privacy check); those that do not pass show "installed · not supported in this version" and the reason. The basic tier has no Sage polyfill (no goal, plan, review, init, compact, or '!'). Promoting a basic-tier harness to first-class later is a product decision, adding only a dedicated adapter without changing components. Amp (no official ACP) and Crush (no embedding interface) are outside this design.

playbook.step: 1. First decide whether it is a Provider or a harness
playbook.detail: Something that offers only an Anthropic, Responses or Chat Completions compatible endpoint (such as some vendor's model API) gets just one ProviderProfile, attached under a first-class harness that speaks that wire protocol, and that is the end of it: fill in the model catalog (each model's input modality, effort, whether it has ultra, speed tiers), effortLevels, compactWindow, visionFallbackModel and the officially recommended env. Without a dedicated preset, use custom first. Only something with its own agent loop, session storage and external protocol counts as a new harness. For something with both identities (DeepSeek), do both, and state in the format of the deepseek section which one is recommended.
playbook.artifact: docs/harnesses/<id>.md: per-axis conclusions, authentication method, data destinations (log uploads, telemetry, screenshots sent out).

playbook.step: 2. Choose the tier and the channel
playbook.detail: Default to generic ACP; the basic tier writes only the launch command and quirks. Promoting to first-class is a product decision, not a technical judgment: write a dedicated adapter only when the owner decides to promote. Confirm the ACP version (only v1 is supported), loadSession, whether MCP goes over stdio or HTTP, and whether fork is supported. Sage neither distributes nor pins harness versions, and writes only the minimum version and known-bad versions.
playbook.artifact: One record in src/harness/registry.ts (tier, channel, detect, versions).

playbook.step: 3. Write StaticInfo and the quirks file
playbook.detail: StaticInfo records kind, label, vendor, channel, the detection method (the login shell's PATH) and install command, instructionsFiles, skillRoots, docsUrl, resumeCommand (returning a value only after conformance verification, otherwise null), versions, dataNotes. The quirks file records only what differs from the standard: launch arguments and env; the required privacyDefaults (how default uploads and telemetry are turned off) and the pre-launch privacy check; the mapping from modes to the four anchors (optional) and which mode is plan; terminal commands to filter; the session id namespace; the {name,value} format of MCP env; the mapping from extension methods (such as cursor/create_plan) to Sage cards; a model-to-modality table (optional); workarounds for known bugs.

Map the agentCapabilities, authMethods, mcpCapabilities and promptCapabilities returned by initialize into Negotiated, leaving anything undeclared absent, including accepted image formats, fork granularity, history source ('sage' when there is no loadSession), permission scope, and usage granularity. Read out the CLI's actual version and compare it with the minimum version and known-bad versions; write one runtime probe for each capability that depends on undocumented behavior.

playbook.step: 5. Bind the semantics one by one
playbook.detail: Choose one binding for every Semantic. The basic tier does not choose polyfill; it can only be passthrough, config, route or none. Choosing none requires writing a Why and choosing the right layer: write harness if the harness itself lacks it, and the corresponding layer if something else blocks it, which decides between hiding and greying out. Before choosing polyfill in the first-class tier, check the three criteria. GoalSnapshot.controls is filled only with operations the harness really has or that Sage explicitly owns (marked pauseBy, budgetBy). The Record type lets TypeScript check for omissions.
playbook.artifact: The bindings table, automatically generating one column of the capability matrix.

playbook.step: 6. Translate events and decide the history source
playbook.detail: Translate session/update into SageItem and SessionState: messages, thinking, tool calls, diffs, plan, configOptions, command catalog, usage, approvals, sub-agents. Only unrecognized tools use the generic card. When history is 'sage', main writes threads/<id>.items.jsonl and can replay it. If a tool call still arrives after Stop when there is no prompt in progress, send cancel once more and handle it as unattended. Use recorded real sessions for golden tests.
playbook.artifact: The translator and fixtures, put into npm test.

playbook.step: 7. Wire up the account and background text
playbook.detail: The basic tier has only one account row, "managed by the harness": render authMethods, route logins that need a terminal through the platform pty, and re-detect automatically after exit; Sage injects no key and writes no harness credential files. failover is none, and usage comes from usage_update or none. Titles use the truncated first message.
playbook.artifact: The harness's Overview section on the Other harnesses page.

playbook.step: 8. Inject the shared tools and pass admission
playbook.detail: Shared tools are injected via session/new mcpServers, and this is an admission condition. Admission has two steps: runtime (initialize succeeds, the sage-mcp handshake is received within 10 seconds after session/new, and the privacy check declared in quirks passes) and conformance (tool results return images and the model can read the random word in the image; when modality is unknown, the degradation tools are usable). If either fails, the harness does not enter the picker and shows "installed · not supported in this version" with the reason. Confirm that the harness's own browser or computer use is off by default or has been turned off; confirm that request_permission asks only once for sage_<nonce> tools.
playbook.artifact: The injection config, the admission record, and a new cell in the "control source" column of the Settings compatibility table.

playbook.detail: Conformance scenarios run against the real CLI on a local machine with a test account. First-class tier: new, send, streaming, approval, cancel, resume, goal (including pause, quit and restart, account switch), plan, review, compact, init, skills, background-task stop, injected tools returning images, message block order, a temporary chat meeting an account switch, killing the process. The basic tier runs only the contract scenarios: admission, new, send, streaming, approval, cancel, resume after restart, command pass-through, one desktop task, one browser task, plus packet capture for dsh. Golden replays go into npm test (CI runs them on every PR). A source scan confirms that src/components has no new harness names or rpc calls. Two matrices are generated: the full-semantics matrix for the first-class tier, and the contract items and admission results for the basic tier.

playbook.step: 10. Accept in the real app, then release
playbook.detail: Run the acceptance checklist that applies to the tier in the real Electron release build. A basic-tier harness that passes admission ships with the release and appears in the picker; promoting it to first-class is decided by the owner, followed by adding a dedicated adapter and passing all first-class acceptance. The release notes state the data destinations and the scope of the basic tier.
playbook.artifact: The acceptance record, StaticInfo.tier, the release notes.

roadmap.title: Conformance probes, release infrastructure, and the gateway capability table
roadmap.goal: In the first week, get three kinds of things done: checks that decide design branches (bring the already-completed Claude 2.1.295 and Codex 0.162 probes into the repo and run the remaining ones, and run admission probes against the 8 basic-tier harnesses); things that can only be verified on a signed build (computer use helper prototype, native dependency packaging, Electron fuses); and things other work packages read directly (remote kill switch, dogfood channel, the gateway /v1/models capability table and Fast pricing). No prerequisites.
items: tests/conformance: bring the claude and codex probe libraries from the scratchpad into the repo (lib/claude.mjs, lib/codex.mjs, lib/acp.mjs), record JSONL uniformly and write results/<kind>@<version>.json; check in the results for Claude Code 2.1.295 (C1–C15) and codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 (X1–X13) directly.

Re-run first-class-harness checks: Claude — with an active goal, after a restartResume (account switch), is the Stop hook preserved, and can Sage re-send '/goal <condition>' to pick it back up; extraArgs {'no-chrome': null} is actually passed through; kill the CLI process mid-turn; after alwaysLoad, Sage tools no longer go through ToolSearch. Codex — X14: can node_repl be turned off per thread via mcp_servers.node_repl.enabled=false, and does codex_apps have a per-thread switch; kill the app-server mid-turn; after set paused before exit, a restart does not resume; re-run X1–X13 against the then-current stable codex.

ACP admission probes: for each of the 8 basic-tier harnesses, record initialize capabilities, the handshake after session/new with sage-mcp (random server name), image return in tool results (the model reads a random word out of the image, using a vision-capable model), modes, configOptions, available_commands_update, and loadSession; for dsh, use --dump-config to confirm session-log-deepseek is off, and capture traffic to confirm the request body contains no session log.

Packaging: asar.unpack (*.node, node-pty's spawn-helper, rg), strip node-pty's win32 prebuilds, have osx-sign cover the unpacked Mach-O files; with @electron/fuses, turn off RunAsNode, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable, and EnableNodeCliInspectArguments, and turn on OnlyLoadAppFromAsar and EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation; set up the build and signing steps for the Swift programs under native/ (shared by helper, sage-mcp, and auth-command); cut a test tag and get release.yml's codesign --verify, spctl, and stapler to pass.

Remote kill switch /api/flags (per channel and version) and the desktop cache userData/flags.json; dogfood channel. The switches are only for turning off a misbehaving harness, injection channel, or computer use, not for hiding half-finished work.

Gateway capability table (pulled forward from WP9, deployed separately from web/): /v1/models returns only priced models and attaches a capability table (the source of the mopilot ProviderProfile's drops); service_tier and speed are priced separately, and unpriced requests are rejected with a readable error; parse usage.server_tool_use and bill Responses web_search calls (#76).
roadmap.exit: Result files for both first-class harnesses are checked in, and every re-run check has a conclusion; each of the 8 basic-tier harnesses has an admission result (pass, or the reason it failed); in the signed test build, the helper's TCC grant is recorded under the helper's name, running the MoPilot binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 has no effect, and the terminal and rg can start; remote switches take effect when toggled in a dogfood build; /v1/models contains no unpriced models, and under MoPilot a Fast request is charged at the priority price or rejected with a notice.

roadmap.title: Harness contract, capability intersection, and chat data model
roadmap.goal: Set up the types and data foundation shared by later work packages: an open harness registry (codex, claude, and 8 acp:<id> entries), three-layer descriptors, semantic bindings, the six-layer intersection and presentation rules, a segment-based chat model, session state and the adapter process boundary owned by main, and atomic persistence that can be rolled back to the old version. No prerequisites.
items: src/harness/adapter.ts (descriptorTs types: no http-sse and no tool binding, polyfill reduced to init, shell, archive, search, three toolInjection kinds, GoalSnapshot with pauseBy, budgetBy, source, and SessionState carrying rev), registry.ts (tier, channel, detect, versions, and quirks id for codex, claude, and acp:dsh|opencode|kimi|qwen|copilot|cursor|gemini|goose), caps.ts (resolveCaps six-layer intersection; the five present CapState values; the Why text table changed to English key-values, extended from FAST_BLOCKED_TEXT), commands.ts (CommandRegistry types and synthesis rules).

Process boundary: the HarnessAdapter instance, ChatController's send queue, pendingSwitch settlement, and the turn state machine (idle, running, awaitingUser, crashed) all live in main (electron/harness, electron/session); src/harness/adapters/* only does IPC proxying. Every action first resolves a NativeRef; queue items keep the full SendOptions and pass them to the adapter on dequeue, and messages carrying plan or goal do not go through steer (#50); goal active and turn running are modeled separately; each turn is marked as user-initiated or unattended.

SessionState is owned by main (electron/session/state.cjs), written only by adapter events, and carries rev; a window subscribing first gets a full snapshot, then applies patches by rev, and re-pulls on a gap; side-effecting handling lives only in main.

Persistence: threads/<id>.v2.json = {schemaVersion:2, segments[{kind, nativeId, instance, provider, model, handoff}], meta{archived, pinned, unread, projectId, config, account, goalHeld, notes[]}}, written per chat by main only, via a temp file followed by rename; prefs become per-key merges by main, with windows sending only deltas (#39); threads/<id>.items.jsonl serves basic-tier harnesses with history:'sage'.

Migration: runs in main before any window opens, is idempotent, and has a completion marker; first back up ui-state.json and threads/*; merge claudeArchived, claudeChats, pinned, unread, and worktreeOf into the v2 files; the old keys in ui-state.json are frozen and not deleted, the old threads/<id>.json are kept, and during 0.3.x changes to Codex and Claude segments are mirrored write-only back to the old locations (acp segments are never mirrored); old chats with no file get a v2 file generated lazily by a single hard-coded legacy rule ('claude:' prefix → claude, everything else → codex), and this rule appears only once, in the migration code.

IDs and routing: the native id of a basic-tier harness is stored as 'acp:<harness>:<id>'; harness ownership is read only from the segment record, and an unknown kind is an error; approval card labels, edit message, like, and the turn-error Sign in all follow the current segment (#40); the rpc layer asserts that the segment kind matches the adapter kind, and a fixture proves a 'claude:' id cannot reach Codex.

Deep links: write with encodeURIComponent, read with decodeURIComponent, regex /thread=([^&]+)/, and move the parsing out of Codex's connect() (store.ts:591, #24). StaticInfo.resumeCommand() and each segment's label are shared by the copy items in TitleBar and Sidebar (#69) and the export title in transcript.ts (#61), with a one-line note at the switch point.

tests/boundary.test.ts: scan src/components and record the counts of harness literals, harnessOfThread, CLAUDE_PREFIX, and import rpc (baseline: 99 comparison lines, 6 harnessOfThread uses, 11 component files importing rpc); counts may only go down, never up, and reach 0 by the end of WP7; wired into CI (ci.yml).
roadmap.exit: Unit tests cover every layer of resolveCaps and the five outcomes of present(); a fixture proves that calls with a mismatched segment kind are stopped by the assertion; two windows changing archive, pin, and prefs at the same time do not overwrite each other; after killing the process mid-migration and restarting, data is intact and counts before and after migration match; after rolling back to the 0.2.0 (7a5bf12) build, archive and pin are both still there, and the only things not visible are those added after migration; the copied resume command works in a terminal; the boundary test is in CI.

File search: bundle ripgrep 15.2.0 (--files plus fuzzy matching), shared by @ mentions, ⌘P, and the Files panel, replacing fuzzyFileSearch.

Chat list, search, and archive: ⌘K merges Codex thread/search and thread/list(searchTerm), main's scan of Claude jsonl, Sage's own stored transcripts, and the basic-tier title index, with mixed ranking and deduplication (#25); the archive page follows Sage metadata, Claude archives are filled in by id with getSessionInfo, and the sidebar paginates, no longer limited by listSessions(200) (#38).

Worktrees and environments: default prefix mopilot/, root directory ~/.mopilot/worktrees, projectless directory ~/Documents/MoPilot, with existing settings not migrated (#63); the setup script runs before adapter.start, and cleanup runs on archive or delete; wire up autoDeleteWorktrees and autoDeleteLimit; environment.toml keeps the original TOML when read and changes only the darwin fields when written (#46).

Instruction files: saved through main's fs:writeText; export sharedRoot() from harness/claude/accounts.cjs (today it is a module-internal function at line 29), and use it for the CLAUDE.md path; AGENTS.md respects CODEX_HOME; paths for basic-tier harnesses come from the quirks' instructionsFiles.

notify(kind): five kinds — completion, needs approval, scheduled task, goal status, needs authorization — all reading the Notifications setting uniformly (#59); keep only one per chat, merge same-kind ones within 60 seconds, and give priority to "needs your attention".

Detection and environment: at startup take an env snapshot of the login shell ('$SHELL -ilc env -0', 5-second timeout), used by harness detection and the launch of every child process (covering ~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, nvm, ~/.bun/bin); Settings can specify a bin path manually.

App gating: render the main UI as long as any harness is available; Codex not being connected affects only the Codex entry point and the Codex thread banner (App.tsx:108-110); the default harness falls back only for the current run and is not written back to prefs (#66); Settings embeds a login terminal and re-detects automatically after the process exits (#42); the app-server starts on demand.
Sage's own stored transcripts: append-writes and replay-reads of threads/<id>.items.jsonl.
roadmap.exit: With the codex binary moved away, in the real app: creating a projectless Claude chat, the terminal, Files and @ mentions, ⌘K finding a Claude chat, saving CLAUDE.md, and logging in to Claude in Settings can all be completed; without Codex, a Claude chat can open in a new window; a CLI installed in ~/.local/bin is detected; the terminal can open in a signed release build; archiving in two windows loses nothing; after saving the environment file, non-macOS entries are still there; with Notifications set to Never, no system notifications are received any more.

roadmap.title: Identity layer: Provider, Account, MoPilot billing, and the welcome page
roadmap.goal: Keep the Harness, Provider, and Account axes separate; subscriptions, API keys, MoPilot credits, and DeepSeek keys are unified as account rows under a Provider, managed in one place only (Accounts & billing), selectable per chat, with switching that does not interrupt a turn and does not rewrite the CLI's own credentials; a new user goes from zero to the first message through a three-step welcome page. Covers first-class harnesses only. Depends on WP0 (gateway capability table, native build chain), WP1, and WP2 (pty, env snapshot).
items: electron/identity/: the ProviderProfile registry (anthropic, openai, deepseek, mopilot, custom, shell), the Instance registry (with billing: subscription | apiKey | credits), and one AccountDriver each for Codex and Claude (failover, perChat, usage, poolPolicy); accounts.cjs, harness/claude/accounts.cjs, relay.cjs, mopilot.cjs, and billing.ts are consolidated into it.

Environment variables: scrubProcessEnv and cleanEnv share a narrowed list that clears only authentication and parent-session identity (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, etc.), with feature variables restored from WP2's env snapshot; Provider variables are written last; the snapshot in diagnostics is redacted with shared/scrub.cjs (#35).

Claude: each sageKey account (DeepSeek, MoPilot, custom) gets its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with no claude.ai login, with settings.json copied and env, model, and apiKeyHelper removed; claudeAccounts allows sageKey accounts without an email; prepare() becomes a two-way merge of the non-login fields of .claude.json (#44); detect() recognizes mopilot and third-party Providers as billing modes and refreshes on receiving mopilot:event (#75).

Codex: MoPilot and custom Responses endpoints are selected through thread/start.modelProvider, with the definition written into the thread config's model_providers.<id> (verified to work on 0.162, so no launch-argument fallback is needed), and credentials go only through auth.command: the signed native/auth-command helper reads the cached key from the keychain, returns within 200ms, exits non-zero immediately on failure, and never shows any interaction (auth.command runs immediately at thread/start); account/login/start is no longer used to log in a managed key, and ~/.codex/auth.json is not rewritten (#72); custom endpoints are no longer silently ignored (#32).

Codex multi-account fixes: counting, pickFor, usage polling, and canPinChats count only subscription accounts (#70); mopilot does not take part in active() fallback or syncDefault (#71); an API key account pinned to a chat goes through pass-through and is not moved away, with the switch note stating the real reason (#64); Replace and Remove act on the row in use (#33).

Account-switch contract: automatic account switching and the "This chat" account choice stay within the same ProviderProfile and the same billing mode; switching from a subscription to metered billing always asks for confirmation; when a Claude login expires, the switch also stays within the same Provider, and the re-login button targets the account the chat uses and offers "Use another account" (#43); the switch note is written into segments; the usage bar, title, extras, and command catalog prefetch all use the chat's account (#65); with no reading, show "unknown"; temporary chats have a pinned account.

Billing switches affect only the next session start or the next turn and do not call closeAll (#34); logging in or out of MoPilot restarts sessions that are using mopilot only when idle, skipping keep sessions (#74); on logging out of MoPilot, write back the subscription or remaining key, and if there is neither, run account/logout and show a notice (#73).

Accounts & billing: grouped by Provider, with each row stating which harnesses it can be used with and "When a limit is reached"; Add API key lives only here; Share usage sits in the OpenAI group and shows only with at least 2 ChatGPT accounts; Pay with, the model picker, and the welcome page all have MoPilot credits (#81); /logout and the app menu's Log Out open the account row the chat uses, for the user to confirm, and never delete directly (#26).
UsageSnapshot{windows, source, at} unifies usage; MoPilot shows the balance; mopilot's drops read WP0's gateway capability table directly.

Three-step welcome page, replacing Login.tsx's "Welcome to Codex" (#41): (1) choose how to pay; (2) recommend a harness according to that choice and install it with one click (the embedded terminal first shows the official install command, then runs it; after installation it automatically does a Re-check, and Codex automatically starts the app-server after installation); with MoPilot only, the default recommendation is Claude Code · MoPilot, which does not need a claude.ai login; when MoPilot is chosen and only Codex is present, set provider=mopilot on the Codex instance and suppress the ChatGPT login prompt; (3) choose the default harness, which is not changed automatically afterwards; detected basic-tier harnesses are listed last, with a Basic badge.
roadmap.exit: For a user with only one ChatGPT account, after logging in to MoPilot the OpenAI group in Accounts & billing is still the single-account view, with no Share usage; for a user who has never logged in to Codex, logging in to MoPilot does not make Codex start charging; ~/.codex/auth.json is byte-identical before and after the whole flow; a Claude turn running while logging in or out of MoPilot is not interrupted; when a Claude subscription quota runs out, the chat is not moved automatically to DeepSeek, MoPilot, or an API key of the same Provider (a confirmation is asked before switching to an API key); two chats in the same Claude Code can use a subscription and MoPilot respectively; when launched from the Dock, CLAUDE_CODE_* in the user's shell takes effect for the shell Provider; on a Mac with nothing installed and only a MoPilot account, the welcome page installs Claude Code and sends the first message.

roadmap.title: Tool-injection seam, signed sage-mcp, and security seam
roadmap.goal: One tool registry, one call entry point that executes only in main, three injection channels, and the security seam that makes "verify the peer" actually hold: a signed native sage-mcp, a random server name per session, token rotation, and parent-process verification. Depends on WP0 (fuses and native build chain) and WP1 (session ownership and the approval model).
items: electron/capabilities/: skeleton and interfaces for registry, policy, approvals, and log; a tool call is handled in main exactly once, and the result carries the chat and segment ownership.

Server requests are handled only once, in main: server.intercept becomes chained, with the interception in accounts.cjs and Sage's interception coexisting; approvals, elicitation, and other server requests are answered in main and no longer broadcast to every window to answer (the -32601 at store.ts:1641-1643 is deleted).

Contents/Helpers/sage-mcp: a signed Swift command-line program, stdio MCP, that relays calls back to main over a unix socket; for each connection main verifies the per-session token and that "the direct parent process pid equals the pid of that session's harness process"; the token rotates on every resume, is valid only in main's memory, and is invalidated when the session ends.

Per-session random server name sage_<nonce>: both the harness permission layer's allow rule and Sage's authorization recognize only this name; a server named sage in user or project config is not allowed through.

sdkMcp: each Claude startSession creates a new createSdkMcpServer instance (the handler cannot get the sessionId, so ownership relies on a closure plus _meta['claudecode/toolUseId']), with tools set to alwaysLoad; canUseTool allows mcp__sage_<nonce>__*; the read-only tier adds observation tools one by one to allowedTools.

threadConfigMcp: generate the Codex thread config fragment for WP5 to attach at thread/start and thread/resume: mcp_servers.sage_<nonce> = {command, args, env:{token}}, default_tools_approval_mode="approve", observation tools with readOnlyHint, plugins["unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"].enabled=false, and, when X14 passes, mcp_servers.node_repl.enabled=false.

sessionMcp: put the stdio sage-mcp in session/new's mcpServers, with env written as an array of {name,value}, and have sage-mcp ready before the session is created; if no handshake is received within 10 seconds, emit an admission-failure event.

ApprovalRequest (ACP shape) gains computerAccess, browserOrigin, and computerConfirm; ModelInfo.input decides whether tool results return a screenshot or an element table, and when input is unknown both are returned and locate and describe are injected.
tests/fixtures/fake-acp-agent: a fake ACP agent for tests, supporting initialize, session/new (including mcpServers), prompt, cancel, and request_permission, shared by the WP4 and WP6 tests.
roadmap.exit: The debug tool sage_debug.echo (returns an image with a random word) is called by the model and the random word is read out, on both the fake ACP agent (sessionMcp) and the existing Claude code path (sdkMcp, subscription account), with the call attributed to the correct chat; with 3 windows open, each call executes only once; observation tools are callable in the Claude read-only tier; with an MCP server named sage committed into the repo, its tools are not auto-allowed; a direct connection from the agent's bash to main's socket (without the token or with the wrong parent process) is rejected. Real verification of the Codex channel is at WP5's exit, and real verification of the basic tier is at WP6's exit.

roadmap.title: First-class adapters for Codex and Claude Code
roadmap.goal: Move Codex's RPC from the renderer's store.ts into main's electron/harness/codex.cjs, and wrap Claude as an adapter on electron/harness/claude/adapter.cjs; native commands and workflows on both sides work as they are, with state following what the harness reports; crashes, external writes, version drift, and quit-and-restart all have defined paths. Depends on WP0 (conformance results), WP1, WP3, and WP4.
items: Move the Codex adapter into main: all the roughly 50 rpc calls in store.ts (67 app-server methods) use nativeOf; direct rpc calls in 11 component files are moved into the adapter or IPC.

Codex goal: /goal X only calls thread/goal/set (on a new thread it starts the turn itself, with no startTurn, no more "send the first turn then set", and appendTranscriptItem is not passed); Sage renders the user's "/goal X" bubble locally; parse clear, pause, resume, edit (the remainder of #10: the startTurn after set and '/goal clear' being treated as a goal; nativeOf was already fixed by #17); Pause or Stop = set paused then turn/interrupt (500ms timeout; store.ts:1489 sends only interrupt today, #2); accept a late paused→complete, and complete gets no Resume; always subscribe to thread/goal/updated; goal/get on opening a thread; ephemeral threads are greyed out and the input is put back on failure (#49); when goals are off, read experimentalFeature/list. Keep release()'s existing checks and do not change them further.

Codex goals across quit and restart: provide pauseAllActiveGoals() for WP7's quit gate, recording "paused on quit" when pausing; on startup, if an active goal is found (the last crash did not get to pause it), first set paused and then thread/resume.

Codex Plan, Review, Compact: collaborationMode explicitly sends plan or default every turn, using thread/settings/update when only the chip is toggled; the plan card comes from the plan item or the last agentMessage, and "Implement this plan" switches back to default (#13); review/start(nativeOf, delivery fixed to 'inline'), taking the result from exitedReviewMode.review and deduplicating (#4); compact records the request and turn id, and the divider wording depends on who initiated it (#51).

Codex fork and session settings: fork passes lastTurnId (with deferGoalContinuation when there is a goal, #62); rollback changes to thread/revert; ultra appears per model (#15); model, effort, and serviceTier (priority or default) are sent per chat, with effort sent explicitly every turn (#29); ⚡ reads serviceTiers and the account type (#57); the version is parsed from userAgent; background terminals are listed and terminated; child threads open in a read-only sidebar.

Codex tool-channel wiring: both thread/start and thread/resume carry WP4's thread config fragment; for old threads being resumed, the token rotates every time; codex_apps calls go through Codex's own MCP approval, rendered as a generic approval card.

Claude adapter: systemPrompt {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append, snapshot:true} (#7); remove the Codex skill rewriting and handoff concatenation, and user-typed messages carry origin human (#6); blocks are handed over in order — images, then user text — and anything starting with / is always the last block (#19); heic and bmp are converted to PNG at the attachment stage (#58); each user message gets a uuid.

Claude native command pass-through: /goal, /init, /code-review (the menu reads aliases), and /compact <args> go through the send queue verbatim (#1, #14, #4, #51); the result of /code-review is taken from task_notification and result.

Claude goal (see claudeGoal): GoalSnapshot is assembled from 'Goal set:', 'Goal cleared:', 'Stop hook feedback' (which counts turns), and the transcript's goal_status; Stop or Pause = interrupt() then '/goal clear', with the condition stored in meta.goalHeld; Resume re-sends '/goal <condition>'; when the budget hits its limit, interrupt first, then clear, and insert a note; after restartResume and after switching Provider within the same harness, re-apply the goal and permissionMode and insert a note.

Claude Plan round trip: ExitPlanMode approval carries updatedPermissions setMode to return to the tier from before entering, reads EnterPlanMode and system/status, renders the plan body only once, and attaches planFilePath (#12).

Claude multi-agent: every applyFlagSettings carries the current ultracode (#15); availability reads getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable, treated as a version-probe item; perTaskStopAffordance:true, background_tasks_changed and task_* maintain the task table, q.stopTask; the reaper skips sessions with tasks, loops, or cron (#17); includeHookEvents, agentProgressSummaries, onElicitation, multiSelect, denial reasons.

Claude permissions and sessions: the auto tier is gated by supportsAutoMode (#67); always launch with allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, call setPermissionMode within the session, and for the read-only tier, when the allowedTools do not match the launch arguments, resume with new arguments (#28); temporary chats use persistSession:false, do not enter the list, and have a pinned account (#9); forkSession(sid, {upToMessageId}) (#62); enableFileCheckpointing plus rewindFiles(uuid), with dryRun first; edit message is greyed out for chats from before the upgrade; structuredPatch is persisted and accumulated in order, and Bash results use the structured exit code (#68); the fast gate is cached per chat account.

Claude command catalog and diagnostics: supportedCommands (including aliases), init.skills, init.plugins, and commands_changed feed the command catalog; commands that exist only in the interactive implementation are filtered by a static list plus terminal_slash_commands; extras(bin, cwd, account) prefetches with initializationResult().commands; getContextUsage, mcpServerStatus, and toggleMcpServer are provided through IPC. #84: first reproduce, on 7a5bf12, the symptom of old settings being sent to the old process; in claudeStartTurn, when the account recorded for the live session differs from the chat's account, do live.delete(nid) before send, and add a test: after switching accounts, setModel and applyFlagSettings are not sent to the old process, and the new process starts with want; if it cannot be reproduced, record #84 as already fixed by a89acf4 (claude.ts:524 already has the check for differing accounts).

Crash path (shared by both adapters via WP1's state machine): when the harness process exits mid-turn, clear any pending approval cards and mark them "{label} quit", abort the computer use action, release the desktop lock, invalidate the sage-mcp token, keep the queue without resending, and mark the Codex goal paused; the app-server restarts automatically with backoff, turning into a banner after at most 3 attempts.
External-write reconciliation: when a rollout or jsonl changes, reconcile() re-reads the native state; when an external turn is detected running, the Composer is greyed out.

Version policy: versions.min and knownBad; runtime probes (Claude's getSettings, perTaskStopAffordance, origin; Codex's thread config Provider, plugins turning off cua_repl, experimentalFeature/list), where a failure turns off only the corresponding capability; when session startup fails, show an incompatibility notice and an entry point for manually specifying the CLI path.
The tests/conformance/codex and claude scenario suites go into the repo (WP0's probes expanded into regression scenarios), with real sessions recorded and replayed as goldens in CI.
roadmap.exit: Conformance passes in full against the real local CLIs: on Codex, /goal on a new thread calls set only once and starts work, the chat has the user's /goal bubble, after pressing Esc the goal is paused and does not resume, and after quitting and reopening the app the goal is still paused; on Claude, /goal continues over multiple turns until the condition is met, the GoalBar turn count matches the number of Stop hook feedback entries, after pressing Stop the goal shows "paused (kept by MoPilot)", the next unrelated message does not resume the old goal, and Resume starts over; after switching accounts with an active goal on Claude, the goal is re-set with a note; /init generates CLAUDE.md on Claude and AGENTS.md on Codex; /code-review with an image takes effect; ultracode triggers a Workflow and produces a task snapshot, ultracode stays on after changing effort once, stopTask can stop one on its own, and after Stop the background subagent is still there; after Plan approval, execution follows the tier from before entering; effort in two Codex chats does not affect each other; sage_debug.echo reads out the random word on a new Codex thread, a resumed old thread, a Claude subscription, Claude+MoPilot, and Claude+DeepSeek, and the Codex tool list has no cua_repl; killing the app-server and the Claude CLI mid-turn each makes the approval cards disappear and show the reason, and the app-server restarts automatically.

roadmap.title: Generic ACP basic-tier adapter and 8 quirks files
roadmap.goal: dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and Goose are integrated at the basic tier through one generic ACP adapter, promising only basicTierContract; a new harness needs only a registry entry and a quirks file. Depends on WP0 (admission probe results), WP1, WP2 (ACP client fs, terminal callbacks, and the env snapshot), WP3 (account row interface), and WP4 (sessionMcp and the fake agent), and does not depend on WP7.
items: electron/harness/acp.cjs: based on the pinned @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.7.0, supporting only ACP v1 (no compatibility with the v2 draft); launch stdio through disclaim using the env snapshot; the initialize negotiation is mapped into Negotiated.

Session mapping: session/new (with sessionMcp), prompt, cancel, and load used only if declared; session/update is streamed and translated into SageItem (text, thinking, tool calls, diffs, plans, usage); without loadSession, use history:'sage', replaying Sage's own stored transcript on reopen and then session/resume.

Approvals: the options of request_permission are rendered verbatim as a generic approval card (allow_always is shown if present); tools of sage_<nonce> are automatically allow-once. Client reverse calls: fs/read_text_file and fs/write_text_file go through the platform fs, and terminal/* goes through the platform pty.

modes, configOptions, and available_commands_update map into the descriptors; when no command catalog has ever been pushed, /xxx passes through verbatim, and when one has been pushed and the user types a command not in it, show a line of explanation plus "Send as plain text"; undeclared semantics are handled by present().

Stop and unattended: Stop = session/cancel; if a tool_call still arrives afterwards while no prompt is in flight, send cancel once more; tool calls arriving while there is no in-flight user prompt are always treated as unattended.

Quirks framework: quirks/<id>.cjs must provide privacyDefaults and admission {requireToolHandshake, handshakeTimeoutMs:10000, privacyGate}; optional are the mode anchor, plan mode id, model-to-modality table, terminal command filter, resumeCommand (returned only after conformance verification), and versions.

Runtime admission: a harness enters the picker only if initialize succeeds, the sage-mcp handshake succeeds, and the privacy check passes; if any fails, Settings → Other harnesses shows "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot" with the reason, and a new chat cannot be created.
Basic-tier account row: shows ACP authMethods; logins that need a terminal are completed in Settings' embedded terminal and re-detected automatically after exit; failover=none, perChat=false.

quirks: dsh (--patch turns off only session-log-deepseek, the acp row's model changed to deepseek-flash; DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; a --dump-config privacy gate before launch, refusing to start if validation fails; single-process workspace-write plus ask; DSH_HOME is not isolated and customSkillDirs is not added), opencode (opencode acp, the user's own provider and agent config is left untouched), kimi (kimi acp, /goal, /swarm, /init, plan config, device code login), qwen (qwen --acp, approval-mode mapping), copilot (copilot --acp, standard, plan, autopilot mapping), cursor (agent acp, cursor/* extension methods mapped to the plan card and question card, with the read-only tier also set under plan), gemini (gemini --acp, unstable_setSessionModel, GEMINI.md), goose (goose acp).

Designs removed: dsh.cjs, dsh multi-process tier switching, DSH_HOME isolation and distribution, dsh goal tool parsing and skill scanning, opencode.cjs, serve lifecycle, the v2 SDK, SSE translation, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT merging, the four-tier agent variants, and the opencode plugin.
tests/conformance/acp-<id>: the contract scenarios for each quirks file; recorded sessions from at least two harnesses are replayed as goldens in CI.
roadmap.exit: Each of the 8 basic-tier harnesses either passes admission and completes every item in basicTierContract.guaranteed (create, send, streaming, approval, cancel, resume after restart, one desktop task, one browser task), or shows "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot" with the reason stated; Kimi's /goal pass-through works; typing /xxx in a dsh chat sends the text verbatim to dsh; a dsh packet capture confirms the request body has no session log, and after the patch is deliberately broken dsh refuses to start; a tool call arriving when there is no user prompt is treated as unattended.

roadmap.title: Semantic command layer, UI, and Settings information architecture
roadmap.goal: All entry points are driven by descriptors and displayed by one set of presentation rules; the init and shell polyfills take effect only for first-class harnesses; Settings is rearranged under the new information architecture; the scheduler and the quit gate land here; the UI stays Codex-style, with the English copy table as the source of truth for wording. Depends on WP1, WP2, WP3, WP4 (approval model), WP5, and WP6.
items: useCaps(chatId), useSession(chatId), runSemantic(chatId, cap, args); components are replaced file by file (select.ts, the rest of store.ts, HarnessSettings, HarnessPicker, then Composer, Sidebar, ThreadView, Items, TitleBar), and Codex-only pages move to components/harness/codex/*; the boundary test counts go to zero.

CommandRegistry: three CommandProviders, with typing and the menu from the same source, matched by command-name prefix, and a command with the same name as a native one is passed through first (#20); a Claude thread lists only Claude's skills and commands, and selecting one inserts '/name ' (#5); /clear, /reset, and /new map to creating a new chat, and /exit is forbidden (#52); an intercepted command takes the attachments with it or clears them, and command execution catches errors (#53); /rename goes through renameThread (#16); unknown commands on a Codex thread get a prompt under a narrow rule; the "Sage" group in the / menu is renamed App.

Only two polyfill engines remain, for first-class harnesses only: init (Codex writes AGENTS.md, asking first if it already exists; when CLAUDE.md exists, offer "let Codex read it too") and shell (Claude's '!' runs through the platform pty, with the output as an attachment).

Shared components: GoalBar (drawn from controls, the Codex soft-budget explanation, Claude's "by MoPilot" pause and limit, the note at the limit), sidebar goal icon; the Plan chip reads SessionState and does not change when an approval card appears (#3); a plan approval card shared by Codex and Claude; the task panel with Workflow, Agent, Skill, and Monitor cards, with Codex child threads opening in a read-only sidebar (#18), and a second Esc within 2 seconds confirming stop-all; the ApprovalRequest card (label taken from the originating segment, 1/2/3 shortcuts, a reason attached to a denial, hold ⌘↩ for one second to confirm); the review result card (PR target, with Claude's result as Markdown inside the card frame); command output styling.

Composer: one status bar (controlling the computer > waiting for approval > goal > background tasks) and one "next message" chip slot; the permission menu anchors on the main label, with a second line for the native name and differences, adds the read-only item (#27), and has "This chat only" at the bottom; the model picker is harness · provider · model, dropping the middle level when there is only one Provider, plus the scope rules and a one-time notice after the upgrade.

SwitchSheet: three columns; settle pendingSwitch first and then route /goal (#11); the Changes column always lists the account and data destination, effort mapping, multi-agent (not migrated by default), and permissions; the user chooses whether queued messages are sent along with the switch or left behind; the rules for carrying a goal over; the "Back on Codex · Caught up on N messages" divider when switching back; switching to a basic-tier harness offers only "New chat with summary".

Routing: the chip states the target harness, the account, and "this is a new chat"; a confirmation box is used the first time each user crosses vendors; voice routing offers "include a summary of this chat".

Entry-point fixes: Feedback appears only on Codex segments and uses nativeOf, and likes on Claude replies go only to MoPilot telemetry (#8); Status uses one template that reads the current segment, and the MCP submenu fetches data per segment (#21); the + menu lists only the current harness's plugins, Claude lists init.plugins, and Try now on the Plugins page is greyed out according to the default harness (#22); the voice hotkey and button read the same voiceChat capability and do not first create an empty chat (#23); wording is interpolated from info.label, doc links follow docsUrl, places unrelated to a harness say MoPilot, and the Mini placeholder, the Plugins and Skills subtitles, and the Browser options are all changed together (#54); "Use API key" jumps to Accounts & billing, and the CLI path can be picked manually (#55).

Settings information architecture: Accounts & billing in one place (the WP3 page); one page per first-class harness, divided into Overview, Models, Instructions & memory, Extensions, and Advanced sections; Other harnesses is one page holding all basic-tier harnesses; Built-in tools (Computer use, Browser, Voice & dictation); Connections (SSH); Applies to is shown only when it is not "all harnesses", and a snapshot generated from the Settings descriptors goes into npm test; at release the sidebar has no more than 21 items and the total Row count is no more than today's plus 10; SECTION_ALIAS keeps old links.

Extensions: Codex is editable, the MCP editor saves with merge, and user servers also render Authenticate (#45); Codex's Plugins, MCP, Skills, Hooks, Control this Mac, and Experimental move to the Codex page (#31); Import is renamed "Import to Codex", and syncImports passes the cwds of known projects (#36); the remoteControl method names change to client/list and client/revoke, and Add goes through pairing/start and pairing/status (#47); Approval policy and Sandbox are labeled "Only affects Codex outside MoPilot" (#30). Claude: the same MCP form runs 'claude mcp add --scope user …' on save (previewing the command first); plugins are listed read-only, with "Install with claude plugin…" (embedded terminal with the command prefilled); hooks are listed read-only with Open settings.json. The top of the Plugins and Customize pages is tabbed by first-class harness.

Dead settings: wire up showReasoning, confirmClose (hooked to this work package's quit gate), numberShortcuts, draftPRs (gh pr create --draft), and commitInstructions (as the prompt when generating commit messages); delete language, prMergeMethod, forcePush, autoMerge, autoMergeInstructions, and the Control other devices placeholder page, with the release notes saying "These settings never took effect and were removed".

Basic-tier presentation: the Basic badge and hover in the picker ("Limited · Chat, approvals, computer and browser control work. Goal, plan and review work only if {label} has them. See what's different"), linking to this harness's list of differences; the compatibility table shows "unverified" per capability.
English copy table: all strings for the Why text, GoalBar, SwitchSheet, routing, computer use, and notifications are written as key-values by layer and code, with the Chinese as comments (see copy).

Scheduler (moved from WP2): tasks are stored in userData/automations, Run with lists only Codex and Claude Code, recording harness, instance, model, effort, cwd, whether computer control is allowed (off by default) and the app list, and the handling when approval is needed (Wait and notify or Skip this run, marked needs attention if not handled within 1 hour); scheduling and Run now go through the same function, via adapter.start/send (#37); the Scheduled page subtitle is "Runs on this Mac".
