roadmap.title: Computer use, browser control, and vision fallback
roadmap.goal: Every harness (including basic-tier ones), every login and billing mode, and every model (including text-only models) can control the browser and the desktop, with the same authorization, takeover, emergency stop, and safety floor. Depends on WP0 (helper prototype and signing chain), WP2 (pty and notifications), WP4 (channels), WP5 and WP6 (real-world testing of each harness's channel), and WP7 (approval card, status bar, Settings pages).
items: Browser: Sage acts as an MCP client proxying the pinned @playwright/mcp 0.0.83 --extension (run by a utilityProcess), with one instance and one tab group per chat and the token stored in the keychain; site permissions are read-only or read-write, and downloads and uploads are authorized separately, all enforced at the proxy layer; Claude always passes extraArgs {'no-chrome': null}; users who had Claude in Chrome on before the upgrade see a one-time migration notice; Built-in tools → Browser has two channels, with an install guide and a connection test (including an extension version check).
Built-in BrowserPanel: webContents.debugger over CDP, a separate partition, nodeIntegration off, no preload, with code asserting that the CDP target is not the app UI's webContents.

Production helper: MoPilot Computer Use.app (Swift, LSUIElement, launched via LaunchServices) with a native CGEvent / AX / ScreenCaptureKit implementation (no embedded cua-driver, decision WP8-3); accepts only connections whose audit-token pid equals the registered main pid and whose signature matches; permission probing. Signing chain: separate entitlements, signed inside-out, packaged via extraResource; development builds sign the helper with a fixed development certificate; release.yml adds helper build and verification. The disclaim launcher is wired in: codex app-server, the claude CLI, ACP agents, and pty are all launched through it.

Safety floor (enforced inside the helper): a no-go zone table; the event tap drops all synthetic events landing on MoPilot windows, letting system assistive technologies (Voice Control, Switch Control) through by source pid; approval cards and permission settings accept only human-initiated input; SCContentFilter screenshots exclude our own windows and the glow layer, with the long edge no more than 2000px.

Authorization: card buttons Allow once / Allow in this chat / Always allow, with levels View only / Click / Full control; grants persist per chat, and Always allow writes into the global list; the permission anchor's authorization table; irreversible action categories are confirmed in every mode.

Unattended rules: tool calls from a turn that the user did not just initiate (goal continuation, a /goal re-sent after an account switch, scheduled tasks, background tasks, sub-agents), after 10 minutes without physical input, or arriving on a basic-tier harness when there is no user prompt, may use only apps on the chat list and the global list; when a new authorization is needed, reject the call, pause the goal (Codex set paused then interrupt, Claude interrupt then '/goal clear', basic tier cancel), and send one notification.

The global desktop lock lives in the helper (one per user, shared by multiple profiles, with the holder shown in the tray); takeover rules: on detecting physical input, immediately pause the current action and release the lock, and the activity bar shows "You took over. The agent is paused · Resume"; only an Esc from a HID source counts; if the permission needed for emergency stop is missing, refuse to start and show a guide card; the tray always has "Stop controlling your Mac"; three layers of indication (tray, glow on the target window, chat activity bar).

Codex native tools: confirm cua_repl is turned off per thread; node_repl is turned off or marked "needs verification" according to the X14 result; when codex_apps cannot be turned off, it goes through Codex's MCP approval and is not auto-approved when unattended; if cua_repl ever appears, its elicitation is intercepted and always rejected, with a line of explanation in the chat.

Vision fallback: when the model's input does not include image, give only the element table and inject locate and describe, backed by a vision model from the same Provider or a vision model on MoPilot credits, asking for consent the first time vendors are crossed; when a basic-tier modality is unknown, give both; with no vision backend at all, work from AX plus a local Vision OCR element table, without blocking.
Telemetry: CU tool calls record only the name and status, and screenshots, the AX tree, and type and clipboard arguments are not uploaded; the local operation log stays on this machine only.

Local dictation: add SFSpeechRecognizer to the helper and add NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription to Info.plist; the dictation engine interface supports local, ChatGPT, and MoPilot; users already using ChatGPT dictation before the upgrade keep their existing engine.

Built-in tools → Computer use: permission status, the chat list and global list, the no-go zone table, the engine version, and a notice that Screen Recording needs re-confirming roughly monthly; a guide card on first use (explaining what the helper is, then jumping to System Settings).
roadmap.exit: On a release-signed build, Codex+ChatGPT, Codex+MoPilot, Claude subscription, Claude+MoPilot, Claude+DeepSeek, Claude+a text-only custom endpoint, and every admitted basic-tier harness all complete the same set of browser tasks and desktop tasks; actions are rejected in the read-only tier; each action is asked about only once; the agent fails to click a MoPilot approval card or to open the privacy panel; neither ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nor a direct connection to the helper socket can control the desktop; moving the mouse mid-operation pauses the agent immediately; with two profiles running at the same time, only one agent is controlling at any moment; when cross-vendor consent is refused and there is no MoPilot, a text-only model completes the task with the AX+OCR element table; when a goal continuation needs a new authorization, the goal pauses and one notification arrives; an Always allow app needs no re-authorization after a restart; the BrowserPanel's CDP cannot reach the app's own webContents; no cua_repl appears in Codex segments.

roadmap.title: MoPilot gateway wrap-up, app identity, updates, and privacy
roadmap.goal: The gateway's optional DeepSeek upstream and transcription route; app identity, updates, consent, cookies, and shortcut wrap-up; migration notes in the release notes. Depends on WP0 (gateway capability table), WP1 (migration framework), WP3 (Provider and accounts), and WP7 (quit gate).
items: The gateway adds a DeepSeek upstream (Anthropic wire, routed by deepseek-*, accepting x-api-key and Bearer, serving only Claude Code·MoPilot, optional) and a transcription route, and the pricing table adds DeepSeek and transcription prices (new migration).

Branding leftovers: the application menu's Quit item, the tray title and tooltip, Show Codex, and the name, title, and version of the app-server clientInfo switch to APP_NAME and the app version (main.cjs:270-282, 356, #82); About's Codex CLI path takes the binary actually launched (#56). The rename, bundle id, and microphone description of #48 were already done by #16 (main.cjs:904, scripts/package.mjs:22-23, 43), and the remaining menu and tray work is merged into #82.

Updates: preference sync moves to the App root component, and configure rebuilds the timer only when the value changes (#77); scheduled checks are silent and run only from /Applications, "Move to Applications" appears only on manual checks and remembers Not Now, and supported is determined by the signature check (#78); Restart to update goes through WP7's quit gate.

Consent: PUT only when the user actually changes it; on login merge by taking the stricter side and write the account value back to local prefs; the web toggle covers all upload types (#80); telemetry batches add versions for the codex, claude, and admitted basic-tier kinds.

Built-in browser cookies: on first launch, first decrypt with the old "Codex Safe Storage" keychain item and then re-encrypt with the new key; back up the Cookies database first, and on failure tell the user the built-in browser needs to be logged in again (#83).
Shortcuts: buildMenu reads keybindings to generate accelerators and rebuilds the menu after a rebind; comboFromEvent maps Semicolon and similar keys through e.code (#60).

Migration entries for the release notes: Claude in Chrome is replaced by Your Chrome in Built-in tools; existing dictation engines and billing modes do not change because of the upgrade; the deleted dead settings; likes on Claude replies go only to MoPilot telemetry; the scope of the basic tier.
roadmap.exit: A turn with web search is billed per call; if the DeepSeek upstream ships, Claude Code·MoPilot completes a turn with deepseek-flash; with a turn running, Restart to update first lists what will be stopped; outside /Applications the background check does not show a dialog; after turning sharing off on the web, restarting the desktop app does not change it back; Codex no longer appears in the tray and menu; after rebinding New Chat, the old key stops working; site logins in the built-in browser are still there after the upgrade, with a notice on failure.

roadmap.title: Conformance tests, capability matrices, and release acceptance
roadmap.goal: Pin every harness's behavior into repeatable checks, generate two capability matrices, pass through two dogfood release rings, then complete all acceptance on the real release build and ship everything together. Depends on all earlier work packages.
items: tests/conformance: one scenario suite per harness, run by the release owner on this machine with a dedicated test account against the real CLI, with results written to tests/conformance/results/<kind>@<version>.json; first-class harnesses run all scenarios, basic-tier harnesses run only the contract scenarios; versions.min and knownBad are written into StaticInfo according to the results.

Generate two matrices from the bindings and conformance results: the full-semantics matrix for first-class harnesses, and the contract items plus admission results for basic-tier harnesses. docs/harness-matrix.md and Settings' compatibility table (including the "control source" column) are both generated from it.
acceptance A1–A27 and the 5 journeys in newJourneys are written as a scripted checklist that can be ticked off item by item.

Two release rings: Ring 0 (two engineers and the product owner, dogfood channel) and Ring 1 (10–30 trusted users, beta channel by invitation), with observation periods of no less than 5 and 10 working days respectively.

On the real Electron release build (a signed and notarized artifact with MOPILOT_SIGN_IDENTITY set, arm64 and x64), run all acceptance and the 27 journeys (22 existing plus 5 new); TCC and auto-update are verified only on release builds.
Check the 84 issues in issueCoverage one by one, each with a record in the corresponding work package's exit checks.

The release notes state where data goes (MoPilot gateway, DeepSeek, dsh session logs turned off, the cross-vendor path of vision fallback, the dictation engine), the scope of the basic tier, and the migration entries; a third-party license list is attached in the app.
roadmap.exit: All acceptance passes; the 84 issues are each verified closed; the two generated matrices match the UI presentation; once go/no-go passes, roll out 10% → 50% → 100%.

acceptance: A1 Only Claude Code installed (codex binary moved away): first launch, logging in from Settings, creating a projectless chat, terminal, @ files, ⌘K, scheduled tasks, and saving CLAUDE.md can all be completed, and the UI has no "Couldn't connect to Codex".

A2 Only one basic-tier harness installed (Kimi Code, or dsh installed by the user): the welcome page lists it (with a Basic badge) and the one-click install of Claude Code; log in in the embedded terminal; create a chat, approvals, cancel, and history intact after restart; terminal, @ files, and ⌘K work; for dsh, a packet capture confirms the request body carries no session log, and confirms dsh refuses to start after the patch is deliberately broken.

A3 Goal: set the goal "make npm test fully pass" on each of Codex and Claude Code. Codex: the user's /goal bubble appears in the chat, work starts after a single set, the GoalBar can pause, resume, and change the budget and states that the budget is a soft limit, after pressing Esc the goal is paused and does not resume, and after complete there is no Resume; when quitting the app with an active Codex goal and reopening it, the goal shows paused and does not resume automatically. Claude: the GoalBar turn count equals the number of Stop hook feedback entries, after pressing Stop it shows "Goal paused (kept by MoPilot)", then sending an unrelated message does not resume the old goal, and after Resume it starts over with the turn count from 0; at the limit set by Sage it stops first, then clears and inserts a note; when an account switch (restartResume) happens with an active goal, the goal is re-set with a note. Kimi's /goal is passed through and displayed in the command output style (in A16).

A4 Plan: open Plan on each of Codex and Claude and send a requirement; after a question card or approval card appears midway the Plan chip does not go out; the same plan card appears on both sides (using the last message when the Codex model produces no plan item), and after approval execution follows the tier from before entering. In a Kimi chat the Plan chip appears only when quirks marks a plan mode.

A5 Multi-agent: turn on Ultra on Codex (appearing only when the model has ultra) and ultracode on Claude and trigger multi-agent once each; the Workflow or Agent card shows the subtasks and each can be stopped individually; after changing effort once on Claude, ultracode is still on; after pressing Stop, background subagents keep running, and pressing Esc again within 2 seconds stops everything.

A6 Review: Codex review/start (inline) and Claude's /code-review with a screenshot both render as a review result card (Claude's as Markdown inside the card frame); both sides can review a Pull request.

A7 Init, compact, skills: /init generates CLAUDE.md on Claude and AGENTS.md on Codex (asking first if one already exists; when the other file already exists, the first option is to have it read that one); Compact is available on Codex and Claude, with the divider stating it was manual; the / menu of both first-class harnesses lists its own skills, and selecting one invokes the skill.

A8 Computer use: Codex (ChatGPT, MoPilot), Claude (subscription, MoPilot, DeepSeek), and every admitted basic-tier harness each write a line in Notes; the authorization cards are exactly the same; clicks are rejected in the read-only tier; pressing Esc stops immediately and releases the desktop lock; moving the mouse mid-operation pauses the agent immediately; the native cua_repl is not used in Codex segments (only Sage's authorization card appears).

A9 Browser: Codex and Claude Code each use "Your Chrome" to open a logged-in site and read out the title, and open a localhost page in the built-in browser and take a screenshot; with site permission read-only, filling a form is rejected; the Claude session launch arguments include --no-chrome. Browser tasks for basic-tier harnesses are in A16.

A10 Text-only model: Claude Code configured with a text-only custom endpoint completes the same desktop task, the activity bar shows which vision model did the recognition, and there is a consent prompt the first time vendors are crossed; when consent is refused and there is no MoPilot, the task still completes with the AX+OCR element table.

A11 Security: the agent tries to click a MoPilot approval card, open Privacy & Security in System Settings, and type into a password field, all of which fail and are recorded in the operation timeline; CU screenshots and the AX tree do not appear in telemetry upload batches; with an MCP server named sage committed to the repo, its tools are not auto-allowed; running the MoPilot binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 has no effect; the agent's bash cannot obtain credentials that connect directly to the helper or main socket; macOS Voice Control can approve an approval card.

A12 Unattended: on each of Codex and Claude, a goal needs authorization for a new app while continuing; the goal pauses and only one notification arrives, and after opening it, the user authorizes and resumes; a tool call initiated by a basic-tier harness with no user prompt is rejected as unattended; when three chats need attention at the same time, notifications merge into "3 chats need you".

A13 Accounts and MoPilot: a Claude turn running while logging in or out of MoPilot is not interrupted; a user with only one ChatGPT account still sees the single-account view after logging in to MoPilot; ~/.codex/auth.json is unchanged before and after; two chats in the same harness use a subscription and MoPilot credits respectively; when the subscription quota runs out only a "Continue on MoPilot credits" button appears, with no automatic cross-Provider move, and a confirmation is asked before switching to an API key of the same Provider; accounts can be changed in only one place, Accounts & billing; the account area of a basic-tier harness shows only the harness's own login, with no MoPilot and no per-chat account selection.

A14 Switching: a Codex chat with an active goal switched to Claude, where the SwitchSheet states that the goal is paused, the account and data destination, the effort mapping, and permission changes, and multi-agent is not migrated by default; after the switch the old Codex thread no longer continues; typing /goal while in the pendingSwitch state lands the goal on the new segment; switching from Claude to Codex and back, the original Claude session is restored, only the delta is re-sent, and the divider states how many messages were caught up; switching from Claude to a basic-tier harness offers only "New chat with summary".

A15 Multi-window: archiving and pinning in two windows at the same time lose nothing; a single computer use click executes only once; a new window can open Codex, Claude, and basic-tier chats; a window newly opened mid-turn shows the same Plan, goal, and approval cards; two windows sending to the same chat at the same time queue it only once and do not send twice.

A16 Basic tier: for each installed one among dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and Goose, either it passes admission and completes all items of basicTierContract.guaranteed (create, send, streaming, approval, cancel, resume after restart, one desktop task, one browser task), or it shows "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot" with the reason; for those that push a command catalog (Kimi /goal, opencode /review, etc.), typed text passes through verbatim and works.

A17 Presentation rules: the + menu of a Claude chat does not list Codex plugins; pressing the voice hotkey in a Kimi chat offers current-chat speech choices with explicit providers; under Claude Code·DeepSeek ⚡ is greyed out with the provider reason; typing a /xxx not in Kimi's command catalog in a Kimi chat shows a line of explanation and "Send as plain text"; typing /xxx in a dsh chat sends the text verbatim to dsh.

A18 Temporary chats: temporary chats on Codex and Claude do not appear in the sidebar; a Claude temporary chat hitting an exhausted quota does not switch accounts and does not lose context; when the default harness is a basic-tier one, pressing ⇧⌘N shows a chip stating which first-class harness and account will be used, and it can be undone.

A19 Scheduled tasks: run one each on Codex and Claude; Run with lists only these two, and the model and effort take effect as set on the task; tasks do not allow computer control by default, and after turning the switch on only apps in the list are allowed; when unattended and an ordinary approval is hit, it waits per "Wait and notify", and is marked needs attention if not handled within 1 hour.

A20 Updates and quit: with a running turn, a background Workflow, or an active goal, Restart to update and Quit first list what will be stopped, and after quitting the Codex goal is paused; after switching to Beta in About, an immediate check uses the Beta source; outside /Applications the background check does not show a dialog.

A21 Settings: Applies to matches the generated snapshot and is shown only when it is not "all harnesses"; the sidebar has no more than 21 items and the total Row count is no more than today's plus 10; Approval policy on the Codex page is labeled "Only affects Codex outside MoPilot"; Control this Mac lists devices and can pair; after saving a Codex MCP edit, hand-written keys are still there; adding an MCP server on the Claude page first previews the claude mcp add command; there are no settings without a reader.

A22 Upgrade and downgrade: upgrading from 7a5bf12 (with archived and pinned Claude chats, multi-segment chats, worktreeOf), data is intact; after killing the process mid-migration and restarting, data is intact; after installing 7a5bf12 again, all old data is still there (except new changes made after the migration); users who had Claude in Chrome on before the upgrade see a one-time migration notice; existing billing modes and dictation engines are not changed.

A23 Harness crash mid-turn: killing the app-server, the Claude CLI process, and a basic-tier process in turn during a turn: pending approval cards disappear and show the reason, the desktop lock is released, queued messages are kept, and the Codex goal is paused; the app-server restarts automatically.

A24 CLI version drift: swap the Claude CLI for a version that has not been verified but is above the minimum version: chats work as usual, entry points show no "needs verification" badge, and capabilities whose probe fails (for example the ultracode switch when getSettings does not exist) are greyed out individually with a reason; swap the Claude CLI for a known-bad version: an incompatibility notice and an entry point for manually specifying the path are shown; move the Codex binary away: only Codex entry points are affected.

A25 Regression items for first-class harnesses: model/effort of two Codex chats do not affect each other (#29); Copy resume command works in a terminal (#69); on export each segment is labeled with the right harness (#61); Feedback appears only on Codex segments (#8); edit message goes through rewind, and for Claude chats from before the upgrade edit message is greyed out with a reason (#68); Fork chat from here starts from that message (#62); Claude sessions use the claude_code preset system prompt (#7); when launched from the Dock, CLAUDE_CODE_* of the shell Provider takes effect (#35); with Notifications set to Never, no more notifications are received (#59).

A26 New user: on a Mac with neither Codex nor Claude Code installed and only a MoPilot account, sends the first message through the three welcome-page steps (choose MoPilot credits, one-click install of Claude Code, choose the default harness), with no claude.ai login throughout and no need to open a terminal manually.

A27 The 5 new P0 journeys (newJourneys: set a goal and walk away, plan first then execute, control a Mac app, use my Chrome, scheduled task when nobody is there) are walked through step by step on Codex and Claude Code.

newJourneys.title: Set a goal, walk away, come back and check
codex: 1. In a Codex chat, type /goal make npm test fully pass and press Enter: the user's /goal bubble appears in the chat, the GoalBar appears, and the budget reads "token budget (soft, checked between turns)".
2. Switch to another app and walk away for 20 minutes; when the thread is idle the server continues automatically.
3. Meanwhile the agent needs to control an app that was never authorized: the call is rejected, the goal does set paused then interrupt, and only one notification is sent.
4. Come back and click the notification: the chat opens, the sidebar chat row has a goal icon, the GoalBar shows paused and the tokens used, and the authorization card is right below.
5. After authorizing, click Resume goal and the goal continues; when done, one "Goal complete" notification arrives, and the GoalBar has only Clear left.
6. Quit the app and reopen it (when the goal was still active): the quit gate already did set paused, the GoalBar shows paused, and nothing resumed while the user was away.
claude: 1. In a Claude chat, type /goal make npm test fully pass and press Enter: the command output style shows "Goal set: …", and the GoalBar shows "round 0".
2. Walk away for 20 minutes; Claude keeps working within one turn, each Stop hook feedback is folded into "Goal check #n: …", and the GoalBar turn count follows.

3. Meanwhile the Max quota runs out and it switches automatically to the second subscription account: Sage re-applies permissionMode and re-sends '/goal <condition>', and inserts the note "Max limit reached. Continued on b@x.com · Goal and plan mode carried over".
4. At the 30-round limit set by Sage (metered billing account): interrupt first, then /goal clear, with the note "Reached the limit (30 rounds). Goal paused" and one notification.
5. Come back and click [10 more rounds] or Resume: Sage re-sends /goal, and the GoalBar states that the round count restarts.
6. Wanting to do something else first midway: press Stop, the GoalBar shows "Goal paused (kept by MoPilot)", then ask an unrelated question and Claude does not resume the old goal.

newJourneys.title: Plan first, then execute (including mid-run approval)
codex: 1. Shift+Tab turns on the Plan chip, send a requirement; thread/settings/updated shows mode plan.
2. An approval card appears while the model reads a file, and the Plan chip does not go out; approve with the number key 1.
3. The turn ends: the plan card appears (plan item; the last message when the model produces none), and the body is rendered only once.
4. Click "Implement this plan ▾" and choose Ask for approval: Sage switches back to default and sends the execution.
5. Write-file approvals during execution appear as usual; the Diff panel shows this turn's changes.
6. Edit the first message: it goes through thread/revert, back to before that turn.
claude: 1. Shift+Tab turns on the Plan chip: setPermissionMode('plan'), and system/status shows plan.
2. The model asks a choice via a question card, and the Plan chip does not change; continue after choosing.
3. The model calls ExitPlanMode: the plan card renders once from the plan field, with the plan file path attached.
4. Click "Implement this plan ▾" and choose Accept edits: the approval carries updatedPermissions setMode, returning to the execution tier.
5. Execute; the status bar shows approval while waiting for approval, and after it ends the Diff panel shows changes accumulated in order.
6. Edit the previous message: rewindFiles first lists the files that would be restored, and rolls back after confirmation.

newJourneys.title: Have the agent control a Mac app (first authorization, takeover mid-operation, emergency stop)
codex: 1. The first time the agent is asked to "write a line in Notes": a guide card appears first, explaining what MoPilot Computer Use is, and clicking Open System Settings grants Accessibility and Screen Recording.
2. The authorization card "Codex wants to control Notes": choose Click, Allow in this chat.
3. The activity bar "Controlling Notes · Move the mouse to take over · Esc to stop", the Notes window glows, and the tray has Stop controlling your Mac.
4. Move the mouse mid-operation: the agent pauses immediately, the activity bar shows "You took over. The agent is paused · Resume", and clicking Resume continues.
5. Press Esc again: the action aborts and the desktop lock is released.
6. Another chat asks for control at the same time: the activity bar shows "Waiting: another chat is controlling your Mac · View". Codex's tool list has no cua_repl.
claude: 1. For the same request, if the authorization guide has already been completed, the authorization card "Claude Code wants to control Notes" appears directly (exactly the same as Codex).
2. Sage tools are available directly without going through ToolSearch (alwaysLoad), and canUseTool no longer pops a second generic card.
3. The activity bar, glow, and tray are the same as Codex.
4. Move the mouse to take over, Resume to continue.
5. Esc emergency stop, lock released.
6. In the read-only tier, ask it to click: the call is rejected and the model receives the reason.

newJourneys.title: Use my Chrome to complete a task on a logged-in site
codex: 1. Built-in tools → Browser → Your Chrome: install the Playwright extension following the guide, and the connection test passes (including the extension version check).
2. In a Codex chat, have the agent open a logged-in site and read out the page title.
3. The first time this site is visited, a site permission card appears: choose read-only.
4. Have it fill in a form: the call is rejected, with a notice that read-write permission is needed; after changing to read-write it completes.
5. This chat's tabs are in a separate tab group, and when the chat is closed the tab group closes.
claude: 1. The same connection, with no claude.ai login needed; the session launch arguments include --no-chrome.
2. Have the agent open the same logged-in site and read out the title.
3. The site permission card is the same as Codex's and is remembered per site.
4. The form fill is rejected, and completes after changing to read-write.
5. A user who had Claude in Chrome on before the upgrade sees a one-time notice the first time they enter the Browser page.

newJourneys.title: A scheduled task needs a new authorization when nobody is there
codex: 1. Scheduled → New task: Run with Codex, turn on Allow computer control, put only Notes in the app list, and choose Wait and notify when approval is needed.
2. At the scheduled time the user is away: this turn is handled as unattended.
3. The agent wants to control Calendar (not in the list): the call is rejected, the model receives the reason, the task chat gets a note, and only one notification is sent.
4. The agent needs an ordinary command approval: wait and notify; if not handled within 1 hour, this run is marked needs attention.
5. Come back and click the notification: authorize Calendar or deny it, and then Run now to run it once more.
claude: 1. The same task with Run with Claude Code, with the model and effort per the task settings.
2. Runs at the scheduled time; the trigger message does not carry origin human.
3. Wants to control Calendar: rejected, one notification.
4. Ordinary approval waits and notifies, marked needs attention after 1 hour.
5. Come back and handle it, then Run now; background tasks in the session are not killed by the reaper.

issueCoverage.note: release() already checks active goals and keeps the lease (store.ts:744-752), so it is not on the fix list; what needs fixing is doing set paused before interrupt (store.ts:1489).
The nativeOf part was already fixed by withLease at store.ts:1612; what remains is routing by harness, and review/start being fixed to delivery:"inline", ignoring prefs.reviewDelivery.

openQuestions: Decision: the only first-class harnesses are Codex and Claude Code; dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and Goose are all basic tier, go through generic ACP plus quirks, and appear in the picker only after passing runtime admission. Premise: the basic-tier contract contains only the core session journey, native commands and mode pass-through, computer use, and the browser.

Decision: opencode goes through opencode acp as a basic-tier harness, not opencode serve. Premise: the basic tier requires only the core journey and the shared tools; ACP's session/new mcpServers actually solves the problem that serve can inject MCP only at the instance level; the lost diff, revert, share, todo, and provider login are not in the basic-tier contract.

Decision: dsh is a basic-tier harness installed by the user; Sage does not distribute it, pin its version, or isolate DSH_HOME, and adds only --patch (turning off session-log-deepseek, changing the acp row's model to deepseek-flash) and DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; before launch, --dump-config verifies that session logging is off, and launch is refused if the check fails. Premise: session logs are uploaded by default up to 8 MiB, which is a privacy floor that must be turned off at every tier, and must fail closed.

Decision: goal is provided only at the first-class tier (Codex rpc, Claude passthrough); Claude's pause and round limit are held by Sage (interrupt() then '/goal clear', with Resume re-sending), satisfying the three polyfill criteria; if a basic-tier harness has a native /goal it is passed through, otherwise it is not provided. No goalLoop and no goal_report. Premise: in Claude 2.1.295 the goal loop was measured to run within a single turn, the goal stays active after Stop, a /goal clear queued during the loop waits until the loop ends, and there are no pause or budget subcommands.

Decision: goal budget defaults: goals on subscription accounts have no limit; under metered billing (API key, MoPilot credits, DeepSeek key), Codex defaults to tokenBudget 2M (a soft limit, settled per turn, stated in the UI) and Claude defaults to 30 rounds (Sage counts Stop hook feedback, and the UI is labeled "Limit set by MoPilot"); both can be changed in settings; when switching to a metered-billing Provider, the SwitchSheet's Changes column states the new budget. Premise: unattended autonomous work under metered billing keeps spending money, so the user must be able to see the limit; spending on subscription accounts is already capped by the plan quota.

Decision: a first-class harness's model, effort, and speed tier are saved per chat, with each instance additionally storing new-chat defaults; choosing on the new-chat page changes the defaults, while choosing in an existing chat changes only that chat; the first time the model is changed in a Codex chat after the upgrade, a one-time notice is shown. Codex therefore differs from the official Codex desktop's global behavior. Premise: the two first-class harnesses in the same app must behave consistently.

Decision: scheduled tasks and projects follow MoPilot's userData and support only Codex and Claude Code; sharing with the official Codex app is a dual-write the user turns on explicitly. Premise: the official app does not recognize the harness field and would run other harnesses' tasks as Codex tasks.

Decision: Claude and basic-tier segments provide no feedback upload and the entry point is hidden; Codex segments keep using feedback/upload as before; likes on Claude replies go only to MoPilot's own telemetry (when the user has consented). Premise: never upload chats across vendors.

Decision: dictation defaults to macOS local recognition for new users; users already using ChatGPT transcription before the upgrade keep their existing engine; ChatGPT-account transcription or MoPilot-credits transcription is optional, and the settings page states where the audio goes. Premise: local recognition needs no account; the Chinese and punctuation quality for existing users must not drop because of the upgrade.

Decision: for new users of the distributed version, the default billing path is MoPilot credits or the user's own API key; Claude subscription login and ChatGPT login are kept, and statements like "personal use" are changed to neutral text in a hover; the billing mode of existing users never changes because of an upgrade.

Decision: DeepSeek offers only deepseek-flash, without listing deepseek-v4-pro separately; the recommended path is Claude Code plus the DeepSeek Provider; the text-only fallback path is built anyway, serving GLM text models, Kimi K2, and users' own text-only endpoints. Premise: DeepSeek has already routed v4-pro to V4.1 Flash and plans to retire it.

Decision: no Codex·DeepSeek is provided; Codex's thread-level Provider (thread/start.modelProvider plus the thread config's model_providers.<id>, with credentials only through auth.command) serves only MoPilot and custom Responses endpoints, on the main branch. codex-cli 0.162 was measured to accept model_providers in the thread config (both nested and dotted keys work), so the fallback of "put it in the app-server launch arguments and restart when the definition changes" is not needed. auth.command executes immediately at thread/start, so Sage's key helper must be fast (reading the keychain cache, returning within 200ms) and non-interactive, and exit non-zero immediately on failure.

Decision: the worktree default branch prefix is mopilot/, the root directory is ~/.mopilot/worktrees, and the projectless directory is ~/Documents/MoPilot; existing settings and existing worktrees are not migrated. Premise: the product name has been settled as MoPilot and will not change again.

Decision: conformance tests are run by the release owner on this machine with a dedicated test account against the real CLIs, one full run before each release ring, and once a week during Ring 1 against the latest stable versions of Claude Code and Codex, with results checked in; golden replays of recorded sessions and the boundary test run on every PR in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, macos-14). The previous version's statement that "the repo has no CI" was wrong. Premise: real-CLI scenarios consume quota, and the project convention requires verifying in the real Electron app.

Decision (revised): Claude Code uses the vendor-native Claude in Chrome the way the official Claude Code does. A user session passes extraArgs {chrome: null} only when the remote switch native.claude.chrome is on (default on), the session bills a claude.ai subscription (OAuth, not routed through Bedrock or Vertex), and the Claude extension's native host is installed on this Mac; every other session, and every helper query, passes {'no-chrome': null}. Where Claude in Chrome runs, MoPilot hides its own Chrome tools so there is one controller; elsewhere "Your Chrome" and the in-app browser are provided by MoPilot's browser channel for every harness. Premise: vendor-native control matches the official product where its runtime exists, and MoPilot's own tools keep the core outcome everywhere else. The user is never asked to open the ChatGPT or Claude desktop apps; vendor plugins and extensions may be used inside MoPilot.

Decision: Codex's Sage tools go only through the thread config's mcp_servers.sage_<nonce> (carried by both thread/start and thread/resume), with default_tools_approval_mode="approve" and observation tools with readOnlyHint; dynamicTools is not used (under forced code mode images are data-URL strings, and the model cannot see them without calling image()); the namespaceTools capability flag from the previous version of the design does not exist, and the related branches are deleted. Codex's own Browser and Computer use (the bundled plugin unified-computer-use@openai-bundled) is switched on per thread on the native path (remote switch native.codex.enabled, default on, and the vendor runtime for that surface installed on this Mac: the plugin from the installed ChatGPT app, the OpenAI Chrome extension, the Codex Computer Use app), and MoPilot then hides its own equivalent tools; managed threads (switch off or runtime missing) and MoPilot's helper threads set plugins["unified-computer-use@openai-bundled"].enabled=false (verified). node_repl is turned off per thread with mcp_servers.node_repl.enabled=false, and for codex_apps a per-thread switch is to be found, both verified by WP0's X14; when it cannot be turned off, node_repl makes computer use on Codex segments marked "needs verification" with the helper's event tap as a backstop, and codex_apps goes through Codex's MCP approval and is not auto-approved when unattended.

Decision: the CLI version policy is "a minimum version plus known-bad versions": anything above the minimum version and not on the bad list works as usual and is only marked "unverified" in the compatibility table; each capability that depends on unpublished behavior gets its own runtime probe, and a failed probe turns off only that one item; when session startup fails, an incompatibility notice and an entry point for manually specifying the CLI path are shown. Premise: the Claude CLI updates almost daily, and putting a "needs verification" badge on the whole harness would make the badge meaningless.

Decision: the Settings information architecture has a budget: at release the sidebar has no more than today's 21 items and the total number of setting rows is no more than today's plus 10; accounts live only in Accounts & billing; one page per first-class harness; basic-tier harnesses fold into a single Other harnesses page; "Sage tools" is renamed Built-in tools. Premise: today there are about 32 navigable pages and about 150 setting rows, and the new design must not be more complex than today.

Open (needs a new review): if in the future a Sage-held goal loop is to be added for some basic-tier harness that has no native goal, it can only be re-reviewed as a new work package. This version removes goalLoop and goal_report, and keeps no code or interface reserved for it.
Decision: Copilot CLI and Cursor CLI ship with their remote switches off by default in the public release; turning one on changes only the switch default, not the architecture.

Decision: plugins are a capability of every harness (semantic plugins): installed once in MoPilot's store and delivered natively per harness family, with what a harness can't run (Codex app connectors elsewhere, hooks and agents on the basic tier) labelled with its reason, never dropped silently. Premise: Claude Code's plugin layout is already what Codex installs natively, and ACP's session/new mcpServers plus MoPilot's tool channel cover the basic tier's MCP and skills. Remote switches plugins.codex, plugins.claude and plugins.acp turn delivery off per family.
risks: One release with eleven work packages landing at the same time: the integration surface is large, and problems will concentrate at the end. Mitigation: each work package has its own exit checks; golden replays and the boundary test run on every PR in CI; work packages are merged in dependency order into one long-lived release branch, and trunk does not take half-finished work; Ring 0 starts around week 12, exposing integration problems more than four months before the public release.

dsh is a developer preview, user-installed, with breaking changes almost every week; a change in the patch format could invalidate the privacy patch. Mitigation: validation with --dump-config before launch, with no launch if it fails (fail-closed); versions that fail admission show "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot"; packet capture in acceptance.

opencode acp coverage is incomplete (no undo/redo, diff, share, todo, or provider login), and ACP behavior may differ between the v1 and v2 lines. Mitigation: these are not in the basic-tier contract; the admission check looks only at the core journey and tool injection.

Dependence on unpublished or changing behavior. Claude: goal state is assembled from the text prefixes of synthetic messages ('Goal set:', 'Goal cleared:', 'Stop hook feedback') and the transcript's goal_status, which breaks if the CLI changes its wording; getSettings exists at runtime but is not declared in d.ts; perTaskStopAffordance, the origin rule, and "/ commands are recognized only in the last block" are all measured behavior. Codex: forced code mode determines how tool results reach the model; pausing a goal cannot stop a turn that is running, and tokenBudget is a soft limit; the key name by which plugins turns off cua_repl, the MCP approval semantics of the thread config, and the latency of thread/search. Mitigation: each item has a runtime probe or a golden fixture; during Ring 1, conformance runs weekly against the latest stable versions; a failed probe turns off only the corresponding capability.

Parts held by Sage differ from the native implementation: resuming a Claude goal after pause means setting a new goal, with the round count starting from 0 and the CLI not knowing how many rounds ran before; when the user manually runs /goal on the same session in a terminal, Sage's paused state is overwritten by the external write. Mitigation: the GoalBar states "Round count restarts when resumed"; external writes follow the reconciliation rule, with harness state as the source of truth; Codex's init polyfill clearly says "by MoPilot".

Multi-process resources: one ACP process per basic-tier instance, plus one SDK process per Claude session and the app-server, so memory usage rises. Mitigation: start on demand and reclaim when idle (no reclaiming when there are tasks or cron).

Computer use security issues: prompt injection cannot be eliminated; the agent may try to control MoPilot itself or system security UI; project config may pre-allow tools; an upstream tool's readOnlyHint may mislead the approval layer; the user and the agent fight over the pointer. The no-go zone table, input validation by source pid, irreversible-action gating, and takeover rules must be enforced in the helper and handlers; cua-driver has no ready-made support for excluding windows from screenshots, so the helper has to capture them itself; Electron fuses and the signed sage-mcp make "verify the peer" actually hold.

Unattended autonomous work (Codex goal continuation, Claude's goal loop within one turn, sub-agents, scheduled tasks, and basic-tier autonomous work outside a prompt: dsh round-driver, Kimi /goal, Copilot autopilot) calls tools and keeps spending money while the user is away. This is contained by the unattended rules (only authorized apps may be used, otherwise the goal is paused and a notification is sent), the default budget under metered billing, and the basic-tier rule that "tool calls outside a prompt always count as unattended".

Collateral damage across Providers or billing modes: if the account-switch logic is not isolated by Provider and billing mode, a subscription chat would be moved to MoPilot, DeepSeek, or a metered API key, changing the model, cost, and data destination, and the DeepSeek endpoint does not yet support redacted_thinking, so resume may fail outright. The contract and conformance must both cover this, and cross-Provider switches in telemetry should be 0.

MoPilot gateway: newly released models are rejected with a 400 until priced at the gateway; the CLI's background models (Claude auto mode classifier, Codex's codex-auto-review) depend on prices preset at the gateway; DeepSeek peak and off-peak pricing needs to be kept in sync.

Signing and TCC: signing is done only in release builds with MOPILOT_SIGN_IDENTITY set, and TCC and auto-update can be verified only on release builds; the helper and sage-mcp need separate signing, and the helper needs separate entitlements and inside-out signing; Screen Recording needs re-confirming roughly monthly; disclaim depends on private APIs and makes the CLI pop up its own permission dialog when it accesses ~/Documents; after turning off the RunAsNode fuse, anything that depends on ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (@playwright/mcp) must be changed to go through utilityProcess. The bundle id has already reset authorizations once because of the rename and cannot be changed again.

Version drift: the Codex CLI, Claude CLI, and all basic-tier harnesses are user-installed and Sage cannot pin them; cua-driver is not embedded (WP8-3), @playwright/mcp depends on playwright's alpha versions, and @agentclientprotocol/sdk releases a version every week. Dependencies distributed with the app are pinned to exact versions and the regression suite is run on every upgrade; user-installed ones are covered by "minimum version plus known-bad versions" and runtime probes.

Data migration: moving claudeArchived, pinned, and worktreeOf into threads/<id>.v2.json touches user data; the old readSegments reads any json with a segments array, and would route an acp segment the wrong way. Mitigation: before any window opens, idempotent, atomic writes, with a completion marker; v2 uses a file name the old version does not read, and acp segments are never mirrored back to the old files; back up first; after rolling back to the old version the old data is visible but new changes after migration are not; if re-encrypting the built-in browser cookies fails, prompt the user to log in again.

UI clutter: badges, greyed-out items, status bars, polyfill notes, and new Settings entries all add elements and drift from the ChatGPT style. This is controlled by "harness-layer differences are hidden in context menus", the Composer keeping only two slots, source badges appearing only in menus and hovers, Applies to appearing only when it is not all harnesses, and the Settings page and row budget.

The semantic layer abstracts too much: unified names may cover native features, and users familiar with Claude Code and Codex cannot find the original names. Keep native names, native commands (including aliases), and source labels, and use the original names in toggle wording.

High regression cost: 27 journeys (22 existing plus 5 new) times 2 first-class harnesses, multiple Providers and models, plus contract scenarios for 8 basic-tier harnesses, all also tested on the real Electron release build, and real-CLI scenarios consume quota. Golden replays cover day-to-day development and run in CI, and real CLIs run only before release rings and weekly during Ring 1.

Concurrency in the same workspace: automatic goal continuation on an old segment, two chats changing code in the same cwd at once, and external clients (the official Codex desktop, claude --resume in a terminal) writing the same session at the same time can overwrite one another. Pause the old goal on switch; show a notice when an agent is already running in the same cwd; grey out the Composer when an external turn is running.

Basic-tier admission failures: whether Cursor (MCP may recognize only .cursor/mcp.json) and Copilot honor session/new mcpServers is unverified; if not, they are not admitted and users see "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot". Also: users expect opencode and dsh to have a first-class experience, so the release notes must state the scope of the basic tier clearly.

Native tools in Codex threads other than cua_repl: the user's own node_repl (connected to Sky CUA and browser-use) and codex_apps (302 connector tools, including side-effecting ones like doordash_checkout) appear in every thread by default. If X14 proves they cannot be turned off, Codex segments would have two sources of computer control at once. Mitigation: computer use on Codex segments is marked "needs verification"; the helper's event tap drops all synthetic events landing on MoPilot windows; codex_apps calls go through Codex's MCP approval and are not auto-approved when unattended.

Codex's auth.command executes immediately at every thread/start: a slow key helper makes every Codex thread start slowly, and if it triggers a keychain authorization dialog, thread startup would hang. Mitigation: the helper reads a cached item that main has pre-placed in the keychain (access control allowing only the signed helper), returns within 200ms, and exits non-zero immediately on failure; conformance tests the startup time.

relation.lede: Sage is not a harness and should not grow into one. A harness is the agent loop itself: calling the model, assembling context, executing tools, deciding whether a turn is over, whether to keep chasing a goal, compacting, and saving sessions, with session state following what it reports. Sage is the host, standing outside the loop, a relationship like VS Code and a language server, or Zed and the ACP agents it mounts. In one sentence: the harness decides what to do in this turn and whether to take another turn; Sage decides which tools to give it, makes it stop when the user asks, and shows you the results.

roles.does: Renders chats, takes input, and shows approval cards, the GoalBar, and the Plan chip.
roles.rel: Draws whatever the harness reports, and only the controls it declared; controls held by Sage (pause and limit of a Claude goal) are marked "by MoPilot".

roles.does: Files, terminal, search, projects, worktrees, scheduled tasks, notifications, dictation.
roles.rel: Independent of sessions and does not pass through any harness.
Sage acts like an MCP tool server; when to call it is decided by the harness's loop; authorization is enforced inside Sage's handlers.

roles.does: The init and shell polyfills, for first-class harnesses only; pausing and resuming a Claude goal.
roles.rel: Drives the harness from outside like a user: sending messages, interrupting, re-sending commands, without reaching into the loop.

bounds: Sage does not call a model directly to do the agent's work. The only exception is vision fallback, which is a tool that internally calls an image-reading model, like an ordinary MCP tool.

Do not rewrite the harness's context and do not fake the harness's state. So when a basic-tier harness has no compact it is not offered, and no new session is made to pose as compaction; pausing a Claude goal really clears the goal, the GoalBar states that MoPilot remembers the condition, and resuming sets a new one.

State held by Sage itself must be labeled with its ownership: the pause condition and round limit of a Claude goal, and the transcript Sage stores itself for harnesses like dsh that have no history replay, are marked in the UI with "by MoPilot" or "History is kept by MoPilot".
A polyfill engine may use only the actions in the adapter contract: send, interrupt, setMode, setConfig, and tool injection.

A polyfill must satisfy three criteria: state ownership stated, the difference explained in one sentence, and any extra spend initiated by the user and with a visible budget; and it serves only first-class harnesses. If these are not met, there is no polyfill, and the capability is hidden or redirected to a first-class harness that can do it.

basicTierContract.scope: Applies to all basic-tier harnesses: dsh, opencode, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, and Goose, integrated through the generic ACP adapter (ACP v1 only) plus their own quirks files. Basic-tier harnesses are user-installed; Sage does not distribute them, pin their versions, or inject Provider and key.
admission: Static: quirks must declare privacyDefaults (the default uploads and telemetry to turn off) and admission; if missing, it does not enter the picker.

Runtime: the bin is detected using the login shell's PATH; initialize succeeds; after session/new with sage-mcp (server name sage_<nonce>), a handshake is received within 10 seconds; the privacy check declared in quirks passes (for dsh, --dump-config confirms session-log-deepseek is off).

Conformance: image return in tool results, with the model able to read out a random word in the image (using a vision-capable model); when modality is unknown, the element table and locate and describe are usable.

If any fails: it does not enter the picker and a new chat cannot be created; Settings → Other harnesses shows "Installed · Can't run in MoPilot" and the specific reason (for example "MoPilot can't give it computer and browser control"). A state of "in the picker but computer use is unusable" is not allowed.
guaranteed: Detection and admission: see admission; once passed, it appears in the picker with a Basic badge, and the hover explains the differences and links to the list of differences.
Login: shows ACP authMethods; logins that need a terminal are completed in Settings' embedded terminal (the platform pty) and re-detected automatically after exit.

Create a chat (local directory or a worktree created by Sage), send text and images (when promptCapabilities.image is true), and display streamed messages, thinking, tool calls, and the diffs inside tool_call.

Approvals: session/request_permission is rendered verbatim from the options the harness gives as a generic approval card (label taken from the originating segment); tools of sage_<nonce> are automatically allow-once, and the same action is asked about only once.
Cancel: Stop and Esc = session/cancel; if a tool call still arrives afterwards while no prompt is in flight, send cancel once more and treat it as unattended.

Resume: after restarting the app, reopening a chat shows the full history (session/load when loadSession exists, otherwise replay Sage's own stored transcript and then session/resume), and sending can continue.

Computer use: the same tools, authorization card, no-go zone table, unattended rules, takeover rules, global desktop lock, and Esc emergency stop as the first-class tier; injected via session/new mcpServers. When model modality is unknown, give both a screenshot and the element table and inject locate and describe; with no vision backend, work from AX plus a local OCR element table.
Browser control: the same browser_* tools for the in-app browser (sage_browser_* while Your Chrome is the active channel) and site permissions, injected through the same channel.
Sage-side metadata: title (first message truncated), rename, archive, pin, unread, project membership, ⌘K search (title plus transcript index), export, copy session ID.
Platform services work as usual: terminal panel, @ files, Files panel, instruction file editing (instructionsFiles come from quirks), notifications.
Privacy: the default uploads declared in quirks are turned off in the launch arguments and verified before launch, and launch is refused if verification fails.

Unattended: tool calls arriving when there is no in-flight user prompt, and those more than 10 minutes after the last physical input, are always unattended; when a new authorization is needed or an irreversible category is hit, reject the call, session/cancel, and send one notification.

MoPilot's plugins: their MCP servers in session/new (stdio unless quirks mcpStdio is false; http and sse when initialize advertises them), and their skills and commands in the / menu and through plugin_skills and plugin_skill_read. Hooks, agents and app connectors are not run, and say so.
optionalIfDeclared: Native command pass-through: when the harness pushes available_commands_update, commands enter the / menu (with a source label), typed text is passed through verbatim, and typing a command not in the catalog shows a line of explanation plus "Send as plain text"; for a harness that has never pushed one, any typed /xxx is passed through verbatim, without interception or prompts.

goal pass-through: if the command catalog has /goal (Kimi, Qwen) it is passed through, with output rendered in the command output style and no GoalBar drawn. Copilot's autopilot is passed through as a mode.

plan: the Plan chip appears only if modes or a category-mode configOption contains plan and quirks marks which one it is, with toggling via session/set_mode or set_config_option; Cursor's cursor/create_plan is rendered as a plan card only if quirks writes a mapping.

modes and permissions: the harness's modes are listed under their original names; quirks may optionally mark each mode with an anchor (readOnly, ask, auto, full), and unmarked ones are treated as ask (affecting only the computer use authorization table); a menu with no modes shows only "Set by {label}".
configOptions: model, thought_level, and other categories are rendered verbatim as generic controls, saved per chat, and take effect on the next turn per ACP.
review, init, compact, skills, /swarm, /fleet, etc.: passed through as long as they are in the command catalog.
fork: if sessionCapabilities.fork exists, provide Fork chat from here.
Usage: usage_update drives the context ring.
resumeCommand: Copy resume command is shown only after quirks provides it and conformance verifies it.

Injection form: stdio sage-mcp by default; when a harness supports only HTTP MCP, quirks declares it, and sage-mcp serves an HTTP endpoint on the local loopback address with the same token and parent-process verification. Injection itself is an admission condition, not optional.
notProvided: Sage polyfills: goal, plan, review, init, compact, '!' shell, per-turn deeper reasoning, speed tier. There is no goalLoop, planGuard, or goal_report.
GoalBar and the task panel (sub-agents are rendered only as generic Agent or tool cards and can only be stopped as a whole).
Temporary chats (⇧⌘N routes to Claude Code or Codex).
Segment handoff with first-class harnesses: switching offers only "new chat with summary".
Sage-managed Provider, key injection, MoPilot credits, multiple accounts, account switching, per-chat account selection, quota bars.
Per-harness Extensions, MCP, and Skills settings pages (only the Overview in the Other harnesses page); plugins come from the shared Plugins page.
Sage distributing or pinning harness versions (Settings shows each harness's version and runs its own install channel's update, #1285); the harness's own TUI sessions appearing in the sidebar.

claudeGoal.summary: Claude Code's /goal is a session-level Stop hook: after '/goal <condition>' is set, the CLI works repeatedly within the same turn, each time the turn wants to end it checks the condition with a small model, and if not met it continues with a synthetic user message "Stop hook feedback", and when met the turn ends. It has no pause, resume, or budget (usage is only '[<condition> | clear]'), the goal is still active after interrupt(), a '/goal clear' queued during the loop executes only after the loop ends, and the local CLI does not emit active_goal. Sage therefore: builds state from synthetic messages and the transcript; holds the pause and the round limit itself, satisfying the three polyfill criteria.
snapshotSources: 'Goal set: <condition>' synthetic assistant message (model '<synthetic>'): status=active, objective=<condition>, rounds=0, and the condition is also written into the chat metadata (needed after an account switch or crash).
'Stop hook feedback:\n[<condition>]: <reason>' synthetic user message (isSynthetic:true): rounds+1, lastReason=<reason>; folded in the chat into one line "Goal check #n: <reason>".
The transcript jsonl's goal_status record (met, condition, reason, sentinel): when met=true, status=complete; Sage already watches this file (#17).
'Goal cleared: <condition>' and 'No goal set': status is cleared; if it is a clear Sage issued for a pause, status=paused, pauseBy=sage.
'Goal active: <condition> (not yet evaluated)' (when the user manually sends '/goal' to look): used for reconciliation and does not change rounds.
active_goal is not used (it is emitted only under CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE), and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is not set (the side effects are too big).

controls.pause: Stop or Pause: first interrupt(), and if the goal is still active send '/goal clear' (a local command that costs no tokens and executes immediately only after the interrupt takes effect), and store the condition in meta.goalHeld = {condition, heldAt, roundsBefore}. GoalBar: "Goal paused (kept by MoPilot) · Round count restarts when resumed [Resume] [Clear]".
controls.resume: Resume: re-send '/goal <condition>' (as the last content block, with origin human since the user clicked it), clear meta.goalHeld, and count rounds from 0.
controls.clear: Clear: when the goal is active, interrupt() first then '/goal clear'; when already paused, only delete meta.goalHeld and send no message.
controls.budget: The round limit is counted by Sage (budgetBy=sage): metered-billing accounts default to 30 rounds and subscription accounts default to none; at the limit, interrupt() first then '/goal clear', the condition goes into meta.goalHeld, a note "Reached the limit (30 rounds). Goal paused · Limit set by MoPilot [10 more rounds] [Clear]" is inserted into the chat, and one notification is sent. Only queuing '/goal clear' does not stop a running loop (measured on 2.1.295), so interrupt must come first.

criteria: State ownership stated: the paused condition is stored in Sage's chat metadata and the GoalBar is marked "kept by MoPilot"; while the goal is running, state still comes only from the CLI's synthetic messages.
Difference explained in one sentence: "Round count restarts when resumed" — resuming amounts to setting the same goal again, and the CLI does not know how many rounds ran before.

Extra spend is initiated by the user and has a visible budget: it starts again only when the user clicks Resume or [10 more rounds]; under metered billing the default is 30 rounds, and the GoalBar shows the limit and where it came from.
carryOver: Account switch within the same Provider (restartResume): after closing the process and resuming, the adapter first uses setPermissionMode to restore plan mode, and when the goal is active re-sends '/goal <condition>' (the condition taken from metadata, with this turn handled as unattended and without origin human), and inserts the note "Max limit reached. Continued on b@x.com · Goal and plan mode carried over". WP0's conformance checks whether the Stop hook is still there after resume; if it is, do '/goal clear' first and then re-send, to avoid two layers of goals.

Provider switch within the same harness (starting a new segment): "Continue this goal" in the SwitchSheet is checked by default; when checked, after the new segment starts, re-send '/goal <condition>', and the old segment does interrupt then clear.

Cross-harness switch (Claude → Codex): the old Claude segment does interrupt then clear, with the condition going into meta.goalHeld; the SwitchSheet does not carry it over by default, and when checked, runs thread/goal/set with the same condition on Codex.
Quitting the app: the quit gate does interrupt then clear on active goals, with the condition going into meta.goalHeld; after restart the GoalBar shows paused and does not resume automatically.

Reopening after a crash or forced quit: if the metadata has an active goal and no goalHeld, Sage sends '/goal clear' (a local command) before sending the next user message, turning the condition into a Sage-held pause, to prevent the next unrelated message from continuing the old goal.
Temporary chats cannot set a goal (pinned account, no account switching).
claudeGoal.unattended: Follow-up check rounds driven by the Stop hook, and a /goal re-sent automatically after an account switch, are not just initiated by the user and are handled as unattended: computer use may use only authorized apps; when a new authorization is needed the handler rejects the call, Sage does interrupt then clear (the condition goes into goalHeld), and sends one notification.
edgeCases: The user types '/goal clear' by hand in a Claude chat: passed through verbatim; if the goal loop is running, Sage does interrupt() first and then sends it, to avoid it queuing until the loop ends.

The user runs claude --resume on the same session in a terminal and operates the goal: reconciled as an external write, with the transcript as the source of truth; when meta.goalHeld conflicts with the transcript, discard goalHeld and show "Goal changed in another app".
When hooks are disabled (disableAllHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly) or the workspace is untrusted, the CLI rejects /goal: the rejection text is shown verbatim and no GoalBar appears.

The CLI itself pausing a goal because of quota (the string has "Goal paused · usage limit reached", not measured): recognized from the synthetic message as status=usageLimited, and the GoalBar shows the reason.
claudeGoal.verify: Measured (2.1.295, C4, C11): '/goal' is recognized only in the last block; the formats of 'Goal set:' and 'Stop hook feedback'; the goal is still active after interrupt; a queued clear waits until the loop ends; there is no active_goal. To be measured (WP0): whether the Stop hook is preserved after restartResume; whether a '/goal clear' sent right after interrupt() executes immediately; whether the goal is still there after reopening following a crash.

conformance.title: Launched through the SDK the way Sage does it; init message
conformance.observed: Launch succeeded with a Max subscription login; init arrives at the start of every turn, with 28 tools, 69 slash_commands, terminal_slash_commands [doctor, color, focus, reload-plugins] and 33 skills; fast_mode_disabled_reason is sdk_opt_in_required; mcp_servers in the first init is empty (MCP starts asynchronously).
conformance.designImpact: cliVersion comes from init.claude_code_version; MCP status follows mcpServerStatus() or a later init; terminal_slash_commands is used for filtering.

conformance.title: systemPrompt preset and Sage's current behavior
conformance.observed: Without systemPrompt the SDK sends an empty string and the system prompt is only 141 tokens; with the claude_code preset it is 3,315 tokens and append takes effect.
conformance.designImpact: #7 is confirmed: always pass {type:preset, preset:claude_code, append, snapshot:true}.

conformance.title: supportedCommands and the terminal command flag
conformance.observed: supportedCommands() equals initializationResult().commands, and its only fields are name, description, argumentHint, aliases, builtin; /review is an alias of code-review; skills, tasks, status, memory, feedback, plan, permissions and resume are not in the list, and typing them returns "isn't available in this environment".
conformance.designImpact: Drop the local-jsx and terminalOriented claims; interactive-only commands = the static list plus terminal_slash_commands; the menu reads aliases; skills come from init.skills and the command list.

conformance.title: /goal pass-through, view, clear, interrupt
conformance.observed: Pass-through works; after the "Goal set:" synthetic message it loops within one turn, and an unmet check arrives as a "Stop hook feedback" synthetic message; active_goal is never emitted (only under CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE); goal_status is written only to the transcript; after interrupt() the goal is still active; a queued /goal clear waits until the loop ends; there are no pause or budget subcommands.
conformance.designImpact: GoalSnapshot is assembled from the synthetic messages and the transcript; a Sage-held pause = interrupt() then /goal clear; reaching the budget limit likewise interrupts first; add a claudeGoal section.

conformance.title: origin human and the ultracode keyword
conformance.observed: origin {kind:human} is accepted and persisted; the ultracode keyword triggers only with origin human; an unknown command is handed to the model with or without origin, with no Unknown command error.
conformance.designImpact: #6 is confirmed; keep "user-typed input carries origin human"; drop the ordering requirement of commandLayer.rules[3].

conformance.title: applyFlagSettings and ultracode
conformance.observed: applyFlagSettings({ultracode:true}) takes effect; changing only effortLevel without ultracode turns it off; availability is in getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable (not declared in the d.ts); there is no stream event announcing a change.
conformance.designImpact: Every applyFlagSettings call carries ultracode; availability is read from getSettings as a version-probe item.

conformance.title: Plan mode round trip
conformance.observed: setPermissionMode(plan) emits system/status; the plan is written to ~/.claude/plans/*.md; ExitPlanMode is loaded through ToolSearch, and canUseTool receives {plan, planFilePath}; approval carries setMode back to acceptEdits.
conformance.designImpact: Confirm the design of updatedPermissions setMode; the plan card attaches planFilePath.

conformance.title: Background tasks, stopTask, perTaskStopAffordance
conformance.observed: stopTask stops only one task; without declaring perTaskStopAffordance, interrupt() stops background subagents, and once it is declared they survive; background shells survive in both cases; close() kills everything.
conformance.designImpact: Confirm that perTaskStopAffordance:true ships in the same version as the task panel; background_tasks_changed serves as a level signal; the reaper skips sessions that have tasks.

conformance.title: In-process SDK MCP image tool
conformance.observed: The model read the random word out of the image; tools are hidden behind ToolSearch by default; the handler's extra.sessionId is null; in the default mode canUseTool fires for it.
conformance.designImpact: One SDK MCP server per session, with ownership tracked through a closure and the _meta toolUseId; tools are set to alwaysLoad; canUseTool auto-allows mcp__sage_<nonce>__*.

conformance.title: persistSession:false
conformance.observed: No jsonl is written, it is not in listSessions, and getSessionInfo is undefined.
conformance.designImpact: Confirm the binding for temporary chats; switching accounts must not close the process and then resume.

conformance.title: Block order: is the / command the last block
conformance.observed: /goal is recognized when it is the last block; when it is the first or a middle block, the whole message is handed to the model as plain text.
conformance.designImpact: Confirm the adapter rule: handoff, images, user text, and the / command always in the last block (#19).

conformance.title: /compact pass-through
conformance.observed: status compacting, compact_result, compact_boundary (trigger manual, pre/post tokens); /compact with arguments is also treated as a command.
conformance.designImpact: Render compact_boundary, compact_result and compact_error.

conformance.title: /init and /code-review run non-interactively
conformance.observed: /init generates CLAUDE.md; /code-review low runs as a background task, and the result arrives through task_notification and result; /context, /usage and /mcp are local commands.
conformance.designImpact: The review result card accepts task_notification; reviews follow the background-task rules.

conformance.title: Control methods in 0.3.295
conformance.observed: getContextUsage, mcpServerStatus, toggleMcpServer, rewindFiles (needs enableFileCheckpointing and a caller-written uuid; dryRun works), forkSession(upToMessageId) and renameSession all work; forkSession and renameSession are top-level functions.
conformance.designImpact: send() writes a uuid on every user message, and rewind and fork locate by it; chats from before the upgrade have no checkpoints.

conformance.title: Other contradictions with the design
conformance.observed: There is no active_goal in the local stream; a queued /goal clear does not interrupt the loop; uuid is not echoed back; SDK MCP tools are deferred by default; getSettings is undeclared; the CLI has --no-chrome (not actually passed today); there is no /rewind command.
conformance.designImpact: Update risks[3] and conflicts[0]; add alwaysLoad; probe getSettings by version; test --no-chrome in WP0.

conformance.title: initialize, model/list, service tiers
conformance.observed: The version is only in userAgent; ultra exists only on models such as sol, astra, terra and daybreak, and the luna series has none; each model has at most one priority (Fast) service tier; multiAgentMode is deprecated; features.goals is stable and on by default.
conformance.designImpact: Gate ultra per model; speed tiers are either-or; parse the version from userAgent.

conformance.title: Goals: set/get/pause/resume/clear, disabled, ephemeral
conformance.observed: On a new thread, set starts a turn by itself and produces no userMessage; appendTranscriptItem does not exist; set paused cannot stop a running turn; resuming a goal that is already complete reruns it; tokenBudget is a soft limit (overshot by about 90x); the model has create_goal and update_goal; when disabled it returns -32600; ephemeral returns -32600.
conformance.designImpact: Remove "send the first turn, then set" and appendTranscriptItem; Sage renders the /goal bubble; pausing needs an additional interrupt; no Resume for a complete goal; budget copy says soft limit; always subscribe to goal/updated.

conformance.title: Plan collaboration mode
conformance.observed: thread/settings/updated carries plan; sol produces a plan item, luna gives only an agentMessage; thread/settings/update can switch mode without sending a turn.
conformance.designImpact: The plan card must accept the agentMessage-only case; the chip toggle uses thread/settings/update.

conformance.title: review/start inline
conformance.observed: exitedReviewMode.review is the full text, followed by an agentMessage with the same text; detached is deprecated.
conformance.designImpact: Render from exitedReviewMode and de-duplicate; delivery is fixed to inline.

conformance.title: thread/compact/start
conformance.observed: The turn contains only a contextCompaction item; thread/compacted is no longer sent; there is no manual or automatic marker.
conformance.designImpact: Sage records the request and the turn id to tell who initiated it.

conformance.title: thread/shellCommand
conformance.observed: Files can be written even in a read-only sandbox thread (bypassing the sandbox); it produces a separate turn.
